text: Proprietary odor enhancer that increases odor life, depth, radiance and a maturation effect in compounds and essential oils. Boosts substantivity on skin, paper and cloth. Described as MSG for perfume.

Givaudan nitrile with a fresh peony-geranium character, watery-rosy and slightly citrus-metallic, very stable in harsh bases. Gives modern watery-floral volume and works as a safe rose-oxide-adjacent freshener in aquatic florals.

Warm, honeyed dried-grass note with coumarin, tobacco, chamomile-tea and slightly animalic facets; smells convincingly of a summer barn. Beautiful naturalizer for tobacco, fougere and chypre bases; coumarin content triggers IFRA considerations.

Symrise gives the odour as floral, lily of the valley, lilac, aromatic, rose and fruity. It offers a soft, creamy complex white-flower facet, supplies green and versatile nuances to floral constructions, and creates waxy, petal-like effects rather than a sharp muguet aldehyde. In a formula it accentuates sparkling red and yellow fruit elements, enhances woody notes and adds freshness to lavender and aromatic accords. The house recommends 0.3 to 10 percent.

Dark, rich, earthy-woody oil with camphoraceous, sweet-balsamic and slightly winey-musty depth that mellows and improves with age. A powerful base note and fixative in chypre, amber and modern woody accords.

Opulent golden-orange champaca flowers: heady floral between ylang and orange blossom with tea, hay, fruity-apricot and slightly spicy-leathery facets. Star material in rich white-floral and opulent floral compositions.

Moroccan centifolia absolute from the Dades valley: sweet honeyed rose on a powdery dried-petal body, with only a whisper of the green that marks the Grasse Rose de Mai. Highly tenacious and a fraction of the French price, so it is the practical centifolia for anything past trial scale.

Sharp ethereal ether-like flash opening green and fruity, drying to a nutty, earthy, faintly vegetable sweetness with a whisky nuance. The classic cheap top-note lift for citrus colognes and fruity accords; extremely volatile, so it flashes off the blotter within the hour.

Softened, esterified cresol: narcissus-like phenolic-animalic note with honeyed ylang and horse-stable nuances, far more wearable than free p-cresol. Classic trace material in narcissus, ylang and animalic florals.

Nez lists Saffiano Leather among the IFF captives of Speed Smelling 2022, where in Juliette Karagueuzoglou's composition it installs a sensuality that cinnamon essential and vanilla Bourbon CO2 extract then enhance. Trade coverage describes it as a leather of the patent-leather and velvety-suede type rather than a tarry birch-smoke leather. In use it lays a smooth, skin-close leather under a composition and gives spices and vanilla something to sit on. As a branded speciality it has no single CAS, and IFF publishes no composition or technical sheet.
Ambergris, woody, dry with a labdanum sweetness and the same soft marine-mineral salinity; a purer, more diffusive cut of the identical ambroxide molecule.
Dry, diffusive fresh-woody note of cedar chips and pine cone warmed by a soft amber glow. Extends and lifts woody-ambery accords without weight; excellent fixative alongside patchouli and cedarwood.

The Good Scents Company gives it as aldehydic, waxy, clean laundered cloth, ozone, green mandarin, citrus and metallic, and rates its odour strength high, recommending it be smelled at 1 percent or less. dsm-firmenich call it an extremely powerful and clean aldehydic note with ozonic, mandarin and floral undertones, one of the strongest aldehydics they sell, with about three days of tenacity on a smelling strip. In a formula it is the modern laundry-and-mandarin aldehyde: a trace lifts a floral or a fougere out of the bottle and puts a scrubbed, airy sheen over the top, and it is loud enough that a careless drop will flatten everything under it.

IFF's trade name for 2-methyl-2-pentenoic acid, sold as an aroma chemical rather than a base. Perfumer Supply House describes it as sour, acidic, sweaty and fruity with a jammy, ripe strawberry note, and a woody nuance. The acid function is the whole point: it supplies the sour-sweaty overripe edge that ester-only strawberry accords lack, turning a candy strawberry into fruit that has actually sat in the sun. It is used in traces beside the fruity esters and the furanone rather than as the body of the accord. Physical form varies between liquid and solid with the season.

Bulkaroma lists Krishna Musk Givco as a Givaudan musk specialty and describes it as a balsamic musk accord: balsamic, musky, soft, terpenic and woody, supplied as a brownish clear liquid. Because it is a compounded Givco base rather than a single musk molecule, it reads as a rounded soft-musk body carrying a resinous, faintly terpenic woodiness instead of one clean musk facet. In a formula it works as a drydown bed: it warms and blurs a base, gives thin woody-amber accords a natural resinous backbone, and lets a nitro-free musk blend sit lower and longer without adding laundry cleanliness.

A soft, transparent floral of rose petal and muguet with a gentle pear-like fruitiness and a clean, sweet citrus lift. It rounds and harmonises a blend rather than signing it. 3-(4-Methylcyclohex-3-en-1-yl)butan-1-ol, a dsm-firmenich floral alcohol.
Fresh, woody, resinous and slightly camphoraceous pine oil with a turpentine-like bite. A classic top note for pine, forest, cleaning and fougere accords.
Fruity, spicy-sweet herbal aroma chemical with coconut, woody, wine, cinnamon and fougere facets; banana-like nuance. A versatile blender.

Firmenich black-pepper absolute with the warmth of crushed peppercorns and dark leathery, smoky, tar-like, earthy and animalic facets that steam-distilled oil does not retain. The supplier identifies a two-step purification using propylene glycol; no carrier share is inferred.

An economical orange base that reflects the typical fragrance of freshly squeezed sweet orange. Exclusive Givaudan ingredients, including a powerful captive molecule, are built in to give it a sparkling, zesty lift the plain oils lack. In a formula it goes into any citrus or fruity accord to push the orange effect towards something more natural and more intense, and it holds that character better than a straight expressed oil would.

Odour is nearly absent. TGSC describes only a very mild minty-phenolic note with a jammy dried-fruit berry trace at 100% and rates the strength low; the supplier datasheet calls it plainly odourless. What it delivers instead is physiological cold: it stimulates the skin receptors directly, builds over roughly the first twenty minutes after application and outlasts menthol by a wide margin, with TGSC measuring 81 hours substantivity. Used where an aquatic, mint or fougere freshness should be felt cold on skin without a mint smell arriving with it.

Sulfurous passion fruit and guava with an overripe, jammy exotic body and a roasted savory, alliaceous undertone at strength. The slower-release ester of the 3-MH family: softer and rounder on the top than the acetate, used at trace to carry tropical fruit into the heart.
Warm, sweet caramel-toffee note with jammy fruit and freshly-baked-bread nuances, softer and less screechy than ethyl maltol. Adds cozy baked sweetness to gourmand, amber and fruity compositions.
Realistic roasted hazelnut with creamy butter, praline, toasted pyrazines and mild coffee-cocoa warmth. An alcohol-soluble aromatic CO2 fraction for nut and gourmand accords.

Mild, sweet vanilla with a fresh, slightly green-balsamic and floral nuance; far less prone to discoloration than vanillin. A stable vanilla note for color-critical applications and a soft rounding agent in florals.
Powerful pine, rosemary and hay-like note with green facets. A nitrile bringing herbal-coniferous freshness and good stability.

Heavy cut-leaf green with an estery fruit nuance of apple, pear, kiwi and unripe banana. Rounds foliage greens into orchard and tropical fruit accords where the acetate or butyrate would read too sharp.
The softer, greener side of pine; woody and citrus-tinged with a dry, nutmeg-like spicy quality. Adds a natural terpenic backbone to citrus reconstructions and a snapped-twig greenness to florals.

Powerful aldehydic green, grassy and pungent, with a ripe-cherry fruitiness and an alliaceous earthy edge underneath. Traces add green-fruit realism and a vegetal bite to fruit and green accords; it fades from a strip within the hour and IFRA restricts it very tightly, so work from a dilution.
Green, earthy, cocoa-and-nutty thiazole with a meaty roasted facet; trace note for cocoa, coffee and savory bases.

Fresh green salicylate with vine, clover and orchid facets, lighter and markedly more diffusive than amyl salicylate. Gives airy floral lift to fougeres and green florals where the heavier salicylates would drag the top down.
A creamy, warm sandalwood-type alcohol with a soft, natural woody-milky character used as an economical sandalwood extender. A supportive note in woody-amber bases.

Mild sweet floral-balsamic with hawthorn, lilac and faint vanilla character, softer and less aldehydic than aubepine. Blender for lilac, heliotrope and mimosa accords; an IFRA-restricted fragrance allergen.

Smoky-spicy phenol with bacon, clove and toasted-wood facets, slightly sweeter and rounder than guaiacol. Adds realistic campfire-and-smokehouse depth to leather, whisky, tobacco and incense notes in micro-doses.
Turpentine-fresh pine, sharp and resinous

10-undecenal: intensely fresh aldehydic note with metallic, waxy-rose and clean-air facets, sharper and more ozonic than the saturated C-11. The classic booster that gives vintage aldehydic sparkle and modern sea-air lift in traces.

Firmenich's Total grade of damascenone: intensely natural rose with plum, berry and apple fruitiness, honeyed warmth and a tobacco nuance. It shares the registry identity of damascenone but is a separately sold grade and must remain a separate catalog and bottle identity.
Sweet anise-basil with a green, slightly fennel-like freshness, lighter than anethole. Builds basil and tarragon effects; IFRA-restricted, so used in small controlled doses.

Rich, heavy balsam with a rosy heart and a green foliage edge; supplied as a white crystalline solid melting near 55C. A classic rose-amber base material, fixing the rose while adding balsamic weight.
Dry, clean Japanese cedarwood with a distinct peppery lift and a rooty, faintly earthy undertone. Rounder and less lemony than hinoki, and a calm base wood for Japanese-style and meditative accords.
Green-fruity waxy odor with an unripe-apple and vegetal nuance. Adds fresh fatty-green naturalness to fruity florals.

Sharp violet-leaf green, more brutal and metallic than methyl octine carbonate, with unripe banana-peel facets. Classic in old-school violet and leather bases; strongly IFRA-limited sensitizer used in tiny traces.

The benzyl benzoate cut of Galaxolide, one of the standard commercial grades ScenTree lists alongside the IPM, DEP and DPG dilutions. The musk itself is IFF's clean, powerful and versatile iso-chroman musk with exceptional persistence, a quality approaching the tone of macrocyclic musks; supplier odour tags are musk, floral, woody, clean, with berry and milky facets in the drydown. It holds a blotter past two days and carries bloom and lift into the base. The carrier is not neutral the way IPM is: benzyl benzoate is itself faintly sweet-balsamic, it is a listed fragrance allergen, and it can discolour a pale base, so this grade behaves differently from the IPM cut even though the musk is identical. Dosed straight from the bottle at roughly twice the weight of neat Galaxolide.

Powerful, creamy-powdery Givaudan musk lactone with a slightly fruity, waxy nuance reminiscent of musk ambrette but nitro-free. Highly substantive on fabric and skin, prized in modern clean-musk drydowns.
A bland, light-textured carrier oil with fairly quick skin absorption, used as a base for massage and essential-oil blends. Not an odorant.
Deep, complex oud oil with smoky, balsamic, animalic-woody, leathery and sweet-resinous facets of great tenacity. The prized natural base of amber and oud-themed perfumery.

Roasted coffee and cooked onion over a heavy sulfury base, thicker and darker than furfuryl mercaptan. The disulfide is the oxidation product the coffee thiol drifts to, so it holds a roast note through the drydown where the mercaptan has already flashed off.

Sweet, phenolic-fruity ester with ylang, tuberose and wintergreen-cherry facets; a prominent natural component of tuberose headspace. Traces reinforce the carnal-medicinal opening of tuberose and gardenia.

Synthetic Dihydro Gamma Ionone, Tadimety TT1310. Warm woody, tobacco and violet-floral character, filed under tobacco/violet using editorial taxonomy. Supplier heart note; strip duration exceeds 48 hours, not an exact duration. Strength is an editorial estimate and working dilution a convention.

Sharp sulfurous thiol ester, oniony and rubbery neat, opening into rhubarb and tropical fruit juiciness at ppm dilution. A lower-cost thiol for sulfury fruit accents where grapefruit or ribes mercaptan would take over the formula.
Fresh, green-floral odor with a geranium, rose and slightly leafy metallic nuance. Used in rose, geranium and green floral accords.

First of the alicyclic ester musks: fresh, fruity-pear musk with a clean, slightly ambrette-like sparkle and a transparent, modern feel. Gives airborne fruity lift to white-musk accords rather than deep fixation.
Sweet, fresh, balsamic-coniferous oil rich in bornyl acetate, with a soft green-woody, fruity forest character. A bright, clean top note for pine-forest and fougere accords.

Waxy pre-absolute of Arabian jasmine: heavier and greasier than the sambac absolute, with the indole pushed forward and the green tea lift held back by the wax. A standard listing at naturals-focused suppliers and the usual starting point for washing your own sambac absolute.

The Somali Maydi olibanum: alpha-thujene and sabinene make it sharper, drier and more conifer-terpenic than carterii, with a fresh pine-citrus lift and only a thin resinous body behind it. No boswellic acids and very little balsamic sweetness, so it is the frankincense to reach for when an incense accord needs brightness at the top rather than weight underneath.
Dry, woody-spicy sesquiterpene with a soft clove-pepper warmth; the backbone of black pepper and clove volatiles. Adds natural spicy-woody body and diffusion to pepper, spice and woody accords.

Powerful dry violet with pronounced woody-cedar and fruity raspberry facets; more diffusive and less sweet than alpha-ionone. Key to violet, osmanthus, boronia and freesia notes, and a classic bridge between floral and woody families.
Cocoa, coffee and roasted nut character with burnt and woody facets. BulkAroma's supplied 10 DPG grade PB-1101LC, distinct from the neat ethyl-dimethylpyrazine isomer mixture.

Sparkling, non-sulfurous blackcurrant with green, juicy berry freshness and real tenacity; a rare cassis note with fixative value. Boosts fruity accords with damascones and excels in grapefruit and rhubarb constructions.

Sweet honey-balsamic hydrocinnamate with fruity, wine-like and soft floral facets, mild and completely without sharpness. A cheap volume filler that rounds jasmine and narcissus reconstitutions and pads out sweet floral bases.

Solvent-extracted geranium leaf: an intense leafy-earthy green with a rich rosy-minty undertone behind it, much darker and heavier than the steam-distilled oil, which leads rosy instead. Carries the tenacious green and rose alcohols distillation leaves behind, so it reads as crushed geranium foliage rather than a rose top-up. Use in chypres, fougeres and rose hearts that need a dense green body the oil cannot give.

Bitter cocoa and dark chocolate character with nutty, honeyed, toasted and slightly green-aldehydic facets. Considered the key impact molecule of cocoa; excellent for realistic dark-chocolate accords in traces.

Warm, sweet-spicy and terpenic with woody, slightly medicinal facets and the characteristic drowsy nutmeg warmth. Classic in masculine fougeres, colognes, spiced ambers and eggnog-style gourmands; restricted for safrole/methyl eugenol content.

Cheerful, sweet, juicy orange peel, simple and sunny with a light aldehydic sparkle. An inexpensive workhorse for volume in citrus top notes; fleeting on its own, so it is usually supported by aldehydes and sinensal-rich fractions.

Symrise gives Green, Hyacinth, Bellpepper, Leafy. It is a powerful leafy green with a nasturtium bite and a true hyacinth floralcy behind it, sharper and more vegetal than a green cis-3 material. In a formula it is the green that makes a hyacinth read as hyacinth, it builds a convincing bell pepper accord, and at low level it supplies the bitter green edge of green tea and petitgrain. Symrise calls it versatile across every category at 0.01 to 2 percent; ScenTree places it as a heart note and lists it as not restricted under the 51st amendment.
Fatty, waxy-green odor with an orange, tallow and cilantro nuance. Trace-use for fatty-green and coriander-leaf effects.
Soft, sweet lemon peel with green and lightly floral facets, a tamed and base-stable form of citral. Chosen for lemon notes in harsh media and to smooth citral's aggression in fine fragrance.

A pale brown liquid with a deep, well-balanced woody-animalic signature, rich balsamic warmth, a subtle spicy heat and controlled musky-leather undertones that read convincingly as agarwood. This is Firmenich's general-purpose oud, deliberately not tied to one terroir: per the house's own glossary a FIRBEST is a co-extraction of natural and synthetic ingredients that does NOT contain the named material, so it carries no agarwood and is CITES-free. In a formula it is a broad oud foundation and a heavy fixative for oriental and woody accords, without the batch-to-batch swing or the price of a real oud oil.

Opulent, creamy-carnal white floral with buttery, camphoraceous-medicinal top notes, wintergreen and orange-blossom facets and a heady coconut-lactonic depth. Extremely diffusive and expensive; the heart of Fracas-style florals, effective well below 1%.
Light, waxy-floral muguet alcohol with natural petal and mild herbal facets; discreet, stable and allergen-listed-free. Good top-to-heart muguet builder in the post-Lilial toolbox.
Roasted, nutty-cocoa and coffee pyrazine with an earthy potato facet; used in trace in coffee, cocoa, nutty and roasted accords.
The most abundant vetiver alcohol, soft, woody and faintly floral-earthy with mild odor strength. Contributes body and naturalness to vetiver reconstitutions.
Pink grapefruit: juicy, sweet and sunny citrus with a soft berry blush, rounder and less bitter than the white grade.
Green, hay-like, animalic narcotic floral

Dry, diffusive woody amber with cedarwood and vetiver character. Ventos blend DB10315, not a single molecule. Fraterworks reports strength 6/10, blend impact 7/10 and more than 400 hours on a blotter; the duration is a lower bound, not an exact measurement or skin-wear estimate. Supplier Category 4 cap: 5.2%. Constituent documents disagree, so formula compliance requires review even below this product cap.

Sweet, slightly pungent fruity ester leading with banana and apple over a pineapple body, with a cherry-wine nuance behind it. Sharper and more diffusive than ethyl isovalerate; used in traces for green apple, banana and tropical accords, and like all allyl esters it needs free allyl alcohol below 0.1%.

Bedoukian's copy reads powdery, woody, wonderful orris-violet, and positions it as more floral than gamma-methyl ionone, with a diffusive orris character and less wood. TGSC files the odour type as powdery, strength medium, substantivity greater than 48 hours at full strength. In a formula it is the orris that does not need orris: it lays a dry violet-powder veil over a woody or ambery base, extends a real iris butter, and softens the edge of an aldehydic or rosy top. Being less woody than the methyl ionones, it also stays out of the way of sandalwood and cedar materials sharing the same base.

Weedy green with a metallic edge, earthy bark and leafy cortex over a phenolic, nutty leather base. Sharper and more vegetal than isobutyl quinoline; a trace-level green modifier for leaf, moss, tobacco and leather accords.

Sweet, grapey orange-blossom note with dusty, slightly musty wine-grape and neroli facets; the signature of Concord grape flavor. Essential to orange blossom, tuberose and gardenia; forms colored Schiff bases with aldehydes, which perfumers exploit deliberately.

Solvent-extracted marigold: the oil's wild apple fruitiness thickened into a jammy, almost stewed richness over bitter green marigold leaf and a chamomile-herbal undertone. Heavier and far more tenacious than tagetes oil; IFRA-restricted for phototoxicity and effective in traces for apple, osmanthus and chamomile accords.

Ambergris, powdery and sensual: musky, woody and delicately animalic with a velvety softness, smoky undertones and a leathery depth; richer and more complex than standard ambroxide, and more diffusive than Ambrofix. MANE's ambroxide, made from sclareol recovered from exhausted clary sage.
Sweet honeyed rose note with balsamic, chocolate, musky and mild animalic facets. Rounds floral and honey accords.

A pleasant sparkling hesperidic accord created from a headspace analysis of the kumquat fruit, which is why it does not smell like any classical citrus oil. The brochure describes a fresh, citrus, fruity, green creation enhanced by an aldehydic complex: the aldehydes supply the sparkle and the green keeps it close to the whole fruit and its peel rather than to a distilled zest. Givaudan positions it explicitly for use as a top and middle note, so it opens a composition and then hands over, and it gives a citrus accord a fruit identity that lemon, bergamot and orange cannot.

Faint, sweet balsamic-floral salicylate that many people barely smell, yet it gives white florals their solar, skin-like amplitude. The great fixative-diffuser of tuberose, gardenia and ylang accords, usable at very high levels, allergen-listed and IFRA-flagged.
Faint, dry woody-terpenic note found in cedarwood oils; weak on its own but adds naturalness to cedar reconstructions. Mostly a diluent/blender.

Eurofragance describes Sylven as conveying a natural fruity freshness to the top notes and at the same time a natural richness and woody volume to the drydown. It is a purified fraction of upcycled western red cedar (Thuja plicata) sawdust from British Columbia mills, obtained by repeated natural purification, and the house positions it as a modern genderless woody that brings intensity and long-lastingness. Its working value is as a binder: it harmonises the materials around it and boosts their volume, and the house calls it particularly interesting in classical fougere, woody and aromatic structures. It launched as L'Ame du Bois and was later renamed Sylven.
Nearly odorless with a faint fruity character. Used as a solvent and carrier in fragrance and flavor compositions.

The modernised de Laire plum base. Symrise describes it as supporting the roundness of the iconic plum note, preserved in the chocolate accents of the Tiramisone captive, the whole of it enhanced by a dark and spicy veil; supplier listings add candied plum warmed by Madagascar spices, long-lasting and hypnotic. It is a character base rather than a nuance: a small dose carries a whole dried-fruit heart through a chypre or an oriental, and because it fixes as well as it flavours it should be judged against the finished accord, not against the fruit alone. It is built on new captives rather than the original lactone-and-spice Prunol accord, so it is not a drop-in for that older base.

Warm spicy clove with woody-phenolic and slightly sweet balsamic facets; the pillar of carnation accords. Indispensable in carnation, rose enrichment, warm-spicy and fougere structures; IFRA-restricted allergen.
Velvety powdery musk with a fruity-damascone glow and suede softness. Wraps florals in cashmere warmth; beautiful with iris and rose.

Floral, sweet and lactonic. Robertet positions it as a foundation for interpreting white flower compositions. The lactonic facet is the whole point: it is the creamy, milky-peach softness that reads as gardenia and that no single molecule delivers on its own. Because no true gardenia absolute exists commercially, a compounded base of this kind is the only honest route to the note, and this one is sold in 25kg as a workhorse rather than a specialty drop.
Fresh camphoraceous-green with eucalyptus-like cineole, sweet spicy myrtenyl acetate and a slightly floral dryout. Adds Mediterranean scrubland freshness to colognes and aromatic fougeres.
Sweet, honeyed-floral rosy odor with a green nuance. Used to add honey and rose facets to floral accords.

Nutty burnt thiazole with hazelnut and Dutched cocoa-powder body over a musty earthy, faintly green base. The vinyl counterpart to Sulfurol and much drier than it: trace amounts deepen cocoa, roasted-nut and dairy accords without Sulfurol's milky sweetness.

Mild, soft woody-balsamic oleoresin dominated by caryophyllene: peppery-woody, slightly sweet and creamy. Inexpensive fixative and blender that extends woody-amber bases and smooths harsh synthetics without imposing character.
Soft, creamy butter and yogurt note, milder and milkier than diacetyl with a faint sour-cream nuance. Rounds dairy, cream and butter effects in gourmand compositions.

IFF specialty base delivering a smooth suede effect: soft, slightly sweet leather with fatty-waxy nubuck and faintly fruity undertones, far gentler than quinoline leathers. Ideal for modern suede accords and to round harsher leather materials.
Diffusive fruity-banana ester with green, slightly lavender-like and winey facets. Used for juicy banana-pear sparkle in modern fruity tops and to add naturalness to ylang effects.

Heliotropine creaminess over a green leafy opening, drying down to a dusty concord-grape fruitiness. The allyl member of the anthranilate set and a tenacious grape end note: it gives depth and body where methyl anthranilate would read too sharp, and like all allyl esters it needs free allyl alcohol below 0.1%.

Steam-distilled from Melaleuca quinquenervia leaves, a fresh, sweet, camphoraceous eucalyptus-like note driven by a high 1,8-cineole content, softer and less harsh than tea tree. A crisp medicinal-herbal top note for fougere, aromatic and functional freshness.

Bedoukian's own copy calls it a powerful lemon-lime topnote drying down to an exquisite black Perigord truffle, and sells it for a combination of lemon-lime, tropical, marine and watery notes. TGSC rates the odour high, asks for a dilute solution on the blotter, and measures the blotter life at under an hour. In a formula it is a spark rather than a note: a trace aerates and blooms a citrus, cool-water or floral opening and gives lift in functional bases, then leaves the drydown untouched. Push it and the sulfurous truffle-and-garlic underside shows, so it is dosed in traces from a weak solution.

A powerful, fresh aldehydic mandarin, softer and waxier than natural mandarin oil, carrying elegant floral-neroli facets and a pillowy, waxy texture without the harsh bite of a raw citrus oil. Firmenich prints it under CITRUS in the bases section of the house catalogue as code 184002 KD. In a formula it is a high-performance citrus booster: it gives a cologne or a fresh top the sparkle of an aldehydic mandarin but holds far better than the essential oil, and the supplier works it at a few percent of a cologne concentrate.

Very faint soft-rose note with balsamic and honeyed depth, closer to dry rose leaf than to fresh petal. A weak-smelling fixative that extends rose and holds PEA into the drydown without adding character of its own.

Rich, sweet vanilla-cinnamic balsam with soft smoky, benzoin-like and slightly medicinal facets. Crude Peru balsam is prohibited by IFRA; only the distilled oil/extracts are allowed at restricted levels - a warm fixative for amber and gourmand accords.

Robertet's listing describes very pure and clean white flower bouquets with jasmine, monoi and frangipani undertones, plus spicy lily and gourmand coconut-milk aspects. It is a gathering of selected fractions taken from Ylang III of the Indian Ocean region, so it carries the ylang character without the fatty, medicinal cresol edge of the graded distillations. The house states its purpose plainly: it brings power and body to modern white exotic floral bouquets, with delicate floral-water topnotes and a rich diffusive drydown. In a formula it is a bouquet-builder rather than a soliflore, giving a tiare or frangipani accord volume and a creamy tail that ylang Extra alone will not hold.

Hermitage describe olive absolute as capturing the fresh, peppery, briny aroma of olives: a humid, balmy, oily opening with a mild blue-cheese nuance that develops into the cooler, refined character of a Mediterranean breeze, its greenness being that of sumptuous unripened olives with hints of green apple and pear rather than of grass or leaf, and they report up to ten hours on the tester strip. Fraterworks describe the same material as rich fruity-green with a distinctive fatty olive character and an unctuous lactonic quality over freshly cut grass, green leaves and ripe olives, supplied as a pale green liquid and placed as a heart note. In a formula it strengthens and modernises green notes, taking the hard edge off green synthetics, and it is reported to blend surprisingly well with seaweed absolute. Note that this is an olfactory extract of the fruit and is a different material from the fixed olive oil used as a carrier.
Noble dry woody note tending toward ambergris; diffusive dusty amber with an elegant cedarwood aspect. Long-lasting amber-woody base material.
Roudnitska's celebrated De Laire base: a luscious floral and fantasy-fruit accord imparting a sweet plummy note, built on a rare methyl ionone with poplar bud, helichrysum and boronia.

Powerful watery-green muguet aldehyde with lily, chlorine-fresh and slightly aldehydic-fatty facets; famously the odorant human sperm cells respond to. Gives modern muguets their crystalline freshness, IFRA-restricted, dose carefully.

Dark, ripe fruit with an overripe edge and rum-like facets. Useful in fruit and boozy accords and alongside leather notes. Generic reference descriptions also give pear, green and a caramel-like drydown.
Soft, dry, woody-cedar ester with a smooth, slightly sweet-balsamic character. A tenacious woody fixative for cedar and fougere accords.
Dry woody amber with a soft cedar-mineral cast.

Virtually odorless natural antioxidant used at low levels to protect carrier oils and oxidation-sensitive aromatics, preferred over BHT in natural and clean-label formulations. Also conditions skin in oil-based perfumes; overdosing can impart a faint oily note.

Roasted-nutty green pyrazine with hazelnut, earthy peanut and light coffee facets over a green vegetable body. Useful in traces for gourmand-green twists, iris-earth effects and natural coffee or nut reconstructions.

Fresh minty-green ketone with a slightly musty herbaceous character, responsible for the minty facet of geranium oil. Used to naturalize geranium reconstructions and add cool lift to rose-geranium accords.

A sharper, greener relative of linalyl acetate: fresh bergamot citrus with a herbal lavender and clary-sage side, a soapy-waxy touch and a faint woody dry-down. Adds bite and lift to colognes, fougeres and lavender accords. Formate ester of linalool.
Fresh magnolia petals with rosy-lily and citrus facets, clean and slightly green. Bridges citrus tops into floral hearts with a modern watery elegance.
Warm, sweet and slightly smoky woody cedar with a rich balsamic depth from deodar heartwood. Used in woody-amber and incense-leaning accords.

Powerful sulfurous rubbery note with a roasted, cooked-meaty body and a dry quinoline-like phenolic edge; ripe-fruity only at extreme dilution. One of the highest-impact materials on the palette, in the pyrazine class of potency: use in the 0.001 to 0.1 percent range to give leather, tobacco and coffee accords their burnt-rubber spine.

Juhi absolute, the third Indian jasmine: hay-dry and herbal-green where grandiflorum is fruity and sambac is tea-like, carrying only a light indolic thread. A distinct species rather than a grade, and the one to use when a jasmine should read rustic and dry instead of opulent.

Nutty, brown cocoa and roasted chocolate with nut-skin, musty-earthy and faint green nuances. The simplest and by far the mildest of the alkylpyrazines, so it is used at percent rather than trace level to build the roasted body of cocoa, coffee and popcorn accords.

Tonka-lactonic coconut with a creamy, fatty-waxy body and a mushroom-dairy shadow, the Trichoderma coconut molecule. An unsaturated pyrone rather than a massoia-type lactone, so it gives natural fresh-coconut without massoia's caramelized bitterness or its IFRA burden.

Fresh green apple over a fruity, tropical-pineapple body, carrying the faint fermented-cheesy undertow every isovalerate has. Adds bite and realism to leaf, apple and green-fruit accords where leaf acetate on its own reads too clean and candied.

Givaudan places it in the woody family with ambery, tobacco and warm facets. It is built for woody, fougere and chypre compositions, where it imparts an interesting ambergris note. In a formula it acts as a main constituent that blends the top notes into the rest of the structure and strengthens the body of the fragrance, so it is a binder as much as an odorant. Tenacity on blotter is three days, and it is stable from base to highly alkaline pH, which is why it survives detergent, shampoo and all-purpose cleaner bases.

Perfumer's Apprentice lists it as a heavy floral character with jasmine absolute notes, a colourless to pale yellow liquid recommended at around 2% of the fragrance concentrate. The Good Scents Company files the same material as floral-jasmin with fruity, jammy, tropical, waxy, naphthyl, oily and green facets. Firmenich builds it as a balanced association of ingredients, several of them captives, so it behaves as a ready jasmine heart: place it where a jasmine absolute would sit, to give body, jamminess and roundness to white-floral accords without the cost or the batch-to-batch variation of the natural.

Warm, dry, powdery ketonic musk (cyclohexadecanone) with a discreet animalic edge, slightly harder and drier than exaltone. Component of several commercial musk mixtures such as Globanone-type qualities.
Diffusive green-apple and pear ester with an ethereal tutti-frutti lift and a faint minty-herbal tail. A low-cost topnote sparkle for fruity florals, softer and pearier than ethyl 2-methylbutyrate.
Intensely floral jasmonate, more jasminic and diffusive than methyl dihydrojasmonate, with watery magnolia and fruity nuances. Enriches jasmine hearts and adds petal-like radiance to florals.

The everyday lime: sharp, fresh, zesty-green citrus with a candied cola facet. Distilled lime is the workhorse of colognes and fresh accords. FCF grade: bergapten/furocoumarins removed for photo-safety; the scent profile is essentially the same, marginally less full in the deep facets.
Non-coloring indole note, more floral than indole and less naphthalenic; a technical solution for clear, powerful white florals.

Ferociously powerful green-leathery note: bitter, earthy, mossy and tobacco-inflected, evoking new leather gloves and galoshes; the signature of Bandit and countless chypre-leathers. Use in strong dilution and small doses - it dominates formulas instantly.

Rich creamy coconut-milk lactone oil with a caramelized, woody-bitter edge; the natural source of the massoia effect, dominated by C-10 massoia lactone. IFRA-prohibited as a severe skin sensitizer, so the effect is normally rebuilt from delta-decalactone and gamma-nonalactone instead.

Faint oily-fatty note like fresh vegetable oil, with a waxy texture and a soft woody undertone. Weak and barely volatile, it works as a texturiser and co-fixative rather than for its own smell, echoing the fatty esters of champaca and jasmine absolutes. A linoleic acid methyl ester that oxidises readily, so it is kept cool.

One of the most potent amber materials in existence: brutally diffusive dry woody-amber with rocky, incense-like and slightly camphoraceous facets. Use in traces (often below 0.1% of the concentrate) or it will flatten an entire formula; incredible fixative power.

Completely odorless, ultra-stable saturated hydrocarbon emollient (now mostly sugarcane- or olive-derived) used as a luxurious carrier for skin-perfume oils. Non-oxidizing, so it never develops rancid off-notes.
Warm, fatty-green celery and lovage character with spicy, slightly soupy phthalide depth. Trace amounts add remarkable natural warmth to citrus colognes, green accords and even ambery bases.

Creamy coconut lactone with a fruity body and a caramellic-coumarinic tail, distinctly rounder and more dairy than the hay-and-tobacco gamma isomer. Use where a tonka accord needs cream rather than dry hay, and to soften coconut and stone-fruit themes.

Staggeringly potent sulfurous grapefruit-juice note, catty and tropical in overdose, brilliantly juicy at ppm levels. Used in extreme dilution (0.1% and below) to make grapefruit and rhubarb accords smell freshly squeezed.

Dark, rich cured-tobacco-leaf absolute from Nicotiana tabacum: honeyed hay, dried fruit, leather and smoky-balsamic depth with a green cigar-wrapper facet. The heart of tabac accords and a superb naturalizer for leather, amber and boozy-gourmand bases.
Dry, woody-peppery and slightly camphoraceous with a smooth, tail-pepper elegance softer than black pepper. Lends refined spicy-woody transparency to modern masculines and incense accords.

Carries the typical olfactive notes of cedarwood, which is unsurprising given it is recovered from the residual liquid left after western red cedarwood (Thuja plicata) oil extraction for L'Ame du Bois. Eurofragance describe the profile as naturally agreeable and specifically say it does not disturb the perfumer's composition, which is the point of the material: it is dosed at extremely low levels as a malodour counteractant rather than as a note you build on. It works two ways, boosting the chemical elimination of certain malodour compounds and olfactively harmonising with others so they read as less present. Treat it in a formula as a functional woody底 that costs you almost no olfactive room.
Crystalline sesquiterpene alcohol with a mild, soft, sweet-woody and faintly rosy character; the main odor constituent of guaiacwood. A gentle woody fixative.
Intense, sharp lemon-peel note, sweet and slightly herbal-metallic, the defining odorant of lemon and lemongrass. Boosts and extends all lemon accords; a known sensitizer with a strict IFRA standard.

Perfumer's Apprentice give the odour as citrus, fruity, bergamot oil, and describe it as a Givaudan specialty blend that replaces the essential oil with improved stability and performance, bergapten-free and with no phototoxic potential. PerfumersWorld break the same Givco 104 profile down as citrus bergamot over linalool, herb, aliphatic and coniferous facets, top and heart, with a relative odour impact of 100 and a working range from a quarter of a percent up to twenty-five percent of the compound, averaging around two and a half. In a formula it is the drop-in bergamot for anything that has to survive light and time: it carries a cologne or a fougere opening the way the expressed oil does, without the bergapten problem or the batch-to-batch drift of a natural.

True tincture of beach-cast sperm whale ambergris: subtle, complex halo of salty skin, seawater, tobacco, old paper and radiant musky warmth that exalts everything in a formula. Legendary natural fixative used at 1-5% tincture strength; rare, costly and ethically/legally restricted in some countries.

Sweet anisic-herbaceous with green, earthy fenchone bitterness beneath the anethole warmth. Gives a fresh garden-herb anisic note to colognes and aromatic compositions; flagged for anethole/estragole.

Extremely powerful fresh melon aldehyde, sweet green cantaloupe and cucumber rind over a vegetal base. The mono-unsaturated melon isomer that 2,6-nonadienal cannot cover, since that one reads violet leaf; supplied dilute because neat material floors an accord.
Sweet, soft, creamy sandalwood with a floral-woody, slightly musky nuance; smoother and more transparent than the natural oil. Widely used in functional and fine fragrance sandalwood bases.

Moellhausen lists it in BoldBases #3 as the round captivating smell of a walk through vineyards. The house word round is the useful one: it is a soft, filled-out grape and vineyard effect rather than a sharp fruit note, carrying the sweetness of the fruit alongside the green and earthy side of the leaf and the ground. As a compounded base it is offered as a building block, so it supplies a whole wine impression in one line where a perfumer would otherwise have to assemble grape, green and earthy materials separately.

A sandalwood base taking its inspiration from Mysore sandalwood, built around Dreamwood, Firmenich's captive from white biotechnology, and rounded out with the house's other sandalwood molecules, several of them captive. The traditional woody creamy warmth of sandalwood is brought forward rather than reconstructed from a single note. In a formula it brings naturality and a natural effect, impressive tenacity, warmth and creaminess, and the house positions it as a cost-effective alternative to sandalwood essential oil. It holds around 400 hours on a blotter, with good substantivity damp and dry and excellent burning effectiveness. Note that this is the compounded base, not the raw Dreamwood captive.
Extremely potent green-fatty aldehyde of cucumber peel, cardboard and violet leaf with a waxy tallow undertone. Effective only in traces for realistic cucumber-green and aldehydic-waxy nuances.

Fruity-floral anisic ester with vanilla and powdery heliotrope facets, drier and more transparent than anisyl acetate. Builds hawthorn, heliotrope and mimosa accords and rounds the fruity side of lilac and lily bases.
Pungent sulfurous pineapple-melon note, oniony neat but astonishingly ripe and juicy in extreme dilution. Used at ppm levels to make pineapple, melon and tropical fruit accords smell freshly cut.
CO2-extracted agarwood with a fuller, rounder smoky-woody, resinous and animalic profile that retains more of the raw wood's sweet balsamic depth. A luxury oud material.
Very soft balsamic-carnation fixative with faint spicy-floral warmth, nearly odorless in dilution. Extends and fixes carnation and spicy-floral accords deep into the drydown; IFRA-restricted.
Green anisic-spicy basil leaf, sweet and peppery with a linalool freshness. A small dose electrifies citrus colognes and fougere tops; classic with lime and vetiver.
Sweet pungent note of orange blossom, hawthorn and mimosa with an almond-cherry, slightly plastic-chemical edge. Trace ingredient for hawthorn and mimosa effects and for lifting powdery florals.

Eurofragance describes Euphorion as invigorating, uplifting and energizing, with a compelling green scent that gives a formula its own identity even at minimal doses. Perfumer Lucas Sieuzac adds a second reading: beyond the fresh green it carries salty facets, almost like dried meat, an umami tone the house links to oil-rich seeds and cured ham, which blends with spicy, fruity, toasted hazelnut and lemony materials. In use it intensifies aromatic notes such as rosemary and sage, accentuates the greenness of tropical fruit, blackcurrant and grapefruit, sits with pepper and nutmeg, and prolongs the freshness of the top instead of flashing off with it. It is Eurofragance's first synthetic captive, so no CAS or structure is published; a trace dose is enough to be perceived.
Fresh camphoraceous-floral with earthy-woody, eucalyptus and sweet freesia-elderflower facets. Adds naturalness to lavender, freesia and tea accords and a dewy green sparkle to florals.

Givaudan's wording is a powerful geranium character, reminiscent of crushed leaves, adding substantivity and body particularly to floral fragrances and especially to rose and geranium. It is a mixture of three phenyl pyrans rather than one molecule. What it does in a formula is structural rather than decorative: it holds a rose or geranium accord open with a bruised green leaf that keeps the flower from going syrupy, and it is genuinely tenacious for a green material, several weeks on the blotter, so it also functions as body under the whole floral heart. Powerful enough that Givaudan caps it at 2 percent, and it blooms strongly in soap and alkaline bases.

Waxy herbal citrus over a soft green neroli body, rounder and much slower to open than decanal itself. The latent form of Aldehyde C-10: it develops gradually and survives alkaline soap and detergent bases where the free aldehyde fades, which makes it a modifier for rose, neroli, bergamot and tuberose accords more than a topnote.

Bright, sharp, juicy-fresh lemon peel with a zesty, slightly aldehydic sparkle. Used for instant freshness in top notes of colognes, chypres and functional perfumery; fades quickly so it is often paired with citral or Lemonile for persistence. FCF grade: bergapten/furocoumarins removed for photo-safety; the scent profile is essentially the same, marginally less full in the deep facets.

The Good Scents Company gives the odour as "sweet musk oily fruity animal floral" at medium strength, with a blotter life of 316 hours at full concentration, and carries the maker's description, "Sweet, soft and tenacious animal-musky". The material is 10-oxahexadecanolide, an oxa-macrolide musk, and it reads as a warm, round, clean-but-animal musk with an oily fruity edge, quite unlike the laundry-clean signature of the nitrile and polycyclic musks. Takasago positions it as a material that gives body and richness to floral, woody and amber accords while contributing a very clean and soft musk note. In practice it is a base-note rounder and fixative: it fills the hollow under a composition and softens rough edges over a very long drydown without ever announcing itself as the musk in the formula.
Third-distillation ylang: creamier, more balsamic-woody and less jasmine-bright than Extra grade. The workhorse ylang for heart notes and soap-adjacent florals.

IFF's captive musk, listed in captives round-ups as powdery, musky and skin-like. It reads as a clean, softly sweet musk with a lustrous rather than detergent quality, described elsewhere as velvety with ambergris undertones. In a formula it is a base-note binder: it adds softness, warmth and skin-close persistence under florals, citrus and woods, and holds a composition together instead of standing out as a note of its own.

Sulfurous and catty with a caramelised onion bite, opening into roast coffee and roast meat, with a tropical nuance on dilution. A trace material at ppm level for roasted coffee and savoury accords where the catty lift is the point.
Balsamic honey-rose note, greener and less chocolatey than the isoamyl isomer. Sweet floral fixative-type ester.

Pungent fatty-green dienal, oily and frankly aldehydic with a vegetative nuance and a faint cake-and-cinnamon edge. Trace levels once gave realism to cucumber, seaweed and marine accords, but the IFRA 2,4-dienals group standard now prohibits its use.

Extraordinary Chinese flower absolute: apricot-peach fruitiness fused with violet ionones, suede-leather, honey and black tea nuances. Signature material for osmanthus soliflores and fruity-leathery floral accords, used in small precious doses.
Soft cherry-blossom salicylate, delicately floral and slightly balsamic. Gives airy blooming petal effects.

Fresh rosy ester with a dried-leaf green lift and a geranium inflection, lighter and more natural than citronellyl formate. Gives a leafy sparkle to the top of rose and geranium accords and flashes off cleanly.
Dry iris-fruity note with fatty, slightly woody-herbal undertones. Moderately tenacious, alkali-stable orris effect.

Symrise's modernised de Laire honey base, an evolution of Miel Blanc enriched with a gourmand twist. Described as a sweet and tart golden nectar blended with the milky nougat of the Tiramisone captive, Madagascar vanilla absolute and white flowers, balancing the original's honeyed character against contemporary creamy notes. In a formula it does more than supply honey: it is reported to accentuate anisic aldehydes and the addictive creamy-coconut facet of Tonkalactone, so it also works as an enhancer under mimosa and other soft floral gourmand accords.

Soft rose over a faint sweet-balsamic body with a honeyed nuance that benzyl benzoate lacks. A near-odorless fixative that rounds rose and amber bases, and the obvious substitute when benzyl benzoate's allergen load is unwelcome.

Solvent-extracted bitter-orange flowers: warm, honeyed, indolic white floral with green, grapey methyl-anthranilate facets and a sensual animalic hum, far deeper than neroli. Cornerstone of orange-flower solifleurs, white-floral bouquets and Mediterranean ambers.
A white waxy powder/flakes with a soft petal-like character; supports all-floral accords, especially iris/orris and rose.
Green, marine-herbaceous aldehydic note with citrus and grass facets. Adds ozonic-green freshness to aquatic fougères and reinforces galbanum topnotes.

Strong dry clove with a harsh woody-phenolic edge, lacking the fruity eugenyl-acetate softness of the bud but cleaner and less crude than the leaf. The middle clove SKU: a cheap high-eugenol workhorse for amber, carnation and low-cost masculine spice bases.
Green and fruity with a wine-like, slightly chrysanthemum leafiness, softer and sweeter than cis-3-hexenol. Rounds green topnotes and adds naturalness to fruit accords.

Soft animalic ester: faintly fecal and leathery, with hay, ylang, narcissus and indolic jasmine nuances and a green edge. Far gentler at the top than p-cresol or p-cresyl acetate but long and modifying in the dry-down; traces add texture to florals, larger doses suit honeysuckle and animalic accords. p-Tolyl octanoate.

Softer, sweeter and more buttery-hay than coumarin, with a creamy melilot and slightly coconut-like tonality. Useful to modulate coumarin in fougere and tobacco accords; subject to IFRA restriction as a sensitizer.
Warm phenolic, medicinal-smoky note with leathery and mild spicy facets. Trace use for phenolic-leather and smoky effects.
Fruity apricot-peel lift over an earthy, powdery carrot-seed background. A fractionated heart for orris effects, fruit-root contrasts and refined earthy florals.

Givaudan describes Gardocyclene as a fruity floral and slightly green material, less anise-like than the other cyclenes. It is the isobutyrate of the verdyl family, 3a,4,5,6,7,7a-hexahydro-4,7-methano-1H-inden-5(6)-yl 2-methylpropanoate, so it carries the same transparent lift as verdyl acetate and verdyl propionate while dropping most of the anisic edge those two show. In a formula it is a rounding heart material: it holds a fruity-floral accord together, gives shampoo and liquid detergent bases several days of clean fruity-green, and can sit under a green top without the licorice bite that makes the other cyclenes hard to place.

Methyl atrarate, the crystalline heart of oakmoss odor: dry, mossy-phenolic, slightly sweet and earthy-woody with remarkable fixative smoothness. The standard allergen-free route to mossy chypre effects, usually combined with traces of real moss or Orcinyl 3.

The crude solvent extract of oakmoss: deep, mossy and earthy, phenolic and woody, with bark, forest-floor and faint sea-shore facets over a green, leafy undertone. Darker and waxier than the absolute.
Soft fruity raspberry wrapped in jasmine warmth with anisic and balsamic transparency, reading more floral than jammy. Blends well with ionones, isoraldeines and musks to soften and enrich accords.
Waxy, oily jasmine-gardenia aldehyde with a soft, slightly herbaceous floralcy that blooms in soap. The classic cheap jasmine body of the 20th century, still invaluable in functional white florals.
Aquatic-green base evoking fresh flowing water, jungle greenery, earth and fresh air. The supplier names Cascalone among its ingredients; this is a formulated base, not a natural extract.
Sharp, acrid, sour-cheesy odor. Trace-use acid contributing sour, dairy and pungent fermented facets.

Powerful green herbaceous-vegetable note with an oily edge, reading as crushed leaf rather than the sharper cut-grass of leaf alcohol. Slow-releases cis-3-hexenol in use, so it carries a natural green top further into the drydown than the alcohol does.
Powerful pungent aldehydic odor with a cocoa, coffee and fermented-fruity nuance. Trace-use for gourmand and malty facets.

Smoky frankincense with burnt-resin, charcoal and dry woody nuances. Payan Bertrand F2468 is a processed frankincense and triethyl citrate blend, not olibanum essential oil. Useful for church-incense and smoky wood accords. Supplier reports more than 400 hours on a smelling strip, not an exact skin-life value. Strength is an editorial estimate. Supplier IFRA 51 Category 4 maximum: 8.163% in the finished product; incomplete trace quantification still requires safety review.

Robertet gives aromatic, aniseed, spicy, basilic, and calls it a beautiful aromatic note widely used in flavour applications; the status line is natural on carrier (MPG). The linalool type is the softer, less anise-dominated basil, so it lifts a fougere or a green top without the sharp tarragon bite of the methyl chavicol types. Because it is carrier-borne rather than a steam-distilled oil, it doses differently and does not flash off with the same speed as the essential oil.
Warm, oaky-coumarinic note with toasted coconut, maple, tonka and barrel-aged whisky facets. Recreates oak-cask warmth in boozy gourmands and adds creamy woody depth to tobacco and amber accords.
Fruity-floral pear and plum with green herbaceous and slightly woody-rosy undertones. Adds juicy naturalness to lilac, freesia and fruity-floral accords and survives well in soap.

A weak, faintly musky-urinous steroid pheromone metabolized from testosterone and used chiefly in pheromone-marketed blends rather than for strong odor value. Contributes a subtle animalic, skin-like warmth and is said to amplify the presence of other pheromone materials.

Crisp, dewy lily-of-the-valley with a green watery transparency and a light aldehydic sparkle, airy rather than the creamy-sweet muguet of the older aldehydes. Symrise's Lilial-era replacement, made from upcycled orange-peel limonene; anchors modern muguet and fresh-floral accords.
Waxy, nearly odorless fatty alcohol. Used as a fixative, carrier and consistency/solidifying agent in solid perfumes and cosmetics.

Crystalline aromatic freshness between linalool and linalyl acetate, capturing clary sage brightness in a white floral frame. Bridges citrus tops to floral hearts and modernises lavender-cologne structures.
Dry, clean woody cedar with a mild balsamic sweetness; a common low-cost source for cedrol isolation. Broadly used in economical woody bases.

Megastigmatrienone, the signature molecule of cured blond tobacco: radiant, warm, dry-sweet tobacco with plum, acorn, tea and balsamic facets of striking naturalness. Extremely powerful - 0.1-1% builds an entire tobacco accord; also enriches amber, oud and woody bases.
Fresh, green-herbaceous salicylate with clover, orchid and azalea facets over a sweet balsamic base. Classic in fougeres and green florals; gives a sunlit meadow effect to white flowers.

Traditional odorless fragrance solvent and extender with excellent solvency and fixative drag; still used in some functional perfumery. Consumer aversion to phthalates has largely displaced it in fine fragrance in favor of DPG, IPM and TEC.

TGSC carries Bedoukian's description: powerful sweet-ethereal, juicy, pineapple and shades of pear, mango and passion fruit. Strength is rated high, it wants a dilute solution on the blotter, and neat substantivity is under a day. In a formula it is a juice note for the opening: it makes a pineapple or passion-fruit accord read wet rather than jammy, brightens pear and mango esters, and gives a tropical top the ethereal lift a plain saturated ester cannot. It burns off fast, so it needs a longer fruity or lactonic body underneath if the effect has to survive past the first hour.
Faint pleasant fruity, mild wine-like character. Used as a solvent/diluent and subtle fruity adjunct.

The Good Scents Company files it as a green odour of high strength, to be smelled at 10 percent solution or less, and gives the description violet, green, cucumber at 10 percent in DPG; the supplier description reads green, cucumber melon, violet, rose-fatty, with an ionone-like drydown. It is a colourless to pale yellow clear liquid, a compounded blend rather than a single molecule, built mainly on Violiff with Neofolione, Mysore Acetate, Liffarome and a trace of 1-octen-3-ol, and Scentspiracy lists it as IFF's violet-leaf facsimile. In a formula it is the violet-leaf green top written to stand in for methyl octine carbonate, giving the crushed-leaf, cucumber-melon bite over florals and chypres while drying down ionone-soft rather than vanishing.

Soft, creamy woody oil built almost entirely on nerolidol and fokienol, so it reads closer to a woody-floral than to a conifer: warm, faintly green-sweet and completely free of terpene sharpness. An exceptionally tenacious fixative that rounds sandalwood, amber and floral bases without adding an edge of its own.
Low, mild slightly fresh solvent character with fruity, citrusy, green nuances. Water-soluble carrier and coupling solvent with high fragrance solubility, suited to air-freshener applications.
Finest red saffron extracted into dipropylene glycol to give a deep red infusion with a very rich, opulent bouquet. Roughly 30 stigmas from 10 crocus flowers per gram of infusion.
Mild sweet hyacinth-balsamic alcohol, softer and greener than phenethyl alcohol. Rounds hyacinth, lilac and honeyed floral hearts.

Woody-earthy ester with a patchouli-like, camphoraceous edge, clove and peppery spice and a slow, sweet amber warmth; Fraterworks likens it to patchouli, cloves, camphor and Iso E Super together. Very slow to evaporate and fixative. The formate of beta-caryophyllene alcohol.
Powerful, penetrating green galbanum note with pineapple nuances. Same profile as classical galbanum molecules but with outstanding substantivity and stability in all applications.

Savory sulfurous thiol: broth, cooked leek and roasted onion at strength, turning to blackcurrant bud, gooseberry and grapefruit zest at trace. A classic Firmenich sulfur specialty found in coffee, passion fruit and cat urine alike; dosed at ppb it lends bite and mouthwatering realism to cassis, citrus and exotic-fruit accords.

Steam-distilled lemon verbena (Lippia citriodora), a sharp lemon-green freshness rich in citral that opens almost aggressively before relaxing into a bitter herbal-tisane, faintly camphoric drydown. Prized for luminous natural lemon character in colognes and fine fragrance, though its high citral load and photosensitizing constituents call for restraint.

Sharp phenolic-tarry note of horse stable, ink and smoke that underlies narcissus, ylang and animal secretions. Indispensable in ppm traces for realistic animalic and narcissus effects; harsh and medicinal if overdosed.
Sweet fruity-rosy ester with apricot and slightly waxy nuances. Rounds rose and geranium bases with fruity softness.

Mild sesquiterpene alcohol from elemi and citronella: soft dry-woody with a clean green-floral rosy edge and a faint sweetness. Sits beside guaiol and bulnesol as a gentle woody fixative, rounding sharp terpenic woods without darkening them.

Symrise gives the odour as floral, magnolia, geranium, pomelo, peony, tea leaves and water lily. It is the isomer-enriched development of Magnolan, brighter and more transparent than the classic material, and it twists a floral accord toward magnolia or gardenia while laying in a fresh, clean, transparent floralcy. In a formula its job is radiance at the opening: it gives the top note lift and highlights tart citrus and green notes so a heavy white floral reads sparkling rather than creamy. The house recommends 0.5 to 10 percent.
Sharp, dry, smoky-woody cedar with a tarry, slightly harsh top; more rugged than Virginia. A functional woody base for soaps and detergents.
Radiant peach and apricot lactonic base with broad diffusion and persistence. A modern fruity-lactonic building block for peach accords, white florals and orris compositions.

Waxy, buttery-dairy lactone with a fatty, faintly cheesy milk body and almost no fruit, the heaviest usable delta lactone. Very quiet but extremely tenacious; lays a skin-like creamy floor under gourmand and musk bases where delta-dodecalactone still reads as peach.

Supercritical extract of cured Dipteryx odorata beans: a cleaner, sweeter and more vanillic coumarin than the absolute, with the hay, tobacco and leathery edges pulled back. Very coumarin-rich, so IFRA coumarin limits bite early; the default tonka for indie gourmand and amber bases where the absolute reads too dry.
Waxy-soapy aldehyde with fresh laundry, orange-rind and slightly rosy-fatty facets, smoother than the undecylenic isomer. Core of the classic aldehydic accord and a diffusion booster in florals.
Green woody-oxirane with a fresh, rhubarb-like and dry ambery-woody character; adds a crisp, natural green edge to woody accords. A distinctive fixative for modern woods.

Bursera graveolens wood oil with a creamy, sweet-woody incense character showing minty-limonene freshness, anisic and slightly medicinal-smoky facets. Distinctive 'holy wood' signature for incense-woody and aromatic compositions.
Crisp eucalyptus-fresh camphor leaf from Madagascar, cleaner and softer than eucalyptus globulus. Aromatic lift for sport fragrances, lavenders and green tops.

Powerful milky-creamy material with green peach-skin fruitiness, floral rose nuances and possible waxy-cheesy edges. Despite the trade name it is a decenoic acid, not a true lactone, and it is not Milk Lactone Super or the delta-dodecalactone mixture sold under similar names.

The dsm-firmenich sheet files it under earthy-mossy and describes it as woody, mossy and very long-lasting, with the typical marine seaweed facet of the traditional oakmoss extract; the Firbest moss range is offered so perfumers can rediscover the olfactory profile of old-time traditional mosses. In a formula it does the job of a moss extract, and the house states Firbest mosses are used at a one-to-one ratio against natural moss extracts, so an old formula can be transposed without refitting the moss level. It is supplied at 50 percent in isopropyl myristate, which keeps it perfectly soluble and convenient in automated workshops, and it is clearer in colour than the traditional natural extracts so it can be used in a greater number of applications. Composition is unusual and worth knowing: Firbest specialties come from a co-extraction of natural and synthetic ingredients, some of them captives, and the sheet states outright that this product contains no trace of natural oakmoss - it contains naturals, but not the named ingredient.
Sweet, earthy-green fruity aroma chemical with woody, herbaceous, unripe-apple, mushroom and lilac facets; mild and smooth blending material.

Roasty and nutty with a faintly meaty, baked-potato earthiness and a roasted-sesame trail. Sits between the dimethyl and diethylmethyl grades in effect, adding depth at trace level to roasted nut, coffee and savoury-gourmand accords.
Radiant blackcurrant, rose and tea note with a camphoraceous opening; one of the finest modifiers for rose ketone accords. Indispensable for tea, cassis and fruity-floral effects.

Dark, sticky solvent extract of Scots pine needles: jammy balsamic conifer with a honeyed-green depth and none of the thin turpentine bite of the needle oil. A tenacious forest base that fixes the volatile pine tops it is usually paired with.

Roasted, earthy-nutty pyrazine with cocoa and coffee facets over a faintly ethereal lift. Drier and less meaty than the 2,3-isomer, it is a standard trace workhorse for rounding roasted gourmand and coffee accords.
Sweet ripe apple ester with fruity-green and slightly fermented cider facets. Used in apple, tutti-frutti and whisky-fruit accords for rounded juicy sweetness.

A de Laire floral bouquet constructed around the ionones and methyl ionones: an exceptionally rich floral blending rose, jasmine and orange flower over a powdery violet-iris core, the base Jacques Guerlain used in Apres l'Ondee. Modern stock is described with a bright, almost citrusy lift on the opening, which makes it a bergamot enhancer as much as a floral heart. In a formula it is a ready-made floral middle: it rounds and powders a bouquet in a way a raw ionone on its own cannot, and it bridges a citrus top into a white-floral heart without a seam.

Fatty, waxy aldehyde with a dry amber-incense body and a citrus-peel and musk trail, much softer and less soapy than the C8 to C12 aldehydes. This is the true straight-chain aldehyde C-14, not the so-called aldehyde C-14 of perfumery, which is gamma-undecalactone.
Soft, dry, powdery woody-cedar ester with a faint fresh-green nuance; smoother than cedar oil. A mild woody fixative and cedar-note extender.

Floral muguet (lily of the valley). A proprietary Fraterworks base developed as a one-for-one olfactory replacement for Lilial, not Lilial itself or another supplier's substitute. The supplier reports 236 hours on a smelling strip, not skin longevity. Heart filing is a catalog convention, not a measured evaporation band.

Light, odorless emollient ester used as a carrier for perfume oils and body products; gives a dry, non-greasy skin feel and excellent solubility for most aromatics. Preferred over DPG when a silky skin-oil format is wanted.
Strongly fruity, sour, juicy and fatty with strawberry, pineapple and raspberry berry facets. A jammy acid modifier for red-fruit accords.

Sweet, sharp creamy vanilla with a spicy clove-like edge, more lifted and richer than the vanillin acetal. The same non-discolouring trick applied to ethyl vanillin: full creamy vanilla in soap, candles and amine bases with no pink or brown discolouration.

Powerful, sweet, hot-spicy cinnamon aldehyde, the character-impact molecule of cinnamon bark, diffusive and slightly balsamic. Gives lift and warmth to amber, gourmand and fruity-spice accords; a listed skin sensitizer used at trace levels.

Earthy potato-bin skin with musty, mouldy-nutty and faintly green-vegetal facets; one of the most potent odorants known, traceable at parts per trillion. Completes the methoxypyrazine set as the musty-earth grade rather than the bell-pepper green of the isobutyl and isopropyl isomers, and needs extreme dilution to lend soil realism to potato, iris, vetiver and roasted gourmand accords.

Fatty, waxy citrus-peel odor with a fresh cilantro-herbal nuance over a sweet mandarin lift, which is the facet it is sold for under the name Mandarin Aldehyde. Trace-use for coriander-leaf, mandarin and fresh natural effects; too powerful to weigh neat, so it reaches a bench pre-diluted at 1 or 10 percent. High-trans commercial grade.

The classical de Laire white honey base, whose archive Symrise now owns. Suppliers describe it as pure honey sweetness without floral complexity: a clean honeyed depth with none of the heavy animalic or barnyard facets that usually come with a honey note, and it stays clear rather than discolouring a formula. Blotter life is quoted at around ten days. In a formula it is the honey you reach for when you want sweetness and warmth without the dirty side, and it historically fed the great Mousse de Saxe base as well as being used directly as a honey note.

Faint sweet vanillin note: a vanilla ketone reading cleaner and fresher than vanillin itself, with less of its spicy-phenolic bite. Low odor strength for a vanilla material, so it serves as a quiet non-discoloring extender behind vanillin rather than as a vanilla in its own right; better known to pharmacology as apocynin.
The definitive banana-candy note, sweet, solventy and pear-like, instantly recognizable. Used sparingly for banana and pear-drop effects and to add a playful fruity lift.
Softened fruity-clove, sweeter and less phenolic than eugenol, with a mild balsamic-floral roundness. Smooths carnation and spice accords where straight eugenol would be too aggressive.

The signature lilac note itself: a floral lily-of-the-valley character with a green aldehydic lift and ozonic, watery transparency, sold as the natural mixture of stereoisomers found in real lilac and linden headspace. Airy and radiant rather than heavy, and nothing else in the palette replicates it. Trace levels build authentic lilac and give muguet accords a transparent, dewy top.
Creamy dairy-coconut lactone, softer and more buttery than its gamma isomer, with a light tropical nuance. Used for milky, creamy textures in fig, coconut and gourmand fruit accords.

Sweet, dry, powdery polycyclic musk with a distinctly ambery, slightly fruity retro character, harder-edged than Galaxolide; still loved for vintage laundry-musk effects. No IFRA standard covers AHTN; in EU cosmetics Annex III of the Cosmetics Regulation (entry 182) restricts it to 2.5% in fine fragrance, 1% in hydroalcoholic leave-on, 0.5% in fragrance cream, 0.1% in other leave-on and 0.2% in rinse-off products.

Tobacco revealed in an addictive, intoxicating way and made with no tobacco natural extract at all. The almond-like roundness of the Tonkalactone captive and the sensuality of Bourbon vanilla absolute meet a tangy cinnamon and the dried-leaf smell of the Tabanone captive, the whole shrouded in a dash of liquor. It is a finished tobacco bed rather than a single note: drop it into the base of an oriental or a gourmand and it supplies the leaf, the sweetness and the boozy warmth in one move, where an unbranded tobacco compound would need vanilla and tonka stacked on top of it.

The supplier describes it as a modern agrestic and herbaceous animalic, a civet-type blend with nuances of woody balsamic and costus facets. It is a slightly viscous, cloudy amber-yellow liquid supplied in triethyl citrate and holds a strip for more than two weeks. In a formula it is the dirty underlayer of a fougere or chypre, giving skin and fur warmth under herbs and woods; being the allergen-compliant reformulation carried in solvent, it is both a different composition and a different working strength from the neat Animalis base and must be weighed accordingly.
Heavy, sweet vanilla-cream with an unusual nutmeg-spicy and slightly fruity warmth. Extends vanilla character with better stability and adds a custardy, spiced-cream twist to gourmand bases.

Elegant, warm, powdery-clean macrocyclic musk with discreet animalic and slightly waxy undertones, very close to the lactonic side of natural deer musk. A classic fixative that gives lift and skin-like diffusion to florals, chypres and ambers.

Fresh muguet-lilac floral with watery cyclamen and slightly green-aldehydic facets; long the backbone of lily-of-the-valley and lilac accords. Now banned in EU cosmetics and heavily IFRA-restricted, retained here for legacy formula reference.

Extraordinary animalic-vegetal note of unwashed hair, wet dog, old wood and orris-like fattiness; nothing else smells remotely like it. PROHIBITED by IFRA as a sensitizer (untreated qualities); modern work relies on traces of treated grades or costus-type reconstitutions.

A Givaudan captive fragrance precursor launched 19 February 2026. Givaudan's release describes it as releasing fruity raspberry and soft powdery vanilla notes, bringing brightness and softness. The molecule is near-silent on its own and oxygen-activated: the fragrant molecules are diffused gradually when triggered by natural factors like the oxygen or humidity of the air, extending the scent notes over days. It is biodegradable per OECD guidelines, developed on the FiveCarbon Path with a Safe-by-Design approach, and aimed at shampoos, fabric conditioners and laundry detergents, in particular the synthetics of the athleisure market. In a formula it is a longevity tool rather than a top note: weigh it for what appears on day two, not for what the blotter does in the first hour.
Soft, powerful white musk with richness and depth. Supplier reports more than 400 hours on a smelling strip; this is a lower bound, not exact lifetime or skin longevity.
Fresh linalool-rich mint oil with bergamot-lavender character and only slight mintiness. Bridges citrus tops and aromatic hearts.
Soft fruity ester with unripe pear, apple peel and slightly green-waxy facets. A gentle blender that adds naturalness to pome-fruit accords.

Sweet ripe raspberry and broader tutti-frutti, grape and banana facets with rose-like and iris florality and soft amber warmth. Supplier classifies it as a base note; differing blotter lower bounds on the page are not converted to exact longevity.
Airy rose-petal and dewy peony character with transparent muguet, fresh clean diffusion and fruity lychee sweetness.

IFF specialty sharing Applelide's CAS but with a different isomer balance: powdery, creamy, relaxed white musk with soft fruity freshness and a comforting textile-like drydown. An uncommon, smooth alternative for clean skin-musk bases.

IFF's ambrette reconstitution base, listed by the supplier in the musk family with an odour of dry, ambrette, musky, sweet and light floral. It is a colorless to amber viscous liquid that reads as the powdery-sweet musk of ambrette seed, warm and faintly floral, without the animalic sharpness of the old nitro musks it was named to replace. In a formula it works as a soft musk foundation and fixative: it holds on the blotter for well over a week, rounds the edges off harsher musks, and lends a warm skin quality under white florals, fougeres and modern chypres.

IFF's branded coumarin and tonka base, classified by the supplier as balsamic with an odour of sweet, balsam, coumarin, fruity, tobacco, hay, woody, nutty and tonka. A colorless to pale yellow liquid, it gives the new-mown-hay and tonka-bean sweetness of coumarin in a rounder, more three-dimensional form than the crystalline material, with tobacco and nutty facets filling in underneath. In a formula it is the fougere and oriental workhorse: it sweetens and warms a base, blurs the join between woods and vanilla, and holds around 200 hours on a blotter.

Sweet fruity cinnamyl ester with almond, soft spice and a tropical apple-banana nuance, rounder and far less harsh than cinnamic alcohol. Used in hyacinth, jasmine and fruity-floral bases to soften the cinnamyl note and add body.

Fine rose alcohol fraction (traditionally ex-geranium, citronellol/geraniol-related): soft, deep and remarkably natural sweet rose with a delicate green freshness. The connoisseur's choice for elegant, vintage-style rose hearts.
A colorless, refined grade of vetiveryl acetate with the cleanest woody-sweet character and least earthy-smoky residue. Used in fine fragrance where clarity is essential.

Sweet jammy-fruity ester with rosy floral and green facets, reading like fruit preserve over petal rather than the cleaner rose of geranyl propionate. The cis counterpart rounds rose and neroli accords that the geranyl series leaves too sharp.

Sweet freshly picked cherries with complex fresh-fruit character. The supplier distinguishes this base from almond-heavy glace cherry. Reported blotter life exceeds 4 hours; no exact duration or skin longevity is established.

Sweet, intensely fruity ester with a soft rosy-geranium body and a tropical nuance; rounder and less sharp than the acetate or formate. Rounds out the citronellyl series in rose and geranium accords that need fruity body rather than lift.

Deep, sweet honey character with animalic, civet-like and slightly sour-floral facets; honeycomb realism in a bottle. The backbone of honey accords, also lending rosy-honey warmth to florals; easily overdosed into barnyard territory.
Warm maple syrup, caramel and roasted licorice character with a slightly smoky, coffee-like depth. Essential for maple, praline and burnt-sugar effects in gourmand and tobacco accords.

A mammalian pheromone, 5alpha-androst-16-en-3-one, whose perception is genetically split: some smell a strong stale-urine sweatiness, others a woody or faintly sandalwood-sweet note, and a large fraction are anosmic to it entirely. Used in trace amounts in animalic and pheromone-marketed accords, where its urinous facet reads as raw skin warmth.

Citrus, orange, minty and woody: the laevo enantiomer reads pine-needle and turpentine rather than the sweet orange peel of its dextro twin, with a herbal, faintly peppery terpene edge. It occurs in pine needle and fir cone oils, turpentine, star anise, peppermint and spearmint. Takasago sells it to give lift and freshness to citrus fragrances, where it carries bergamot, orange, lemon, mandarin and grapefruit; TGSC rates the odour medium with 4 hours substantivity at 100%. Stable in most bases but not in alkaline bleach, and like all limonene it oxidises, so it is bought fresh and stored cold.
Sweet balsamic vanilla-cinnamon resin, rougher and spicier than Siam benzoin. Classic amber and balsamic fixative that sweetens without cloying.

Robertet's own descriptors are tobacco, herbaceous, powerful, and the product's status line reads naturals on carrier (MPG), meaning the natural extract has been put onto a propylene glycol carrier. It reads as cured dried leaf with the green bitterness of yerba mate underneath rather than as smoke. Used to build tobacco, fougere and chypre accords where a neat mate absolute would be too dark, too viscous and too concentrated to dose finely.

Symrise's datasheet gives the odour axes as amber, wood, warm amber and animalic, and calls it a very powerful and long-lasting base note that creates a unique warm and gentle woody-ambery profile. It is a clear, colorless to pale yellow acetal that smells like a dry, radiant super-amber with an animalic undertow, and the house note that it intensifies the typical characteristics of oud notes. In a formula it is a trace material: the successor to Ambrocenide and far stronger, a fraction of a percent pushes amber-woody diffusion and blotter life past almost anything else on the shelf, so it goes in last and sparingly or it flattens everything around it.

Intensely sweet cotton-candy and caramelized-sugar note with a fruity-strawberry jam facet, several times stronger than maltol. The defining material of modern gourmand perfumery since Angel; overdoses easily.

Extremely tenacious woody-amber with musky undertones; among the longest-lasting materials known. Pairs superbly with the Limbanols, Okoumal and Tobacarol for body and fixation in amber-wood structures.

Geranium-rosy ester with a fruity sweetness and a distinctly herbaceous green edge, faintly melonic in dilution. Used in rose, geranium and osmanthus work where geranyl acetate needs a herbal lift rather than more sweetness.
