Dark chocolate, soft smoke and warm leather with a grape-wine quality and a whisper of vanilla; mild but extraordinarily lasting. Vanillin stripped of obvious sweetness and given smoky depth.
Fruity grape/cognac, oily brandy-like note with a waxy facet. Adds fruity-vinous body and diffusion.
Green coconut-milk and bitter leaf sap, the true smell of a fig tree in the sun. The natural anchor of every fig fragrance; pairs beautifully with sandalwood and lactones.

Explosive galbanum-pineapple green with hyacinth and blackcurrant-bud facets, enormously diffusive. Used in small doses to give lift and a natural galbanum sparkle to fresh fougères and green florals (famous in Cool Water type accords).

Powerful long-chain aldehyde combining clean aldehydic-waxy character with marine-ozonic freshness and a floral muguet-lily nuance. Modern diffusion booster for transparent florals, aquatics and clean-musk themes.

Powerful caramelized strawberry-pineapple note, sweet cotton-candy and burnt-sugar, jammy and mouthwatering. A trace gives ripe cooked-fruit sweetness to berry and tropical gourmands; overdose smells like a candy factory.
Fresh, sweet fruity odor reminiscent of banana and pear with a solventy lift. Common building block for tropical and jammy fruit accords.

Smooth, warm woody-ambery dioxolane with full-bodied tobacco and musky nuances; rounder and more velvety than the screechy woody-ambers. Combines beautifully with cedar, patchouli and sandalwood materials to build plush amber-woody hearts.
Sweet, powdery-ambery nitro musk with a soft animalic warmth, once used in opulent bases. PROHIBITED by IFRA; historical reference only.
Powerful fatty-aldehydic note with a strong orange-peel character, waxy and sharp when neat but juicy and sparkling in dilution. Used in traces to give citrus tops natural zest and diffusion.

A Mane branded base described as a highly diffusive floral grapefruit with orange blossom, positioned as a contemporary alternative to methyl pamplemousse. The supplier files it under floral first with citrus second, and rates its odour strength at six out of ten with an impact of five, so it is a shaping material rather than a bruiser. It contains the Mane captive Bigarane, which is where the green lift under the peel comes from. In a formula it does the job methyl pamplemousse used to do, giving grapefruit diffusion and zest that survives into the heart, but with an orange blossom floralcy that keeps it from reading thin or sulphurous. Lasts more than 24 hours on a smelling strip.

Firmenich's robust Iralia Total grade: rich powdery violet and orris over a more pronounced warm woody backbone, creamy floral depth and a faint raspberry facet. It is less delicate and more woody than classic Iralia and remains a separate bottle identity.

The waxy pre-absolute stage of bitter-orange blossom extraction: the same honeyed indolic orange flower as the absolute, but heavier, greener and slowed down by the floral waxes that alcohol washing would strip out. Used where the wax is the point, in solid perfumes, balms and pomades, and as a long fixative orange-blossom heart that will not flash off.
A soft aqueous floral from the blue butterfly pea flower (Clitoria ternatea): fresh, clean and lightly ozonic with a delicate soapy-floral character.

Bright, peppery-lemony resin note with green, dill-like and distinctly 'fresh paint' elemicin facets from Canarium luzonicum. Superb sparkling incense top note that links citrus openings to olibanum and woody hearts.

Methyl ester of hydrogenated rosin: pale, nearly odorless viscous fixative with a faint balsamic-piney whisper. Classic cost-effective fixative-plasticizer that reduces volatility of top notes and improves tenacity in soaps and functional perfumery.
Fresh, lemony-spicy and warm with a zesty, slightly woody pungency true to fresh-cut ginger root. Energizes citrus tops and adds fizzy warmth to modern woody-ambers and gourmand ginger-ale accords.
Waxy, fatty, cheesy odor with a slight coconut nuance. Trace-use acid for waxy-fatty and cheesy nuances.
Animalic, woody amber-musk with a strange, polarising character when smelled pure. In a blend it naturalises and adds a musky elegance, especially in sandalwood, tobacco and incense accords.

Robertet describes it as a concentration of the most rosey, fresh, spicy and marine notes of elemi. It is a fractionation and reblend of selected elemi essential oil fractions, from the frankincense family, keeping the crisp incense character with its citrus and peppery facets and leaving behind the harsher petrol-like side that whole elemi oil shows. The material is stabilised with natural tocopherols. In a formula it is elemi with the flaw removed: use it to give an incense or amber accord a lit, peppery brightness at the heart, or to lift a resin base without the solvent edge that makes whole elemi hard to place in a clean composition.
Intense fresh green ester with unripe fruit and cut-grass character. Natural green-fruity lift for apple, pear and foliage accords.

Green, faintly spicy hyacinth alcohol with balsam, lilac and honeysuckle facets; more floral but less rosy than phenethyl alcohol, and much softer and rounder than hydratropic aldehyde. The reduced alcohol of the pair: use it where the aldehyde's sharp green bite is too aggressive, in hyacinth, lilac, gardenia and spring floral hearts.

Fresh fir-needle and pine note, green and natural, with a light citrus-fruity lift, a soft cistus-labdanum warmth beneath and a faint woody undertone. Givaudan suggests up to about 2% to freshen herbal and pine tops. Fir carboxylate, a methyl bicycloheptane carboxylate.

The N-methylated anthranilate: drier, fresher and more petitgrain-like than methyl anthranilate, with mandarin-leaf and orange-blossom character and no Schiff-base discoloration. Preferred for stable, non-discoloring orange-flower effects.

Extremely powerful fenugreek, maple syrup and burnt-sugar note, becoming curry-like when overdosed; detectable at parts per billion. A trace-level secret weapon for maple, immortelle, rum and caramel realism.

Takasago prints floral, muguet, green and sweet, with a very diffusive bloom, and places it in almost any floral accord but mainly muguet and lilac. It is the chiral (S)-hydroxycitronellal made by asymmetric hydrogenation, and suppliers describe it as a very clean version of hydroxycitronellal: a delicate sweet lily-of-the-valley that seems to gain odour strength with time on the strip, tenacious and diffusive, good in white florals and comfortable alongside citrus. Substantivity on skin, fabric and hair is poor, so it works as a character material rather than a fixative, dosed under five percent.
Powerful warm-spicy, herbaceous green oil with woody undertones. Trace use gives natural green-spicy complexity to herbal and fougere accords.

dsm-firmenich list JASMINE EGYPT SFE CERT (952657) as floral, fruity, animalic: the fragility of the flower set against the astonishing power of its scent. A supercritical CO2 extract of Jasminum grandiflorum rather than a solvent absolute, so the low-temperature extraction keeps the natural profile identity of the flower and gives a fresher, more transparent reading than the absolute, with the indolic animalic facet still present but less heavy. Roughly 660 kg of flowers make 1 kg of extract, with biomass from third-party audited sources. Use it as the jasmine heart where the absolute would smell too dense or too solvent-laden.
Sweet, balsamic-amber with soft cinnamon, dried-fruit and honey nuances, longer-lasting than methyl cinnamate. Excellent glue between spicy top notes and ambery-balsamic bases in opulent perfumes.

Retailers describe it as an incredibly beautiful reconstitution of neroli oil: bright clean neroli, floral green perfection, very useable and modern. Listings tag it across citrus, floral, herbal, mandarin, orange flower and petitgrain, which is the shape of the material, a neroli built out of its own petitgrain and citrus edges rather than a single floral note. It is carried as a drop-in for natural neroli where cost or batch consistency rules the natural out, and works in a formula as a bright floral heart that lifts a cologne or a chypre top without the honeyed indole weight of orange flower absolute.
Waxy, fresh citrus-orange odor with a fatty herbal nuance. Adds a natural fresh-peel and coriander-like lift. Sold as the predominantly-trans commercial grade.

Sweet, rich, balsamic and powdery notes of the aroma of honey, sold by Perfumer Supply House off the IFF product sheet and classed there as a base note; Perfumer's Apprentice lists the same material as a deep, rich honey with light powdery notes. Buyers consistently report it reads floral-pollen rather than purely gourmand, closer to picked dandelions with powder over them than to a syrup. Scentspiracy describes it as recreating the sweet, waxy-balsamic warmth of honey by combining honey absolute with synthetic enhancers, worked at a fraction of a percent up to a few percent. In a formula it is the warming, faintly animalic sweetener that thickens white florals, tobacco and amber accords without the fatty beeswax drag of the absolute.
Anisic, sweet-spicy note in the direction of estragole with licorice and sassafras character. Stable methyl chavicol replacer for fougere, anise and basil effects.

Robertet publishes the olfactive description as "Floral, white flower, sweet" and describes the material itself as the reaction product of a hydroxycitronellal/indole Schiff base with methyl anthranilate. It is supplied at 50 percent, so the bottle standing on the bench is already a dilution and the weighed amount is not the weighed amount of active. What it gives is the indolic depth and honeyed animal warmth of a real white flower, jasmine, tuberose or orange blossom, without the sharp naphthalene mothball attack that free indole brings and without indole's habit of going brown and dirty in the drydown. Being a Schiff base it is heavy and tenacious, so it anchors a white-floral accord down in the base instead of blooming in the heart, and it is the material to reach for when a jasmine reads thin and clean but will not tolerate raw indole.
Sweet fruity-plum note with heavy white-floral jasmine undertones. Rounds jasmine, gardenia and tropical fruit accords.

Givaudan's specialties brochure calls it a pleasant citrus accord which evokes freshly squeezed tangerine peel blended with floral marine notes, giving it an unusual sparkling zest. It is described as extremely diffusive and long lasting and holds up in most functional product bases. Designed as a top-to-middle note, it gives freshness and volume to citrus, floral and green accords, and reads brighter, wetter and more persistent than a straight tangerine oil in the same slot.

Sweet herbaceous-winey amber with tea, tobacco and slightly animalic ambergris facets from sclareol; far softer than Dalmatian sage. Indispensable in fougères, ambers and tobacco accords for natural sweet-hay depth.
Fresh green-spicy Thai ginger relative, cooler and greener than ginger, with terpinen-4-ol freshness. Modern spicy-fresh top note.

Supercritical nutmeg with the whole spice cabinet intact: sweet-woody, faintly boozy and far rounder than the steam-distilled oil, which by comparison reads thin and terpenic. Holds much longer in amber and gourmand bases; safrole and methyl eugenol still cap the dose.

dsm-firmenich places this under EARTHY - MOSSY in the naturals section of its perfumery ingredients catalogue, alongside the oakmoss Firbest grades, so the house's own placement is an earthy, mossy note. What matters more than the heading is what a FIRBEST actually is: the catalogue's own glossary defines the FIRABS/FIRBEST range as co-extractions of natural and synthetic ingredients, some of them captives, and then says of the FIRBEST grades specifically that they are developed the same way BUT they do not contain the mentioned ingredient, calling them reconstitution-like ingredients, a technical response to an artistic demand. So this smells of treemoss while containing no treemoss. In a formula it does the job treemoss absolute would do, the earthy mossy floor under a chypre or a fougere, and it arrives ready-diluted at 50% in triethyl citrate so it can be dosed straight from the bottle. Note the catalogue is a code-and-name leaflet: the family heading and the glossary are the whole of the published olfactive text, and no longer description exists in the source.

Chemically ethyl 5-norbornene-2-carboxylate. Bulkaroma describes it as a very impactful fruity tropical exotic note giving richness and opulence to any white flower accord, with a touch of green minty leaves, and lists it as ethereal, fruity, sweet, tropical, mango and guava. It is the opulence lever for mango, jackfruit, melon and guava accords, and its real value is under white florals, where it reads as the ripe pulpy sweetness a tuberose or frangipani has in the living flower. Impactful enough to shout, so it is dosed against the accord rather than poured into it.

The Good Scents Company carries it as green type at medium strength and describes it as green, fresh, floral, pear, bell pepper, tropical and radish; IFF's own compendium gives it as green, fresh floral (flower shop), vegetable and fruity. It is an ether of cis-3-hexenol, so it reads as the crushed-stem greenness of the hexenol family pushed toward flower-shop air with a watery pear-and-radish edge rather than plain cut grass. Blotter life is under an hour neat, which is exactly what it is for: a trace in the top gives a formula the wet, just-picked opening that a natural green note loses within minutes, and it clears before it can flatten the heart.

Modern Givaudan linear musk with unusual top-note radiance: silky, fruity red-berry musk that blooms early and adds a glowing, lifted muskiness through the heart. Useful where musks normally arrive too late.

Bedoukian describes a smooth, natural, green, sweet Anjou pear aroma with sugary notes; The Good Scents Company types it fruity and reads it as fruity green pear, and supplier copy gives a fruity-green, smooth Anjou pear with tropical undertones. Launched in 2023 and named for the pear variety, it is used to put a green, just-ripe pear into fruity and tropical accords alongside apple and mango, and Bedoukian also positions it as a way to bring sweetness to a woody accord.

The supplier describes it as woody and ambery, the pure dextro isomer of Norlimbanol, and in longer form as an incredibly powerful woody-amber signature with penetrating animalic dryness, elegant musky warmth, subtle sandalwood aspects and patchouli-direction nuances, producing an exceptionally diffusive and tenacious extreme desiccation effect. That desiccating dryness is the point of it in a formula: it strips moisture out of an accord and leaves a rasping, skin-close woody amber under everything else. It is a base note lasting over two weeks on a smelling strip, averages around 0.25% in a compound, and the same supplier notes the standard racemic quality is the easier of the two to dose, so the dextro wants weighing with precision.
Citrus-terpenic note with fresh lime and herbal facets. Reinforces lime, bergamot and petitgrain top notes.

A dsm-firmenich muguet base, not a single molecule: the house lists it as a balanced blend of Florol, Mayol, Hivernal Neo and a proprietary captive, built with their Natural Ingredients Centre as part of the Beyond Muguet work. It offers fresh, floral, muguet, watery and green notes associated with a light blooming transparency, with green, watery and aldehydic facets. Very stable, it replaces less stable floral aldehydes one for one and takes overdose well, where it lifts the freshness, transparency and diffusion of a muguet or white floral accord; it is one of the materials reached for in place of Lyral and Lilial.
Pungent, fruity-caramellic note with a sharp green lift; used in trace in fruity and rum accords.

Dry pine-resin and crushed green leaf with a peppery terpenic lift; brighter, thinner and far more volatile than the Chios gum absolute, which is thick and balsamic by comparison. A Mediterranean maquis top note that lifts labdanum and cistus chypres and gives fig and incense accords a resinous edge without weight.

The classic sweet, creamy vanilla note - powdery, balsamic and slightly phenolic - forming the sweet pole of nearly every amber accord. Cross-reference for the amber base trio (labdanum-benzoin-vanillin); powerful and extremely tenacious, and can discolor products.
Refined green-floral ivy leaf with soft woody and lychee nuances; the dioxolane acetal of Ligustral. Enriches fig, muguet, galbanum and aldehydic accords with natural leafy transparency.

An intense green-leafy, floral-aldehydic note recalling broom, with a sweet orange-blossom warmth and a citrus-peel edge underneath. Very long lasting; naturalises green, mimosa, honeysuckle and gardenia accords. Schiff base of Triplal and methyl anthranilate.

Waxy-soapy aldehyde with violet-fatty, slightly citrus-pine and clean linen facets, rounder and quieter than C-11. Smooths aldehydic tops and adds waxy petal realism to violet, lily and lilac accords.

Bedoukian describes a gourmand, sweet, nutty, walnut and hazelnut scent with a spicy, fruity and maple undertone. The Good Scents Company types it nutty and reads a characteristic black walnut aroma with woody nuances and a subtle herbaceousness, and gives a fragrance use level of traces to 1%. It is the material for a real nut rather than a praline: it emphasises walnut and hazelnut in gourmand accords, and used low it gives woody and fougere structures a dry, roasted, faintly coffee-and-liquorice nuttiness.
Powerful alliaceous-savory sulfur note; used in extreme trace for onion, garlic and savory reconstructions.

Takasago lists citrus, floral, grapefruit and rhubarb. The character is clean and natural, at first reminiscent of geraniol and citronellol but carrying a distinct grapefruit nuance and a tart rhubarb edge that keeps it from reading rosy. Adding 0.1% to 3% to a compound gives naturalness and freshness to a wide range of floral notes and even to citrus-fruity accords, softening the synthetic edge of rose alcohols without adding weight. Good substantivity on skin and hair, with over 24 hours on the blotter.
Fruity-floral, fatty rose-cognac note with a green edge. Rounds fruity and rose accords.

Fresh green-spicy cinnamon with a herbal lift, rounder and less biting than cinnamaldehyde itself. Hydrolyses back to cinnamaldehyde in acidic media but holds up in soap and alkaline bases, carrying the cinnamon note where cinnamal browns and oxidises; IFRA-restricted as a sensitizer in its own right.

A citrus floral aldehyde (IFF) with fresh orange, ozonic and lightly fruity facets and an exceptionally clean fresh-air quality. Strong and persistent for an aldehyde, it brightens colognes, citrus and modern floral tops with a diffusive outdoors freshness.
Robust tannic black tea with dry leaf, mild earthiness and brewed astringency. A low-dose base for black-tea accords that can be steered toward Earl Grey or smoky tea themes.
Sweet fruity-rosy ester with honeyed banana-pineapple nuances over a warm petal base. Rounds fruity-rose and honey accords and softens harsh rose alcohols.

Roasted peanut and hot popcorn with potato-chip and toasted-cereal facets over a savoury base. More powerful and more characteristic than plain acetylpyrazine, so it is kept to trace level for peanut, praline and fresh-popcorn gourmand effects.
Mild, dry woody-terpenic hydrocarbon from pine and cedar sources with a faint oily nuance. Used as a woody diluent and feedstock for woody-amber synthetics.
Sweet anisic-green floral with hawthorn, heliotrope and slightly fruity-almond facets, more diffusive than anisaldehyde. Modern anisic-floral heart note for lilac, mimosa and powdery fougère accords.

An elegant long-lasting woody base reminiscent of sandalwood and Alaskan cedarwood that is creamy, powerful and diffusive. A compounded Firmenich reconstruction rather than a sandalwood oil, so it carries the milky, rounded sandalwood signature with the cedar dryness that gives it projection, and it does so at a consistency and cost the natural cannot match. In a formula it is a base-note foundation for a santal accord or the creamy floor under a woody-floral, and its diffusivity means it pushes rather than merely persisting, which is unusual for a sandalwood character.

Bee-glue resinoid: warm balsamic resin over a waxy, honeyed body with a dry cinnamic-vanillic tail. The natural bridge between beeswax and labdanum, and a quiet fixative that gives hive and amber accords a lived-in sweetness.
Warm, herbaceous, medicinal thyme with a phenolic bite. A powerful aromatic note for fougere and spicy-herbal accords.

Berjé describes a sweet and refreshing natural citrus product packed with an intense juiciness reminiscent of freshly scratched orange peels. The aroma sits very close to conventional orange oil, but the juicy quality is more pronounced and, unusually, stays consistent all the way through the evaporation instead of thinning out after the first minutes. Sold from the Citrus EE Series as a way to enhance or extend the potency and tenacity of an orange profile, so it is weighed in beside an expressed orange oil to keep the peel character alive further down the drydown. Berjé lists the plant part as exudate and publishes no CAS on the product page.

Firmenich polycyclic methoxy-aldehyde with a crisp green-aldehydic, metallic-ozonic freshness and watery cucumber-floral facets; very diffusive and unusually stable in bleach and alkaline media. Used in traces to give marine lift to functional and fine fragrance. Subject to IFRA restriction, so dose within current standards.
Enzymatically transformed patchouli fraction with a spicy, peppery, woody-ambery and oud-like character bridging patchouli and agarwood. A distinctive modern woody-spicy signature.
Fresh, sweet fruity odor with pineapple and green-apple facets. Widely used in fruity flavor-type accords.

Sweet, creamy woody oil that reads closer to sandalwood than to cypress, with honeyed, faintly smoky and fruity nuances over a guaiol-eudesmol backbone. A tenacious natural fixative for woody, incense and amber accords; the guaiazulene formed during distillation gives the oil its blue colour.

Kao calls it a very powerful and natural fresh green note reminiscent of pollen, with a natural fruity undernote, and gives its olfactive reading as Green - Aldehydic - Floral. The pollen character is the reason to stock it: a dusty, slightly stamen-like green that sits between a leaf green and a floral rather than on either side of it. The house's own word is powerful, so it is dosed low and pre-diluted; used at trace it makes a floral accord read as a living flower instead of a reconstitution, and overdosed it turns the whole top harsh and aldehydic.
Sweet honey-rose ester with warm floral depth. Honey nuance for rose, geranium and opulent floral accords.

Steam-distilled lemon leaf and twig: a sharp citral-driven lemon, greener and distinctly more bitter than the expressed peel oil, with a woody undertone and a faint orange-blossom close. The citral body outlasts a cold-pressed lemon top, making it the natural way to hold lemon through a cologne, chypre or fougere.
Sweet, sherry-like caramel with fresh strawberry and slightly nutty-toasted facets; the methyl ether of furaneol. Adds sparkling jammy-caramel lift to fruity and gourmand accords at trace levels.

Fresh bergamot-citrus ester with a woody-floral body and a mild lavender herbaceousness, close to linalyl acetate but fully saturated. Chosen for bergamot and lavender effects in soap, bleach and alkaline bases where linalyl acetate hydrolyses or oxidises.

Purified, odorless distilled water used as the aqueous phase and diluent in water-based fragrance formats such as body splashes, mists and hydro-alcoholic bases. Contributes no odor of its own and is combined with ethanol or solubilizers to carry aromatics.
Warm honey and dry woody note with chrysanthemum, dried-flower, powdery orris and phenolic aspects. Enhances ionones and bridges woody-floral accords.

An original leaf concept built from new specific Givaudan molecules, which is why it cannot be reproduced under another house's name. It smells of dry green tea leaf rather than brewed tea: convincing, leafy and clean, with a hay-like and clean-laundry aspect and no bitterness. Suppliers describe it as extremely diffusive and strong. In a formula it adds freshness, luminosity and a sense of cleanliness, and it is used in fresh florals, citrus colognes, musk accords and contemporary woody bases, as well as in beauty and laundry care where its diffusion earns its place.

dsm-firmenich file it under the musky family with the descriptors musky and ambrette, and call it a well balanced association of ingredients, some of them captives, blended into a specialty rather than sold as a single molecule. Perfumer's Apprentice describe it as a delicate and elegant musk built from fine alicyclic and macrocyclic musks, with a fruity-musky side from Helvetolide and Romandolide enhanced by Habanolide and Exaltolide. In a formula it is a finished musk accord in one bottle: clean and soft with a warm ambrette-seed edge, it sits in the drydown and lends smoothness and a substantive tail to anything from an airy floral to a detergent base, saving the work of balancing four musks by hand.
Yeasty, fruity and green ketone used as a fresh fruity-green modifier.

Takasago describes it as much cleaner and closer to lemon than the commonly known racemic mixture, sitting across citrus, green, fruity and floral with the characteristic nitrile undernote beneath. That cleanliness is the point of the chiral grade. It gives a bright lemon top that survives where citrus aldehydes and esters die, with outstanding stability across the whole pH range including inorganic acid cleaners and bleach. In fine fragrance it is a clean citrus lift dosed under five percent; in functional bases it is the reason a lemon top note is still there at the end of the wash. About six hours on the blotter.
Intensely sulfurous, alliaceous onion-garlic odor. Ultra-trace use for savory, tropical (durian, blackcurrant) and vegetal effects.
Delicate lemon-like citron peel oil, sweeter and more floral than lemon. Refined natural citrus for colognes and eau fraiche styles.
Warm amber-herbaceous resin straight from the sun-baked shrub: honeyed, leathery, slightly medicinal. Drier and more aromatic than labdanum absolute; the heart of amber accords.

Sweet lemon-orange citrus, rounder and softer than citral itself and without citral's metallic bite. Chosen for lemon notes in soap, bleach and other harsh acid or alkaline media, where free citral would drift to p-cymene off-notes.

Symrise blend of macrocyclic lactone musks (cyclopentadecanolide with cyclohexadecanolide isomers) giving a smooth, warm, powdery-clean musk with slight animalic depth. Convenient ready-made replacement for pure Exaltolide at lower cost.

Robertet's supplier listing describes it simply as woody, leather, ambery, floral and fruity. It is made by fractionating Cedarwood Atlas essential oil and blending back only the woody, leathery, floral and ambery fractions, so the sharp terpenic and sour edges that make raw Atlas cedarwood hard to place are absent. The Good Scents Company profiles Atlas cedarwood fractions in the same direction, as oriental, lactonic, balsamic, leathery, amber, floral and fruity at 3% in dipropylene glycol, with a slightly fruity liquorous drydown. In a formula it does the job of a creamy, sandalwood-leaning cedar base: it will hold a woody-amber or leather accord together for the whole drydown without the dryness and rasp of the whole oil, which means it can sit under florals where straight Atlas cedarwood would tear them.

Fresh clean citrus with a pronounced sweet-orange peel character, lightly aldehydic and ozonic over a green leafy base. The latent form of Aldehyde C-8: it hydrolyses slowly to release octanal, so it gives the same orange-peel lift without the sharp neat aldehyde or the acidic drift that spoils C-8 in the bottle.

Sweet floral anthranilate with rose, grape, orange and iris facets over a honeyed base; softer and much less pungent than methyl anthranilate but far more tenacious. The heaviest of the common anthranilates: a fixative that carries orange-blossom, tuberose and narcissus effects into the drydown without the Schiff-base discoloration risk.
Woody vetiver specialty base with citrus and floral facets. Adds a clean freshness to vetiver accords.

A soft, clean soapy-waxy fatty alcohol with warm honey and coconut undertones and an earthy edge. Quiet but very persistent; a fixative for mimosa, cassie and aldehydic florals. 1-Dodecanol, a waxy solid at room temperature.
Green muguet with melon and fresh-air nuances, softer and rounder than Precyclemone B and free of indolic heaviness. Excellent naturaliser for green accords and lily of the valley effects.

Eternis describes its cis article as sweet, almost creamy and woody with a stronger floral undertone than regular PTBCHA, and that comparison is the whole reason this grade exists. The cis isomer is the softer, more floral-powdery half of the material, with an orris-like dryness and a faint fruit-skin nuance, while the trans isomer carries the flat cedar-woody depth; enriching the cis shifts the whole character toward fine-fragrance florals. In a formula it is a blender: it sits under ionones, cedarwood and rose to give a clean woody floor without smoke or resin, and it is famously stable in alkaline media, so it is a standard soap and detergent workhorse as well. Dose it low as a rounding agent or push it up where you want the woody-floral to lead.

Delicate, waxy linden-muguet sesquiterpene alcohol with a mild green-floral, slightly balsamic petal character; natural in rose, jasmine and tuberose. Quiet fixative that prolongs floral hearts and doubles as a deodorizing agent.
Fresh, fatty-waxy, slightly rosy alcohol with an aldehydic character softer than nonanal. Citrus and rose modifier.

Givaudan's own specialties book: it reflects the distinctive fresh fruity and tasty red apple odour and evokes the taste sensation of a red apple juice, and the house descriptor table shortens this to fruity, fresh, red apple. A floral background enhances its volume and provides a nice harmony in fragrance, giving sophisticated fruity natural freshness to floral accords with lift and radiance. In practice it is a top-end fruit modifier rather than a complete accord: dropped into a floral it reads as juice rather than as candy, and because the floral underlay carries it, the effect lifts the whole composition instead of sitting on top of it.

Penetrating camphoraceous-herbaceous sage with thujone sharpness and a slightly spicy, cedar-leaf dryout. Adds savory herbal bite to fougères and aromatic colognes; thujone content warrants restraint.

Balsamic cinnamyl ester with fruity, floral and green-herbal facets and a distinct narcissus tonality, lighter and sharper than the acetate. Used in hyacinth, narcissus and lilac bases where a green-balsamic cinnamyl lift is wanted.

IFF specialty ether with a clean marine-ozonic odor, drier and less sweet than Calone, evoking cool coastal air with a subtle floral transparency. Useful to extend ozone accords into the heart without watermelon fruitiness.

Sweet, heavy, fruity-powdery nitro musk with a distinctive ambrette-seed warmth, once the soul of countless fougeres and ambers. PROHIBITED by IFRA (photoallergen and neurotoxic); reference material for understanding vintage formulas only.

Rich, boozy coumarin-hay sweetness with tobacco, almond, caramel and dried-fruit depth from cured Dipteryx odorata beans. The natural, more complex alternative to coumarin for amber, fougere and tobacco bases; its high coumarin content makes IFRA coumarin limits apply.
Fresh, sweet-aromatic and softly spicy with a linalool-driven floral-woody smoothness and a peppery nuance. A versatile modifier bridging citrus tops with spicy-floral hearts in colognes and ambers.

Fresh, intensely floral muguet alcohol with transparent, lightly green and fruity nuances, close to the dewy smell of the living flower. Very stable in bases; a mainstay of modern hydroxycitronellal-free muguets.

Moellhausen describes this base as intriguing, delicate and inebriating, its jasmine entry in the third BoldBases series. It is a composed base, not an absolute and not a single jasmine molecule, built to a narrow olfactory profile of fewer than eight elementary components with high intensity and persistency. In a formula it does the work of a jasmine heart in one line: the delicacy keeps it from going flat and soapy, while the inebriating side gives a white floral the heady lift that usually costs a careful blend of several materials.
Potent buttery caramel and toasted malt with baked-pastry and faint liquorice facets. A trace material for bread, pastry, caramel and dairy accords; distinct from Corylone/Cyclotene CAS 80-71-7.

The violent green of crushed grass and torn leaf, grassy and weedy over a fatty base with a fruity apple-skin edge. Nothing else lands this cut-grass impact; it isomerises to the trans-2 isomer readily, so it is worked from dilution and added late.

Steam-distilled Bulgarian/Turkish rose oil: honeyed, spicy-lemony rose with waxy petal and green facets, crystallizing at room temperature due to stearoptenes. The reference heart for fine rose accords; a trace lifts citrus colognes and chypres.

Bedoukian describe Valencial as "Aldehydic with peely, orange, waxy notes", their fuller listing adding fatty, waxy citrus peel with hints of cilantro. The Good Scents Company give "citrus metallic mandarin orange waxy aldehydic" at high odour strength, recommend smelling it at one percent or less, and record a blotter life of 72 hours at ten percent in dipropylene glycol. It smells of the zest itself rather than the juice: a slightly metallic mandarin peel that is oily and green-fatty underneath. A trace at the top of a citrus accord makes the fruit read as freshly grated instead of distilled, and it lends a natural, faintly herbal cilantro edge to mandarin, coriander and neroli work. It is powerful and fatty enough to turn heavy and greasy fast if overdosed, so it belongs in the traces.

Smooth, slightly sweet ketonic musk (cis/trans cyclohexadec-8-enone) with a warm, faintly animalic and powdery profile, close to Velvione but softer. A versatile Symrise workhorse for rounded, natural-smelling musk bases.

Rosy-spicy damascone-like note with fruity-berry, rose oxide and woody-herbaceous nuances; sweeter apple facet, less metallic than the damascones and free of their IFRA restriction. Excellent in rose, carnation, chypre and fougere.

A clean green apple ester (IFF), 2-tert-butylcyclohexyl acetate, with a crisp fruity woody character that leans more toward Granny Smith apple and pear than cut grass. Brighter and more transparent than cis-3-hexenyl acetate, it adds fresh fruity volume and a subtle woody lift to fruity, floral and functional accords.

Firmenich indane aldehyde delivering a cold, mineral, ozonic-muguet freshness reminiscent of crisp winter air and sun-dried laundry, with green watery nuances. Powerful modern alternative for aldehydic-fresh lift in transparent florals and clean musks.
Sweet fruity-floral note with berry, green, pineapple and rhubarb facets.

A natural-reading rose de mai note: green and lightly earthy, with a spicy edge, honeyed sweetness and tea-rose and peony facets. Adds authenticity and lift to rose, peony and other floral hearts. 2-Methoxybenzyl ethyl ether.

Odorless, biodegradable citrate ester solvent favored in natural and clean-label perfumery as a DPG/phthalate alternative; also a mild fixative that slows evaporation. Good solvency for most aroma chemicals and safe in deodorant formats.

Intensely smoky, tarry, phenolic juniper-wood note evoking campfire, smoked meat and creosote. Tiny doses give birch-tar-like leather and smoke effects to leather, incense and oud accords; only rectified qualities are permitted and IFRA-restricted.

A Givaudan captive precursor launched 19 October 2022. The house release describes a long-lasting floral green effect with honey and linden blossom facets, and high-performance floral fresh rosy signals with powdery anisic undertones. As a precursor it releases its fragrant molecules when exposed to natural triggers such as oxygen, light or humidity, delivering the notes gradually to extend performance and longevity rather than showing everything at once. It is biodegradable and was made using green chemistry through the FiveCarbon Path. In a formula it is the rosy-green tail that keeps working after the top has gone, joining Tonkarose, Clean, Juicy and Berry on the same palette.

Harsh but effective lemon-citrus nitrile with green-metallic and slightly floral-geranium facets. Formerly a functional-perfumery citral substitute; now prohibited by IFRA, kept here mainly for legacy formula reference.
Raw green apple-grass aldehyde, sharp and fatty in overdose, freshly juicy in traces. The green edge of apple and unripe fruit accords.

Soft floral lilac with piney-lily undertones and a faintly citrusy freshness; the backbone of classic lilac reconstructions. Inexpensive floralizer used widely from fine fragrance to functional products.

Sweet nutty and roasted coffee furanone with a caramelised, bready warmth and none of the sulfur harshness of the coffee thiols. The clean partner to those mercaptans, useful for coffee, praline and toasted-bread accords where a thiol would read rank, though it flashes off quickly.

Petrichor itself: wet earth after the first rain on a dry field, beetroot skin, damp cellar air. Deceptively soft in a 1% smelling - and one of the most potent odorants known (threshold in parts per trillion), a drop or two carries an entire formula. Trace use only, or everything turns dusty.

The Quest International speciality coded ABQ2977, now carried by Givaudan. Perfumer's Apprentice describe it as an exotic fruit, lychee and raspberry with a touch of herbal green, a very elegant fruity blend used in many popular modern perfumes; Hekserij read the same base as forest fruits, especially raspberry and blackcurrant, and note it is not particularly potent used alone. Its signature is the cassis lift of the Givaudan captive Neocaspirene, present at a few percent of the base, while the herbal-green undertone keeps the fruit from turning candied. In a formula it is a ready-made red and exotic fruit accord that needs no adjustment, working across the top and heart with a little carry into the base; suppliers suggest a few tenths of a percent up to about five percent of the base in the finished composition, and warn that aggressive media such as soaps and deodorants will partly compromise it.

Sweet, spicy carnation with a powdery, slightly smoky-vanillic aspect; an elegant, stable stand-in for isoeugenol. Widely used to rebuild carnation and warm-spicy hearts without isoeugenol's IFRA burden or discoloration.

Fresh and powerful green with a lemon-grapefruit bite. It is a coded speciality base sold separately from Firmenich's Oxane 50 TEC, and its job in a formula is the opening: a sharp green-citrus lift that cuts through a blend at very low dosage. Its power means it is worked from dilution, since a heavy hand pulls the whole top note toward it.

Givaudan spiro-ketal with a clean, dry woody-amber odor showing sparkling, almost pine-fresh top facets over a diffusive ambery trail. Gives modern transparency to amber accords and boosts woody notes without heaviness.
Rosy-green pyran with a fresh geranium and rose-oxide character, more complex and less metallic than rose oxide itself. Gives powerful, modern rose lift to florals and functional fragrances.

Vivid, citronellal-rich lime-leaf note, green, zesty and slightly rosy-metallic, instantly evoking Thai kaffir lime leaves. Adds an exotic culinary-green citrus twist to modern colognes and tea accords.
Transparent, almost dewy hyacinth floral with natural green top notes.
Warm, diffusive jasmine cyclopentanone with a fruity, slightly celery-like nuance; a good stable floralizer. Valued in soap and functional bases where jasmine absolutes fail.

Sharp, diffusive green-metallic rose top note with geranium, lychee and slightly minty facets; the smell of a rose stem snapped in the morning. Powerful, overdose turns metallic and harsh; a few tenths of a percent electrify rose and lychee accords.

Takasago: adds a natural, powerful and very diffusive earthy green odour reminiscent of fresh soil and morning dew, with mossy and woody facets around it. Supplied at 50% in dipropylene glycol and used between 0.01% and 0.2%, it is a trace-level naturaliser rather than a note you build on: it puts damp ground under green and floral accords and restores the wet-earth realism that synthetic muguet, violet-leaf and chypre constructions lose. Stable across a wide pH range, and about two days on the blotter.

Vigon 501460 cyclohexanone diethyl acetal, with rum-like boozy character and tobacco/woody nuances. Supplier top note and four-hour strip life. Strength is an editorial estimate; 10% dilution is a working convention, not a supplier recommendation.

Ambergris, woody and dry with a labdanum warmth, a soft marine-mineral salinity and a light sweetness. Radiant and long-lasting; the backbone of modern amber and skin-scent perfumery, from traces to bold overdoses.

Givaudan describe it as a fresh, juicy, green citrus floral note with a trendy grapefruit connotation and a soft peony undertone. The patent covering the molecule calls the character a clear citrus odour with a green grapefruit and rhubarb connotation, and stresses that it is highly blooming. In a formula it works as a bloom and lift material: a few tenths of a percent open a citrus top, push freshness and cleanliness without shifting the overall profile, and bridge grapefruit accords into a floral heart because of the peony facet.
Soft woody-floral linalool in natural form: clean, gently camphoraceous, rosewood-like. The sustainable rosewood alternative and a natural linalool source for IFRA-friendly florals.

Bland, transparent jasmin with lily, green and a faint lemon edge, much quieter and less oily than amyl cinnamic aldehyde itself. The stabilised form for soap and bleach-containing bases: it holds the jasmin body without the yellowing the free aldehyde causes.

Perfumer's Apprentice give the odour as woody, ambery, balsamic, rose, and describe the material as bright, powerful, diffusive and slightly animalic, built on rich dsm-firmenich captive ingredients that lend a fine unctuous character to a composition, with a fresh and fizzy undertone over a radiant oud-like warmth. It is a compounded house base carrying a mixture CAS, despite the generic name. In a formula it is a whole woody-amber drydown in one line: it gives projection and an unctuous rosy-balsamic body to an oud or amber accord, and a very little of it will dominate the base of a light composition.
The quintessential sweet pineapple ester, juicy and tropical with a slightly fatty edge. Small doses give convincing ripe pineapple; IFRA-restricted like most allyl esters for skin toxicity.

The cis-isomer of geraniol: fresher, wetter and more seaspray-green rose with a magnolia-like transparency and light citrus lift. Excellent for dewy rose tops, neroli accords and to freshen heavy florals.

IFF's own ingredients compendium describes it as a citrus, grapefruit note also reminiscent of the dry notes of bitter orange oil and melon, and says it is useful in colognes as a freshener to overcome the candy-sweet notes of orange and lemon oil. The molecule is the acetate of 2,4-dimethyl-3-cyclohexene-1-methanol, and unlike most citrus materials it is substantive for around twelve hours, so the grapefruit impression carries well past the opening and into the heart. That is precisely its job: a dry, bitter-peel grapefruit with a melon edge that refuses to turn sugary, holding a cologne bright long after the natural oils have gone.

Robertet's published description, carried by Perfumer's Apprentice, is "Gourmand, powerful, cocoa powder effect". The material is made by extracting cocoa with an ethanol and triacetin blend and then molecularly distilling it, which strips the colour and the non-volatile load while leaving the olfactive facets intact; Robertet's own perfumer describes the result as reminiscent of biting into a piece of dark chocolate, rich and full, everything from the raw bean through to the melting sweetness. Against a whole cocoa absolute it is far more concentrated and effectively colourless, so it is dosed much lower and does not drag a brown viscous mass into a pale composition. It carries the dry, dusty bitterness of cocoa powder over a sweet chocolate base and is the practical way to build a gourmand base that has to stay clear. Note that the supplied material is a mixture with its extraction carriers, so it has no single CAS of its own.
Powerful, somewhat harsh heavy fruity note reminiscent of ripe apple. Low tenacity; used for fruity top-note lift.

Kao describes it as fruity, flowery with an apple and wine-yeast note, and gives the descriptor triad Fruity - Apple - Green. The wine-yeast facet is what separates it from the ordinary apple esters: a slightly fermented, cidery lift under the fruit that reads as ripe rather than confected. In a formula it is a top-note apple with a floral tilt, useful where a green apple accord needs to feel fermented and rounded, and it fades quickly, so it opens a composition rather than carrying it.

The supplier listing describes Crisalys S as a fresh and transparent powerful note, slightly fruity, slightly powdery, with a hint of earthiness, akin to someone making a powder out of ivy and violet leaves. That comparison is the whole material: the cool crushed-leaf green of ivy and violet leaf, but dried and softened rather than sappy, with a faint fruit edge underneath. It is recommended at 3 to 5 percent to develop freshness in fruity-floral perfumes, where it opens out the top and keeps a sweet fruit accord from reading as jam.

A soft, dry-sweet wood with a floral lift from its high nerolidol content, recalling orange blossom, rose and muguet, plus balsamic warmth and a faint metallic brightness. Long-lasting; blends easily with cedarwood and naturalises neroli and orange-blossom accords. Wood oil of the cabreuva tree (Myrocarpus fastigiatus and/or M. frondosus).
Fresh, green-fruity, lavender-and-herbal alcohol with a mild sweet body; used in lavender, fruity and floral top notes.

A lush tropical pineapple note with a distinctive bubblegum character, enhanced by complex sweetness and rich, warm undertones. It belongs to Mane's Natpop range, a 100% olfactory reconstitution of fresh fruit notes, so it reads as a whole ripe fruit rather than a single ester, and unusually for a fruit note it holds over 24 hours on a smelling strip instead of flashing off in the top. Used in large amounts it gives a rich, lasting pineapple effect; in trace it sweetens a formula and adds fruity complexity. It suits tropical accords, gourmand blends and white florals, and works alongside coconut, gardenia and ylang bases. Note that it sits in the heart, unlike Mane's own top-note Pineapple Supreme.
Popcorn, corn tortilla and cracker-like roasted note with a sweet malty nuance. Used in ultra-traces for popcorn, bread-crust and roasted-grain effects in gourmand accords.

Sweet ambery-herbaceous absolute loaded with sclareol: hay, tobacco leaf and a honeyed wine-like warmth, with none of the oil's linalyl acetate freshness. The natural of choice for building ambergris and tobacco accords, and a quiet fixative sitting under fougeres and chypres.

Powerful fresh aldehydic citrus with mandarin and orange-peel bite over a green, faintly fatty body, lifting to crushed cardamom at trace. The cis isomer smells markedly closer to real citrus skin than the trans; hugely diffusive, so it is dosed in traces to naturalize citrus tops.
Creamy, coconut-and-peach lactone with a soft milky body; used in creamy fruity and dairy-gourmand accords.

A composition that captures the purity of a fresh river breeze: hints of watery notes and airy aldehydes lend a crisp, modern clarity. Firmenich classes it as Floral, and Master Perfumer Wessel-Jan Kos describes it as a versatile one-for-one replacement of cyclamen aldehyde, perfectly capturing the fresh muguet aspect and watery feel of that material. In a formula it is used exactly where cyclamen aldehyde would be, dosed at one to two percent in the house's own published trials; at the lower level it lifts orange blossom nuances and at the higher level it deepens the effect, and it cuts cleanly through creamy lactonic fruitiness to add refreshing clarity. It carries an EcoIngredient Compass green score above seventy percent and is ultimately biodegradable.

Fresh, transparent muguet-lilac indane alcohol with watery, soapy-clean petal character and high volume. A key Lilial/Lyral-replacement generation material for lily-of-the-valley, lilac and gardenia transparency.

A fruity tropical guava odour that, per the supplier listing, brings strong tropical guava, mango and passion fruit notes and enhances juiciness even at low concentration. A colourless to pale yellow liquid holding about a day on the blotter, with very good burn performance and very good substantivity when damp. In a formula it is a ready-made exotic fruit heart: a little makes a generic fruity accord read as ripe and mouth-watering, and larger doses carry a full tropical theme without having to build guava from single esters.

Powerful animalic quinoline with a civet-like warmth, a leathery undertone far lighter than isobutyl quinoline and an ambergris-like nuance in dilution. Used in traces for synthetic civet and discreet animalic effects, and in honey and tobacco accords; a good fixative. 6-Methyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinoline.

Pine and camphoraceous with a citrus lift and a woody, balsamic body; The Good Scents Company records it as a balsamic odour type of medium strength and describes it as sweet balsamic citrus pine herbal. It is the workhorse pine alcohol rather than a signature: in a formula it carries and extends woody and coniferous accords, rounds the raw turpentine edge off pinene-heavy naturals, and holds a fresh forest note through a soap or cleaner base where the terpenes themselves would collapse. TGSC gives about thirty-two hours on the blotter, so it is a genuine fixative for its family. It is unforgiving next to delicate florals, where even a modest dose flattens them.

Ferociously fecal and ammoniac in concentration, but at high dilution it blooms into radiant, honeyed animal warmth that makes florals glow with life. The classic 'dirty' secret of jasmine and rose grand classics; use in traces from strong dilution.

Perfumer's Apprentice list it in the woody family with the odour given as woody and ambery, and describe it as a fresh, light, crisp teak blend from Firmenich. It is a compounded house base carrying a mixture CAS rather than a single molecule, currently supplied as version 109955 GRF17 after the earlier version was discontinued in 2023. In a formula it is a dry sawn-timber woody-amber that reads lighter and crisper than a sandalwood or oud base, useful as the woody spine of a masculine or a modern fougere where a creamy wood would sit too heavy.

Smooth mossy wood with balsamic sweetness, warm resin and soft leather. A Synarome oakmoss reconstruction for chypres, fougeres and green fixation, without claiming the identity of natural oakmoss absolute.
Sweet rosy-geranium floral note with a fruity leafy nuance. Used in rose, geranium and fruity accords.
A modern captive woody note with a smooth, creamy sandalwood-cedar character and radiant diffusion. Used to add refined woody warmth and volume.

dsm-firmenich describe Z11 (product 992964) as dry, woody and ambery notes with a strong trigeminal effect, filed under the ambery olfactive family and recommended for fine fragrance as a heart and base note. The trigeminal bite is the point: it does not just smell ambery, it produces a physical cooling-tingling sensation that makes the whole drydown feel wider than its mass. Made by sugar fermentation and bio-conversion, and only sold as this 10 percent MIP dilution, so it is weighed as supplied. Use it where Ambrox alone reads flat, to give a woody-amber base volume, dryness and a mineral edge.

Sulfurous tropical thiol reading as pink grapefruit and passion fruit with guava, gooseberry and blackcurrant facets and a box-tree green underside. One of the most used sulfur materials in modern fine fragrance and the signature thiol of Sauvignon Blanc; the tenacious member of the family, dosed at ppm and below to make fruit accords smell juicy rather than candied.
Sweet, warm floral absolute of the night-flowering jasmine (coral jasmine) with honeyed, orange-blossom-like and slightly spicy facets. Exotic Indian floral for amber bouquets.
Camphoraceous-fresh cineole blast with cooling medicinal and slightly woody facets. Instant freshness for aromatic fougères, sport scents and mint accords; a little goes far.

Distinctive Japanese citrus combining mandarin sweetness, grapefruit bitterness and a green, floral, slightly herbal peel character. Used for exotic, transparent modern citrus tops; expensive, so often recreated with bases.

Lemon-sherbet citral brightness on a green, herbal-tea body, with a soft neroli-like floral facet and a hay-like, lightly woody-spicy drydown; far longer-lasting than the oil. Solvent-extracted absolute of the aerial parts of lemon verbena (Lippia citriodora), Morocco.

IFF orris specialty delivering a powdery, suede-like iris-butter effect with woody-violet undertones at a fraction of the cost of natural orris. Functions as a soft fixative and texturizer in powdery florals and cosmetics accords.

Sweet, candy-like lime with a distinctive boiled-sweet, slightly terpenic-piney character, less peely than the expressed oil. Classic in colognes and men's fougeres (the famous lime of barbershop accords) and in cola flavors-turned-fragrance.

With its unusual animalic essence and prominent woody and ambery notes, Oud Samrat carries the distinctive oud quality wanted in fine perfumery, and is very strong and long lasting in the typical woody animalic facet of oud. It is the third of Firmenich's three Oud Assafi specialties alongside Anokha and Maleki, and leans warm and ambery where Maleki stays dry. Supplied at 10 percent in DPG, it is used as the oud heart of an oriental or woody base at low dose, where its amber side lets it sit against labdanum and benzoin without fighting them.
Fresh camphoraceous-herbaceous sage with lavender-like and eucalyptus facets, softer than Dalmatian sage. Herbal freshness for fougeres and colognes.

The perfumer's workhorse diluent: odorless, colorless, low-volatility solvent used for diluting aroma chemicals, making study dilutions and formulating oil-based and functional fragrances. Fragrance grade (low odor) is essential; slows evaporation slightly versus ethanol.

Crisp green apple with a waxy body, fleshy banana-pear nuances and a faint spicy-tropical lift. A workhorse in apple and pear accords, longer lasting than hexyl acetate and cleaner than hexyl hexanoate.

Nutty peanut-butter roast with musty-fermented coffee facets and a dry tobacco edge, rounder and less harsh than the methyl homologue. A softening trace note for coffee, tobacco and roasted-nut bases where the sharper pyrazines cut too hard.

Fraterworks Royal Leather, safety-document grade 674276A, a smooth leather base with animalic and sandalwood character. Distinct from Cuir de Russie and Suederal. The product page uses reference 674276; current SDS, IFRA and allergen declarations identify 674276A. Supplier strip life exceeds 400 hours, a lower bound only. IFRA 51 Category 4 maximum is 49.23% in finished product. Strength is editorial and 10% working dilution conventional; group-level constituent allocations remain under review.

Zeon's own catalogue describes a powerful floral-herbaceous, sweet odour like jasmin absolute, giving the soft and elegant smell of the jasmin flower. The Good Scents Company records it as jasmin flower, oily, green, petal-soft and greasy at medium odour strength, which is the honest reading: it is the waxy, slightly fatty petal facet of a real jasmine rather than a clean floral chemical. Zeon notes that a small addition creates a long-lasting exciting effect, and it holds around 256 hours on a blotter neat. In a formula it is the floraliser for jasmine, white floral and fruity-floral accords, needed at considerably lower weight than hedione for the same lift. Note that this is methyl jasmonate, not the methyl epi-jasmonate sold by the same house as Zeppin.
Roasted, popcorn-and-cereal pyrazine with a nutty-toasted body; used in trace for popcorn, bread and gourmand notes.

Bergamot leaf and twig, very high in linalyl acetate: bergamot's sweet-green freshness laid over a soft floral-woody petitgrain body, cleaner and less bitter than bigarade. Carries the bergamot signature with no bergapten, so it lifts a cologne top without the expressed oil's phototoxicity cap.
Fresh citrus-terpenic, slightly harsh note found in many essential oils. Used for lift in citrus, herbal and functional fragrances.

The Good Scents Company lists it as green type at medium strength: fresh flower shop, green, natural green, tropical fruit, with fruity apple and pear facets. It is the cyclopropanecarboxylate ester of cis-3-hexenol, so the cut-grass signature of hexenol arrives softened by the ester and carrying ripe apple, pear and banana over it. Neat it is sharp and almost aldehydic and shows very little of itself; it opens out only on dilution and in blend. Perfumers use it in the top and upper heart to give a natural, growing greenness with fruit underneath, and it is one of the standard ways to stop a green accord from smelling only of cut leaf.
Sweet fruity, rum-candy floral note with a citrus nuance. Diffusive powerful blending agent for fruity-floral accords.

Soft, sweet-floral absolute of the Nile blue water lily with green, honeyed and slightly spicy-tea nuances. Exotic mystical floral note; distinct from pink lotus and sacred (Nelumbo) lotus. Avena Lab's safety sheet files the absolute under CAS 91723-04-5 and classifies it as a mild skin and eye irritant and a skin sensitiser; no supplier found publishes a breakdown or an IFRA certificate for it, so its content stays unassessed here.

Barely there: a faint, heavy waxy-fatty note with a creamy, candle-wax and oily skin-like softness. Used for texture rather than scent, to slow top notes, anchor musks and add the waxy body of petals or orris butter. A C16 saturated fatty acid.

Bold, zesty lemon-citral character in nitrile form: sharp, slightly green-metallic, and dramatically more stable and tenacious than citral. The go-to citral replacer for soaps, cleaners and long-lasting lemon tops.

Three to four times stronger than vanillin with a richer, sweeter, more chocolate-like vanilla character. Used at lower levels than vanillin to intensify amber and gourmand bases; blends of the two give the most natural effect.
Soft, fresh-rosy fruity ester with a natural geranium warmth, rounder and more refined than citronellyl acetate. Lends a polished petal effect to rose and floral-fruity tops.

Molecularly distilled heart of olibanum resin with rich balsamic incense depth, warm spice and a clear lemony-terpenic lift. It is a purified resin-derived grade, not olibanum essential oil, absolute or CO2 extract.

The house files it as Balsamic. Traditional olibanum, they write, carries a sweet, woody and balsamic undertone over a green, terpenic opening, sensual and rich and typically ambery; this SFE grade instead offers an extremely pure, noble profile, because low-temperature supercritical CO2 extraction preserves all the facets and purity of the extract. In a trial fragrance it takes a composition that leans greener and more stem-like, with vegetal and raw facets, and softens exactly those, giving a rounder, more polished impression that becomes more balsamic and gains depth and smoothness. Principal Perfumer Fabrice Pellegrin uses it to give vertical vibrations to musky notes and to reinforce their mineral facets. Boswellia carterii gum tapped on the Golis mountains of the Sanaag region, Somalia, from FairWild certified biomass.

Powerful rose ketone with green apple, blackcurrant bud and slightly minty-woody facets, the most diffusive of the damascone family. Used in traces to modernize rose and add fruity radiance to florals and chypres.
Fresh, clean citrus-lime odor with a mild floral-metallic nuance; more stable than dihydromyrcenol. Used in fresh fougere and functional accords.
Fresh bergamot character with floral and fruity-pear facets; a stable modifier that improves the bergamot effect in fresh and floral accords.
Dry, dark tea leaf with hay, herbal and smoky facets and a leathery, arnica-like character, drying down to a clean, long-lasting castoreum-like leather. A strong fixative.

Takasago's house description for the Orbitone T line is woody, ambergris, floral and violet, an ingredient that gives sophisticated body and velvety richness. Fraterworks describes the 2026 Neo reprocess as an elegant, velvety woody-amber with sophisticated balsamic and creamy facets and subtle violet floral undertones, reading more balsamic and creamy than standard Iso E Super with greater transparency and a sense of space. In a formula it is a volumiser rather than a statement: dosed at several percent it lifts and rounds everything around it, blurs the seams between fresh-fruity, floral and woody-amber accords, and lays a soft ambergris, vetiver and patchouli shadow underneath. The higher gamma-isomer content of the Neo grade buys slightly more diffusion than the original it replaces.
Crystalline sesquiterpene alcohol with a soft, dry, mild woody-cedar odor and faint camphoraceous nuance. A near-odorless fixative and volume-builder for woody bases.

Givaudan's description is a strong dry woody note with camphor and warm metallic undertones, classed olfactively as woody, dry and ambery. It is 4,5-decamethyleneoxazole, and it is sold only as an 80 percent solution in dipropylene glycol, so the bottle on the bench is already a dilution and the dosing has to account for it. Its real function is as a musk booster and fixative: it has good substantivity on both damp and dry substrate and works synergistically with musky and ambery materials, Ambrofix in particular, lifting them without adding a sweet amber of its own. Normally kept below 1 percent, though it can be pushed higher to build a distinctive dry woody signature. Several days on the blotter and excellent bloom in soap.

Givaudan's own specialties book reduces it to citrus, fruity, bergamot oil, and describes the material as a reconstitution that is bergapten-free and has no phototoxic potential, a bergamot made to replace the essential oil with superior stability and performance in functional products. PerfumersWorld resolve the profile further as an aliphatic-citrus and herbaceous opening moving into a linalool-rich citrus heart with a coniferous edge, at a middling relative odour impact and a typical use of a couple of percent in a compound. In a formula it is the bergamot you reach for when the natural oil would discolour or fade: it gives the classic fougere and chypre top, performs well in alcoholic perfume and in bath and shower gel, and its known weakness is discolouration in antiperspirant and chlorine-containing bases.

FAO's benzoin trade study records it as an excellent economical substitute for benzoin resinoid products, similar to them in odour performance, with a characteristic balsamic, vanilla, resinous complex, used at up to 5%. Unlike the 63 it is built on proprietary synthetics rather than around natural benzoin resin, so it is the cost-driven choice for the same warm, sweet, balsamic fixative role in ambers, orientals and vanillas, and its natural-content claim differs accordingly. It is a compounded base and carries no single CAS.
Green vegetable and sulfurous-metallic character reminiscent of fuzzy peach skin and apricot, with earthy, fruity, nutty, tropical, coffee and meaty facets.

Perfumer's Apprentice describes it as a "naturalistic accord" that "embodies the ripe and fresh qualities of a fresh summer strawberry". Both halves are stated on purpose: ripe carries the sweet fruit body, fresh keeps a bright top on it, and together they read as the whole fruit rather than the confectionery version. Being an all-natural compounded base, it is a single line in a formula that would otherwise take several materials to assemble. Sits well in the heart of a fruity floral, and pairs naturally with the raspberry from the same range when a mixed-berry impression is wanted.

Explosive bitter-green resinous burst of snapped stems, green peppers and pine-like terpenes over a balsamic, slightly animalic dryout. The reference natural green note, essential in chypres, galbanum florals (Vent Vert style) and modern green fougères.

Egyptian bitter-orange blossom oil: greener, sharper and more metallic-terpenic than the Tunisian, with less of the soft linalool sweetness and more bitter petal bite. The main price and quality alternative to Tunisian neroli, and the better choice when the blossom has to cut through a cologne rather than soften it.

Privi gives the character simply as "Woody, Ambery": a smooth, dry, transparent woody-amber of the octahydrotetramethyl acetonaphthone family, more a velvet backdrop than a sharp cedar. What separates it from an ordinary grade of that chemistry is the declared isomer split, with an alpha and beta balance of its own and a charm peak specified in the low single-digit percent range, because it is the charm isomer that carries most of the perceived odour. Privi publishes a tenacity of about one week and a use level up to ten percent, which is the clue to how it behaves: low impact per drop, but it takes large doses without shouting and it lifts and rounds everything around it. Standard duty is as a volume and diffusion booster under woods, amber and musk.
Warm, sweet, spicy cinnamon: the red-hot heart of amber and gourmand spice accords. Bark-type, rich in cinnamaldehyde.

Narcissus-like animalic ester combining horse-stable warmth, honey and phenolic-floral facets. Bridges animalic-leather bases with white florals and adds vintage 'barnyard chic' to narcissus, leather and tobacco accords.

Carvone-dominant and caraway-like: warm seedy spice with a cool spearmint edge and only a thin trace of the grassy dill-herb greenness. Sharper and more spice-cabinet than dill weed oil, which is green-first; use it where a rye-bread or caraway effect is wanted in herbal and aromatic tops.

Dark cherry flesh and tart fruit skin, with an almond-kernel accent and a cherry-liqueur impression. Restrained sweetness meets a dry woody trace and a faint smoky edge. A compounded heart-note base; the boozy scent does not establish its solvent or composition.
Fresh lime with a slightly pine-lemon, trace-citronella tone; a bright citrus-cologne note distilled from the fruit of Citrus hystrix.
Rich caramel-maple sweetness close to furaneol but deeper, rounder and more cooked-sugar than fruity. A trace material for realistic caramel, maple and roasted-sugar effects in gourmands.

Tuberose, ylang, sweet, fruity, with a dry weedy edge, assessed at 1% in dipropylene glycol; the odour type is floral and the strength is high, which is why evaluation is recommended at 1% or less. The reason to keep it on the shelf is what it does rather than what it is: it is described as a very powerful floral modifier related to ylang that gives diffusion and lift, and it carries the salicylate and cresyl harmony that runs through many white florals, so it slots into a tuberose or ylang accord and pushes it outward without adding weight. Use level is small, up to about half a percent in the concentrate, and it holds around 16 hours on a strip at full strength, so it lifts the heart rather than anchoring the base. It is also sold under the name tuberose acetate. Not recommended for flavour use.

Cedarome's solvent-extracted black-spruce needle and twig absolute from Picea mariana. Dark, sweet-balsamic conifer with a blackcurrant-bud tang over smoke and soft leather; heavier and more tenacious than a distilled needle oil.

The Taif otto: peppery, spicy rose with a honeyed lychee sweetness and a dark, spicy depth built by altitude and desert heat. A reference material rather than a workhorse; a trace is what gives Arabian rose-oud accords their real signature.
Fresh, dry-spicy and terpenic with a warm woody body, peppery bite without the sneeze-inducing pungency of the ground spice. Adds sparkle and masculine energy to citrus, woody and fougere top notes.

Powerful, rustic lemon-citral note with grassy, herbal and slightly earthy-rooty undertones. Used in functional perfumery and to reinforce citrus-herbal accords cheaply; harsher than litsea, so dosed with care in fine fragrance.

Sold as a rich leather base, named as a key component of Guerlain's Habit Rouge. It is a compounded speciality rather than a single aroma chemical, so it delivers a finished leather character in one addition and behaves as a deep, tenacious foundation that a woody or ambery structure can be built on top of. It is a distinct product from Firmenich's Coranol, a linalool-type alcohol building block sold separately in the same range.

IFF's grade of the OTNE woods, cut to a different isomer ratio from Iso E Super and drier for it. Sanded cedar plank rather than fresh sawdust, over a soft amber warmth, with a mineral-musky floor and a thin clean lift on top. Transparent and enormously diffusive without ever being loud, which is why it takes double-digit percentages. Not a drop-in for Iso E Super: same family, different ratio, different smell. Some noses barely register the OTNE woods at all, so bench it on more than one person before judging a dose.
Mild sweet floral-balsamic salicylate with a green, slightly fruity clover nuance. Blender and fixative for florals and sun-tan accords.

Soft, suede-like nuances of fine leather: velvety, warm and subtly animalic, an elegant suede rather than the phenolic bite of birch tar. Odour strength is medium but tenacity is very high, with a blotter life suppliers quote in the hundreds of hours, so it behaves as a long-lasting base note that anchors without shouting. Alcohol-soluble only. In a formula it is the leather bed under woody-leather and ambery-oriental structures, sitting well with labdanum and benzoin, and it smooths a fougere spine of lavender, coumarin and musks without ever turning tarry.

Sharp, honeyed-rosy screwpine flower with an anisic sweetness and a terpenic-green bite, the neat pandanus distillate with no sandalwood carrier under it. Far more penetrating and much less creamy than Kewda attar; a trace lifts rose, hyacinth and opulent florals.
Ultra-potent green pyrazine with galbanum, ivy-leaf and carrot-earth facets, slightly softer and rounder than the isobutyl isomer. Used at ppm level to naturalize green and violet-leaf accords.

Honeyed and balsamic with a cocoa warmth and a dried-fruit sweetness behind it. Slower and rounder than the lighter phenylacetates, it holds the honey idea down into the base where the ethyl and methyl esters have already evaporated.

The Reunion island quality of vetiver: rootier, smokier and more chocolate-earthy than Haitian, with a praline warmth prized in fine fragrance. A distinct product from generic vetiver, not a substitute.

Full coconut character with an oily opening and a sweeter, complex drydown. Supplier reports more than 200 hours on a smelling strip, not exact lifetime. A proprietary base, not gamma-nonalactone itself.

Bedoukian describes a powerful, fresh, watery and ozonic effect combined with fruity shades of raspberry and melon and dewy white petal notes of muguet and tuberose. It is their captive BRI 279-SUS, a hydroxy aldehyde, and it behaves like one: the ozonic lift arrives immediately but the material has real body under it rather than evaporating off the top. In a formula it is the wet-petal join between an aquatic accord and a white floral, giving muguet and tuberose the dew they usually need hydroxycitronellal for, and adding a raspberry-melon roundness that keeps a marine note from reading metallic. The house works it at a substantial level in the concentrate, so it is a structural note here, not a trace effect.

Powerful, characteristic vetiver ketone with a dry, woody-earthy, slightly rooty and green-camphoraceous character; the key natural lead for vetiver odorants. Used in trace to reinforce vetiver notes.
Soft, sweet, woody-floral oil rich in linalool, with a fresh, slightly spicy and rosy character bridging wood and flower. A refined woody-floral note and linalool source.
The softer, sweeter citral isomer: lemon peel without geranial's sharpness.

Molecular-distilled pale patchouli, redistilled away from iron so it carries none of the drum-grade's metallic mustiness: cleaner, sweeter and more transparently woody, with the damp-cellar note lifted off and the patchoulol left standing. The grade fine fragrance actually buys, and the only patchouli pale enough to leave a juice clear.

Floral with honey and marshmallow notes. Robertet places it in the Floralines range, which the house defines as reconstitutions enriched with natural ingredients, and calls it very interesting for both fine fragrance and functional perfumery. The published build includes neroli, neroli Morocco oil, neroli Tunisia oil, styrax absolute, concentrated vanilla extract and Schiff indol hydroxy, so the sweetness is structural rather than decorative: the styrax and vanilla sit under the orange blossom and pull it toward a soft confectionery warmth instead of the bitter green edge a straight neroli oil gives. Use it where a natural neroli would cost too much or vary too far batch to batch.

Givaudan's synthetic answer to the cost and availability crisis on natural grapefruit oil: the brochure claims it gives the same effect as a high quality natural grapefruit oil in every formulation. It reads as a clean hesperidic top, the bitter-sweet zest of grapefruit peel without the weight of an expressed oil. In a formula it is a drop-in replacement for grapefruit oil at the head of a citrus, cologne or fresh floral, carrying the lift and the tart peel character while sidestepping the price and the batch-to-batch drift of the natural.

Grade II ylang: the creamy floral body is still there but the jasmine brightness has faded and a woody-balsamic weight has come forward, with a persistent clove edge. The soap and functional workhorse grade, and a cheap way to carry ylang character down into a base.

Bitter, woody grapefruit-peel sesquiterpene ketone with dry, slightly rhubarb-like facets and remarkable tenacity for a citrus note. Anchors grapefruit accords into the heart and adds natural bitterness to citrus colognes.

dsm-firmenich and Perfumer's Apprentice describe it as an olfactive reproduction of the fragrance of ripe raspberries. Fraterworks expands that to a realistic ripe raspberry, sweet and tart in equal measure, juicy and jammy with a seedy, slightly green freshness, and TGSC files the same raspberry specialty as berry, fruity, jammy and juicy with cotton-candy and tropical facets. In a formula it is a ready-made berry heart rather than a single effect: it carries fruity accords and fruity-floral hearts on its own, turns a chypre toward jam as a modifier, and holds on the blotter far longer than the single raspberry ketones do, so even a trace keeps a berry impression alive under the drydown.
Very soft, sweet floral-muguet diol with a clean, slightly honeyed petal character and almost no top note. Gentle fixative-blender for muguet and rose hearts where a whisper of floralcy is needed.

Firmenich's classic refined methyl-ionone grade: elegant powdery violet and orris with soft woody depth, subtle raspberry-red-berry fruitiness and a fine tea-like nuance. It is a separate supplied grade from Iralia Total despite the shared CAS.

The natural deer-musk enantiomer: powerful, rich and elegant musk with warm animalic depth and a powdery, skin-like drydown. Rounder and creamier than the racemate because the (S) form is nearly odorless, so it reads roughly twice as strong per gram; sold at a premium for deer-musk reconstitutions.

Sweet, honeyed, warm-herbal character with hay and caramel facets, a soft fruity-apricot undertone and a woody warmth, described by the supplier as the smell of a freshly brewed cup of rooibos with honey. Despite the name it is not a tea at all, and it behaves as sweet herbal warmth rather than as a tea note: it carries gourmand, oriental and warm woody bases, sits with vanilla and tonka for richness, with immortelle and honey absolute for a golden heart, or with cedarwood and vetiver for a darker read. A pale straw liquid, so unlike the dark tea resinoids it does not colour a composition.

Perfumer's Apprentice give the odour as fatty, floral, orris root, woody, and state that Irival Oliffac 0612 provides different facets of natural orris absolute: floral, woody, powdery and gourmand. It is a colourless to pale yellow liquid filed in the floral family, used up to a few percent, holding forty or more hours on the blotter, and carries no single CAS, being a mixture. In a formula it is the orris seat that natural orris butter is too costly to fill: a fatty-powdery, rooty floral that lends body and a cosmetic, lipstick-like softness under violets, roses and iris accords, and stretches well because of its tenacity.

Intensely green, cucumber-watery and leafy with a metallic floral-violet undertone and earthy depth; dominated by nonadienal and violet leaf alcohol. Used in small doses for dewy green naturalness in violet, iris, fig and masculine fougere accords.
Mild, sweet balsamic-honey odor with a faint floral-spicy nuance. Used for balsamic depth and honeyed facets.
Herbal, green and fruity. Heart filing is a catalog convention, not measured evaporation or longevity.

The waxy green-brown concrete the Rose de Mai absolute is washed out of: soft honeyed centifolia rose wrapped in floral wax, quieter and slower to open than the absolute. Used neat in solid and anhydrous work, and as a natural fixative that holds a rose heart down for hours longer.
Fresh fruity-rosy ester with citrus and slightly waxy-green facets, softer than geranyl acetate. Used to smooth rose-citrus transitions and add fruity freshness to soaps and colognes.

Waxy and fatty first, then a green tropical pineapple body with a watercress bite and a metallic-soapy edge. The heaviest of the allyl fruit esters: where allyl caproate is pure juicy pineapple, this one smooths and fattens a fruit accord rather than brightening it, and like all allyl esters it needs free allyl alcohol below 0.1%.

Ambergris, dry, woody and old-wood with a clean marine-mineral salinity and a light musk. The most ambergris-forward and least sweet of the ambroxides: softer, rounder and smoother than ambroxan, a smooth ambergris base note.
