It opens waxy-green, deepens into a creamy, narcotic, slightly indolic white floral, and finishes warm and softly powdery, covering the leafy, woody, rooty, indolic and cinnamic facets found across commercial tuberose. Reported at over 480 hours on a smelling strip, it is effective from around 0.1% and is far more versatile than expected: small amounts lift herbal and other floral accords, and it is the backbone of any serious tuberose note.
Mild camphoraceous-terpenic freshness with green pine-needle facets. Support material for camphor, pine and herbal topnotes.
Sweet, honeyed-floral odor with a warm rosy and slightly animalic-cress nuance. Used in trace for honey and floral depth.

dsm-firmenich's concentrated Clearwood, at least 90% patchoulol produced by sugar fermentation. The house describes it as beaming with light, offering the creamy warmth of amber and a dark woody character reminiscent of patchouli, more delicate than standard Clearwood and a good partner for floral bouquets. It sits in the heart and base with high tenacity, so it supplies patchouli's body and depth in a cleaner, more transparent form and at a far smaller dose than the standard article.
Fresh fruity-jasmine ester with green plum and cherry facets. Volatile fruity lift for jasmine and fantasy fruit notes.

Finest saffron extracted into natural triglycerides to give a decolorized, light-yellow oil-based saffron, suited to massage, creams, lotions and cosmetics where the red saffron would discolour the base.

The Good Scents Company gives a sweet, balsamic odour with a tea-like quality and natural connotations, carrying tuberose and chocolate nuances; Perfumer's Apprentice sell it on the shorter reading balsam, fruity, chocolate, ylang, tea and file it as gourmand-balsamic. It is a quiet rounder rather than a statement note, warming white florals from underneath and laying a cocoa and tea shadow beneath fruit. Substantive at 96 hours neat on the blotter, so it works as a low-key fixative; usable up to 15 percent of the concentrate.
Faint sweet balsamic-rosy salicylate crystals with peach and hyacinth undertones. Mild fixative for rose and balsamic bases.
Sweet banana-pear ester, slightly more solvent-like and less candied than the iso isomer. A workhorse fruity lifter in flavors and functional fragrance tops.

Neat it is reminiscent not only of spearmint (Mentha spicata L.), but also of garlic and onion, so the bottle reads far more alliaceous than the name suggests. Dosed into a composition that raw sulfurous edge resolves into the spiciness of wasabi and lends depth, freshness and fruitiness to the top. Symrise works it at around 0.001% of the perfume oil, where it still makes a statement, so it is an accent used in traces rather than a body material. It is a patented captive made from D-limonene upcycled from orange-juice peel waste.
Bright, clean, sweet polycyclic musk with a fresh, slightly camphor-woody sparkle, more radiant in the top than most musks. Good for lifting soapy accords and adding early musk presence.

Brutally fecal barnyard note in anything above extreme dilution, yet at ppm traces it lends creamy warmth to civet bases, jasmine and tropical florals. Handle at 0.1-1% dilution and dose with a toothpick, not a pipette.

Mild, sweet amber-balsamic diterpene alcohol from clary sage with faint tobacco, tea and woody nuances. Low odor impact but valuable as a fixative and natural amber-building block in labdanum and ambergris reconstructions.

Fresh waxy-aldehydic with a smoother, more citrus-floral and less fatty profile than the straight-chain C-11 aldehydes, showing light ambrette and orange nuances. Modern aldehydic sparkle for clean florals and colognes.
Mild green herbal, cool phenolic leafy extract used as a natural antioxidant for essential oils and compounds. At 0.1-1.0% it slows oxidation without affecting the odor.
Warm, spicy-woody rhizome oil with rooty, slightly balsamic and camphoraceous facets used as an aromatic fixative in Indian attars and amber woody accords.

Payan Bertrand's SIMPPAR 2025 innovation, made by co-distilling Sumatran patchouli with osmanthus flower rather than blending the two oils. Trade reports of the launch describe an astonishing woody-animalic note, a chypre leather with fruity suppleness that reads as both primal and terribly chic. The osmanthus apricot fruitiness is carried inside the earthy patchouli instead of sitting on top of it, and it works as a single leather-chypre base where a formula would otherwise need a patchouli, an osmanthus and a leather accord.
Spicy-phenolic clove note with a drier, smokier, slightly medicinal woody character than eugenol. Adds spicy-leathery warmth to masculine woody and carnation bases.
Creamy, sweet vanilla with phenolic and musty facets. Heart filing is a catalog convention, not measured evaporation or longevity.

Delicate freesia-like floral with a fresh citrus lift, a waxy body and a quiet sesquiterpene woodiness. A soft fixative and blender for white-floral, neroli and muguet bases where nerolidol itself reads too woody.
Creamy sweet lactone with a distinct tonka and hay character, warm milk and delicate vanilla-almond facets. A photostable coumarin alternative for fougeres, solar and milky gourmand notes.
Soft floral, green, mildly rosy-woody note. A gentle floralizing alcohol for muguet and rose directions.

Fraterworks Floranol 959281 (FRW-50012), a compounded neroli fantasy base with a fresh orange-blossom character for cologne and floral accords. Not phenoxyethyl isobutyrate and not natural neroli oil. Supplier states 168 hours on a smelling strip; heart placement and strength 5 are editorial working choices. The 10% working dilution is conventional, not factory dilution or a safety limit. Conflicting constituent disclosures require safety review; the product certificate alone does not clear a finished formula.
Fresh, minty-camphoraceous and herbaceous, pennyroyal character. IFRA-restricted; use in traces for lift in mint and herbal accords.

Green, terpenic-resinous absolute of Pistacia lentiscus gum from Chios with peppery, coniferous and slightly aniseed-woody facets. Gives a bright Mediterranean 'lentisque' signature to incense, fig and green-woody compositions.
Fruity, sweet apple-pear odor with a fresh solventy lift. Common commodity ester for fruity and fresh accords.

Givaudan's reading of star jasmine (Trachelospermum jasminoides), which the brochure calls a most elegant spicy-floral odour. Star jasmine is a different flower from jasmine grandiflorum or sambac: heady and sweet but far less indolic, with a distinct spicy edge in place of the animalic depth. The base carries linalool and indole, and Givaudan replaced the isoeugenol with an exclusive molecule of its own. It is offered for use in all floral and chypre compounds. Perfumers who have worked with it note it is cleaner and less smoky than the living flower, so it blends as an elegant floral heart rather than a literal soliflore.

Cyperus scariosus root oil: dry, smoky-leathery wood with earthy vetiver-like, spicy and slightly oud-like facets. Widely used to extend oud, build leather-woody bases and add an Indian earthy-incense signature.
One of the most famous classical bases, the achingly sweet peach accord around aldehyde C-14 used in Mitsouko. Far more than the raw lactone: a complete, rounded vintage peach.

Damascena concrete: rich jammy-honeyed rose held inside a heavy floral wax, warmer and much slower to open than the absolute. A real formulation choice when the rose should arrive late and stay, and the wax fixes the rest of the heart with it.

A vegan beeswax reconstruction carrying sweet honeyed notes. Moellhausen builds the base as the symbol of safeguarding the bees, giving the beeswax character without the animal-derived material, so it stands in for beeswax absolute in a formula where a vegan claim matters. One of the seven finished branded bases in the BoldBases collection, dosed as a single line item. It is a different material from natural beeswax absolute rather than a synonym for it.
Steam-distilled white fraction of camphor tree oil: fresh, cooling, camphoraceous-eucalyptus with coniferous-minty, lavender, pine and nutmeg-spice facets. Cineole-rich.

An economical sandalwood oil reconstitution. It reflects the natural tonality of the oil well, with its powerful volume and its milkiness, and is a complex mixture of patented aroma chemicals containing no sandalwood oil. It gives a natural sandalwood effect in all applications at an exceptional cost/performance ratio, with very good substantivity, and is called out as performing exceptionally well in agarbatti. Distinct from Sandalwood Givco 203: this is the rounder, milkier and cheaper of the two reconstitutions.

Omani hojari frankincense: a bright lemon-pine terpenic opening riding a very high alpha-pinene load, drying to a sweeter, more balsamic incense body than the Somali carterii grade. The quality to reach for when the incense has to read clean and sacred rather than dusty.
Milder cresyl ester with a fruity-phenolic, slightly honeyed animalic character leaning toward narcissus and mimosa. Useful where a gentle stable-warmth is needed without cresol's aggression.
Ultra-powerful violet leaf and galbanum green note with cucumber facets. Used in traces for dewy leafy effects.

Clean aldehydic lily-of-the-valley with a green, lemon-geranium brightness and a waxy-woody drydown. Far more substantive than a citrus aldehyde, so it carries that fresh aldehydic lift right through the heart of muguet and fabric-care florals instead of flashing off the top.

Bedoukian describes a soft, jasmine, white floral aroma with creamy lactonic notes. The Good Scents Company types it creamy and medium strength: mild, creamy fatty coconut with condensed-milk creaminess and fatty nutty nuances at 1%, turning oily, waxy, jasmin, coconut and buttered-cookie at 10%, with substantivity of 168 hours at 100%. In a formula it is the fatness underneath a white floral rather than a note of its own: it rounds jasmine, tuberose and frangipani, gives sandalwood and vetiver a milky skin, and adds naturalness and body to heady floral accords.

The Good Scents Company classes the odour type as thujonic at medium strength and describes it as woody, herbal, cedar leaf, thujone and minty, adding that it is powerful, with camphor, earthy, eucalyptus, wet and minty facets. The molecule is 1-(3,3-dimethylcyclohexyl)ethanone, a ketone that reads like the dry resinous top of cedarleaf oil without the oil's weight or its bitterness. In a formula it is an aromatic and fougere worker: it sharpens lavender and sage, carries a cool camphoraceous lift down into a woody base, and a small dose gives an outdoor, crushed-herb impression that holds through the heart.

An alcoholic infusion of cured Madagascar vanilla pods, made by the traditional maceration of vegetal material in alcohol and traceable to the farm through the house's Path2Farm platform. dsm-firmenich describes it as creamy, leathery and woody, profound, sensual and animalic, sitting on a sweet vanillin, balsamic-woody body. In a formula it is a natural gourmand bottom note that deepens floral and amber compositions. Because it is an infusion rather than an absolute it carries far less odorous material per gram, so it is dosed generously where an absolute would be dosed sparingly, and it should never be substituted one-for-one for vanilla absolute.

A bright, lively apple top note that is not overly sweet, with a clean, fresh aroma, as Perfumer Supply House lists it; ScentScientists sells it at 10 percent in DPG and describes fresh, vivacious apple that stays clean rather than candied. Scentspiracy names it as IFF's fully synthetic green-apple accord contributing crisp, bright freshness, worked at mid single-digit percentages. Buyers note unusual persistence for a top note. In a formula it is a finished apple opening that lifts florals, fresh fougeres and shampoo-clean accords without the sharp vinegary edge single esters bring.

Givaudan describe it as a close reconstitution of civet absolute which it can replace in equal amounts, containing no animal extract at all. Their odour index entry reads animal, warm, musky, civet like. In a formula it adds diffusive warmth and supplies the distinctive effect natural civet gives to floral-jasmin, amber, oriental, chypre and tobacco accords: a trace lends body and a sensual, slightly dirty depth under white florals, while an overdose flattens everything above it. It is worked heavily diluted.

Soft, sweet animalic musk fixative base containing natural oils and absolutes alongside synthetic ingredients. Fraterworks revision 997971D is a modern restoration inspired by historical Fixomusc, not proof of the historical product's identity.
Rooty, woody-spicy oil of spiked ginger lily with camphoraceous, cineolic and slightly sweet balsamic nuances. Aromatic base-heart note used in Indian attars and incense accords.
Peppery-woody note with dry spicy warmth reminiscent of black pepper over cedar. Adds bite to masculine woody compositions.
Deep herbaceous-sweet with hay, tobacco and fruity undertones and the characteristic blue chamazulene color. Adds warm herbal-hay depth to tea, tobacco and herbal-amber accords.
Lemony-rosy citronellal freshness with a balsamic eucalyptus undertone, smoother than citronella. Natural citronellal source; brightens rose and lifts herbal colognes.

Refined, dry, powdery ketonic musk very close to the odor core of natural musk but cleaner and less animalic. Expensive nitro-free classic used in fine fragrance for a true 'musk deer' character without the funk.

Almost odorless with a faint sweet-balsamic, slightly almond nuance; a natural constituent of balsams widely used as a solvent/diluent for absolutes, resinoids and crystalline materials. Has fixative value in balsamic bases; IFRA-restricted and a labeled allergen.

Soft floral-fruity ester, sweet rose carrying peach and apricot with an apple nuance at dilution. Adds naturalness and a fruit-flesh roundness to synthetic rose hearts that read too thin on PEA alone.
Clean, sweet, slightly fruity-pear macrocyclic oxa-lactone musk with a soft powdery drydown; smooth and rounded rather than animalic. A cost-effective musk for functional and fine fragrance alike.

Corn-chip and popcorn character with toasted bread crust, taco-shell and a sweet caramelized roasted background. One of the strongest roasted notes identified in bread aroma and a far more stable route to the acetylpyrroline effect: use at trace in bakery, popcorn and cereal gourmands where 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline would degrade.
Faint, dry, woody-terpenic hydrocarbon accompanying alpha-cedrene in cedarwood oils; weak but naturalizing. Used as a woody diluent and cedar reconstruction component.
Intensely creamy vanilla with a clean, non-smoky profile and huge substantivity. A modern vanillin booster that survives soap bases and lasts for days.

Sweet, warm vanilla-balsamic resinoid from Styrax tonkinensis with almond, powdery and slightly cinnamic facets; smoother and more refined than Sumatra benzoin. Indispensable rounding agent and fixative in amber, balsamic and gourmand bases.

The supplier lists it as a waxy jasmine with creamy-celery freshness, and expands that to a sweet floral-jasmine aroma with warm herbaceous facets, soft woody undertones, fresh celery-green nuances and a diffusive waxy quality. The celery-green edge is what separates it in use from a plain jasmone: it keeps a floral bouquet from going syrupy and adds a natural, slightly vegetal jasmine presence. Worked at 0.1% to 1% with about 0.4% typical in a compound, it is a heart note holding roughly 32 hours on a smelling strip and stretching to a few days at working concentration.
Sweet, floral-balsamic ketone with jasmine-cherry and slightly almond facets; a natural component of night-blooming flowers. Softens white-floral hearts and blends florals into gourmand bases.
Sweet, fruity-caramellic and rummy note with a green plum facet; used in fruity, rum and brown accords.

Sweet fruity ester of apple and pineapple over a herbal, faintly musty-powdery background. Used in heavy blossom and amber bases where it blends with opopanax, and as a fruity rounder in rose and fougere accords.

Fraterworks' finished apple accord: a crisp green apple opening from prenyl and tert-butylcyclohexyl acetates that settles into a soft, creamy lactonic base of gamma-undecalactone, Applelide musk and a hydrogenated rosinate fixative, which is why a top-note modifier lasts past 24 hours on a strip. Fraterworks rates it strength 4 and impact 6 out of 10 and calls it deceptively powerful through a trace of rose ketones. Positioned as a modifier for top notes when a more complete apple note is needed: a few percent lifts a fruity floral or a fresh fougere, and it can carry the whole apple opening on its own. IFRA 51 certificate: not limited in category 4, 23% in category 2, 45% in category 8, not approved in categories 1 and 6, driven by 2% hexyl cinnamal (a declarable allergen), 0.05% of a dimethylcyclohexene aldehyde and 0.01% rose ketones.

Elegant orris-violet with a powdery, slightly woody and waxy character, cleaner and finer than the straight ionones. Workhorse of iris and violet bases and a diffusive floralizer used generously in fine fragrance and soap.

Rounder and less aggressive than the steam-distilled bud oil, keeping the fruity-sweet eugenyl acetate top that distillation strips away. The choice when clove has to sit in a fine fragrance rather than shout in it; excellent in carnation, gourmand bakery and warm amber accords.
Moist, freshly sawn wood with powdery incense dryness and refined amber warmth recalling good frankincense. A superb blender bridging transparent woods and heavy amber bases.

Perfumer's Apprentice gives the odour as balsamic, cinnamic, honey, amber, and the product as a long-lasting blend of cinnamic and vanilla notes with honey and amber, sweet and smoky, which can also be described as powdery, woody and resinous. It is filed in the balsamic family and carries no single CAS, being a mixture. In a formula it is the warm sticky floor of an oriental: it sweetens and rounds ambers, tobacco and vanilla accords and holds them down, giving the cinnamic-balsamic character of Peru balsam in a compounded blend that is easier to weigh and pour than the crude resin.

Fuller and warmer than the distilled oil, with the dry resinous bite and heavy sesquiterpene body that steam distillation leaves in the still. Gives pepper a heart rather than a flash; the standard indie companion to the essential oil in woody, leather and masculine spice accords.

Bitter narcissus floralcy, sweet and slightly naphthalic, closing woody; on dilution the maraschino-cherry and almond character of the parent aldehyde reads through. The standard almond note for soap and detergent, where plain benzaldehyde oxidises to benzoic acid and dies.
Dry woody-resinous, smoky-ambery absolute of cypress, deeper and sweeter than the essential oil. Natural woody depth for chypre and amber accords.
Carnation-brand liquid paraffin. Virtually odorless, stable base/carrier oil with a light baby-oil feel; poor solvency for powders, crystals, resins and terpenes.
Fresh green banana-pear over cut grass, sweeter and fruitier than the parent alcohol. Excellent green lift for fruity, floral and fougere topnotes where cis-3-hexenol alone would be too raw.

Moellhausen describes this base as fresh and juicy, part of the third BoldBases series built on simple everyday experiences. It is a building block with a narrow olfactory profile of fewer than eight elementary components, sold on high intensity and persistency. In a formula it supplies a whole apple effect from one bottle, the crisp fresh lift and the juicy body together, which is the part that is hard to reach by stacking single fruity esters.
Earthy, woody-spicy rhizome oil with camphoraceous and rooty facets, akin to a drier, more medicinal turmeric. Grounding note for woody, amber and incense accords.

Waxy floral-rosy aldehyde with citrus-orange and cucumber-melon nuances; the most floral of the fatty aldehyde series. Gives waxy rose-petal realism and aldehydic lift to rose and classic floral bouquets.
Extremely powerful, radiant and long-lasting sandalwood with a creamy, rosy-metallic sparkle and exceptional substantivity. Effective at trace levels as a diffusive sandalwood-woody signature.
Sweet, fruity honey note with rosy-winey and slightly cocoa facets, smoother and rounder than the methyl ester. A versatile honey-sweetener for florals, tobacco and gourmand compositions.

Harsh green-fatty aldehyde with a penetrating oily, slightly fruity-herbaceous character reminiscent of clary sage's aldehydic facet. Used in strict traces for green-aldehydic lift in florals and fougeres.

Moroccan geranium: a rosy, green-leafy geranium over a sweet, slightly earthy-herbal base, with a minty lift from its menthones. Softer and less sharply minty than Bourbon, close to Egyptian but a touch greener and less rosy-sweet.

High-purity (95-96%) denatured ethanol, the standard carrier of fine fragrance: flashes off quickly and cleanly to present the perfume without odor of its own. Quality matters, use fragrance-grade denaturants (e.g., IPA or Bitrex types) since harsh denaturants taint top notes.
Fresh creamy white floral oil with citrus-green sparkle and fruity nuance. Natural bridge between citrus tops and white floral hearts.

Wild Madagascan vine pepper: a bright limonene-sabinene lift over a warm peppery body, with a floral-woody sweetness and a resinous forest edge that Piper nigrum has none of. The peppercorn to use when a spice top has to stay elegant rather than sharp.
Smooth creamy-fruity lactone with peach, coconut and dairy facets, subtle and persistent. Used to extend creamy fruit themes into the base without shouting.
Light, fresh muguet-lavender alcohol with a clean, slightly camphoraceous-fruity freshness that evaporates quickly. Useful crisp top-note floralizer for muguet, freesia and cologne styles.

Described at source as delicate, orange blossom, powerful and long-lasting, and explicitly more woody-neroli than the absolute. It is a low-temperature extraction of the flower onto natural nerolidol, so the natural solvent itself contributes a soft woody-floral tail the absolute does not have. In a formula it gives a genuine, unsharpened orange blossom heart with far better hold than orange flower absolute, and because it arrives already on a nerolidol carrier it is dosed as a ready-diluted speciality rather than weighed like a neat absolute.

Soft, slightly honeyed fresh rose-petal note with a green hyacinth nuance and mild yeasty-wine undertone; the volumetric backbone of rose absolute. Cheap, stable and used at high percentages to give petally body to almost any floral.

Hot buttered popcorn, fresh bread crust and the warm cereal sweetness of basmati rice and pandan leaf. Threshold near 0.02 ppb, among the lowest of any known odorant, and nothing else reproduces this note; unstable neat, so it is supplied only as a dilute solution and dosed in traces.
Powerful, rich creamy-woody sandalwood note reminiscent of Mysore album, dry yet warm and long-lasting. Used in soap and fine fragrance for a full sandalwood body.
Cedarwood and ambergris, dry, woody and soft; a smooth cedar-amber bridge.
Warm, dry woody-amber with cedarwood character; a substantive IFF blender with marked synergistic effect in woody complexes. Supports most florals and rounds amber accords without sweetness.
Pungent, green-malty aldehydic odor with a fresh cereal nuance. Ultra-trace for malty, green and fresh-lift effects.
Light, very volatile ester with a fresh, slightly harsh fruity-rum character: strawberry and apple over an ethereal, boozy sweetness. Gone from the strip in about four hours. Methyl propanoate.

Nez reports that juniper berry, which as a steam-distilled oil is usually very terpenic and reads piney and camphoraceous, unveils fresh, punchy, fruity notes when taken through Mane's supercritical Jungle Essence extraction. The work is done at low temperature so the odorous molecules are not denatured, which gives a more complex, multifaceted extract than other methods and lets the crushed berry come through instead of the needle. In a formula it is a top-note lift with the gin-berry signature intact but without the resinous pine drag of the essential oil, so it can be dosed more freely against citrus or a green heart than the distillate can.
Diffusive sweet fruity ester of pear, banana and apricot character. Juicy fruity top for fantasy and tropical accords.
Woody, fresh and sugary Canadian Pinus banksiana needle/twig essential oil, obtained by steam distillation.
Faint, sweet-balsamic salicylate with a mild creamy floral facet; classic fixative and UV filter (Salol) used for tenacity.

Givaudan's lemon speciality, listed in the Givco range as fresh lemony yet still powerful. It is an imitation of the natural lemon odour built for stability and substantivity in finished products, which is the whole point of reaching for it: cold-pressed lemon oil is bright but fugitive and prone to going off in base, while this keeps the peel character intact through the top and into the early heart. Use it where a formula needs lemon to still read as lemon after the first ten minutes, or as a stable lemon spine under a cologne or a fresh fougere.

Hot, dry phenolic herb: a carvacrol bite close to oregano but drier and more resinous-woody, with a peppery medicinal edge and no sweetness. Traces give fougeres and aromatic tops rustic Mediterranean scrub; its carvacrol and thymol load caps it hard in use.

Sweet spicy clove and carnation over a phenolic, peppery, smoky-woody body with a powdery dry-out. The defining phenolic of wheat beer, roasted coffee and clove; very high impact, so it works in ppm traces and slots between guaiacol and eugenol in the guaiacol series.

Intense celery-maggi note, warm, soupy-green and slightly musky-caramelized, dominated by phthalides. Ultra-trace doses give gourmand-herbal depth and a natural 'bouillon' warmth to chypres and immortelle accords.

Nutty roasted hazelnut and musty corn with a raw-potato earthiness and a bready trail. Known in the trade as filbert pyrazine, it is a staple trace note in gourmand and coffee accords, supplying the nut-skin bitterness that plain acetylpyrazine lacks.
Powerful roasted, meaty-nutty and earthy pyrazine; trace note for roasted, potato and savory-gourmand effects.

Near-odorless coupling solvent (Transcutol/Carbitol type) that bridges fragrance oils into aqueous and surfactant systems; also used in some skin products for its solubilizing power. Choose cosmetic grade for leave-on applications.

Soft sweet violet alcohol with a fruity-berry lift and only a whisper of the ionone woodiness, the reduced form of alpha-ionone. Reach for it where ionone reads too dry or too orris, and for fresh violet, raspberry and tea nuances that need no woody tail.
Sharper, drier and smokier than clove bud, nearly pure eugenol with a phenolic bite. The workhorse spicy-carnation note and a budget eugenol source for leather and amber bases.
Warm, spicy-phenolic leaf oil with clove-like eugenol/chavibetol facets over a green, peppery herbaceous body. Adds exotic spicy-green depth to amber and leather accords.

The commercial isomer of ambrettolide (oxacycloheptadec-10-en-2-one): sweet, smooth, musky-floral with a soft waxy warmth, nearly indistinguishable from natural-identical ambrettolide in use. Widely sold under the Ambrettolide name by IFF.

Symrise gives the odour as earthy, mossy, camphorous, patchouli and beetroot. It resembles the humid-earthy aspects of patchouli and fresh vetiver roots, and carries the earthy part of green ground-growing moss, so it supplies damp soil without the dusty grey of an oakmoss substitute. In a formula it reinforces a pleasant dark fruitiness and makes a composition fuller, richer and more radiant. The house recommends 0.1 to 3 percent; it is supplied as a pale white to white solid.

Steam-distilled immortelle: a curry-like diketone heart on dry hay and honey, lifted by a fruity-rosy neryl acetate freshness the absolute does not have. Far greener and more aromatic than immortelle absolute, so treat them as separate materials and dose in trace before the curry facet takes over the formula.

Distilled from bitter-orange leaves and twigs: fresh, green-woody, bittersweet floral-citrus dominated by linalyl acetate and linalool, like neroli's leafier, more masculine sibling. Workhorse of eaux de cologne and an inexpensive way to extend orange-blossom notes.

Givaudan writes that it surprises with its natural, fresh, cassis, sage flower character, and lists the facets as fruity, blackcurrant, grapefruit and green. It is sold only as the oxime at 10% in isopropyl myristate / triethyl citrate, so the bottle on the bench is already a tenth-strength solution and is still worked at traces. In a formula it is a modifier rather than a theme: it drops a fresh fruity or green cassis edge into citrus, modern lily of the valley and lavender accords. The house notes it stays linear, gives about a week of life on the blotter, is strongly substantive on both damp and dry fabric, and is stable in soap and detergent.

Advanced Biotech list it as a clear yellow liquid with lemon and orange like flavours, sold as a natural flavouring and citrus enhancer rather than as a single aroma chemical; supplier listings add that it is only partly soluble in water and soluble in most organic solvents. The house's own dual CAS shows what it actually is, acetaldehyde carried in orange oil, so what you smell is the pungent, ethereal, green-fruity flash of acetaldehyde sitting on sweet orange peel. In a formula it is a top-note booster rather than a citrus note in its own right: a trace at the head makes the fruit read as freshly cut instead of distilled, then the acetaldehyde flashes off within minutes and leaves the orange behind. Dose it in traces, because overdosed it turns sharp and solventy and takes the whole top with it.
Drier, sharper and more resinous than Mysore album, with a nutty-woody, slightly bitter-green top and a soft creamy base. A sustainable natural sandalwood source for woody and amber accords.

The Good Scents Company carries Dimyrcetol as an IFF trade name and describes it as citrus type at medium strength: fresh, lime, cologne, herbal, air and marine, adding that it delivers a fresh citrus of great power with an excellent performance-to-cost ratio. Ventos lists it under two registry numbers, 18479-58-8 and 25279-09-8, that is as dihydromyrcenol carrying a dihydromyrcenyl formate component, and that second component is where the ozonic-marine and faintly woody edge over plain dihydromyrcenol comes from. Blotter life is under three hours, so it works as a top-note freshener: it opens colognes and fougeres with a clean lime-and-air lift and supplies shower-gel brightness cheaply.
Powerful sweet fruity-pineapple note with a green apple body; a diffusive workhorse for fruity accords.

Warm, pungent and fatty-spicy with the biting rhizome character of fresh-grated ginger and only a muted lemony lift. The gingerols carried through by CO2 extraction give a pungent, tenacious body the steam-distilled oil lacks, so it holds ginger warmth into the heart of woody-ambers and gourmand accords instead of flashing off on top.

Mild, sweet floral-green benzoate with a balsamic, lightly fruity body and a soft musky, amber-like dry-down. A quiet floraliser and blender for honeysuckle, sweet pea and other fantasy florals that tolerates high doses. n-Pentyl benzoate; commercial grades may include 2-methylbutyl benzoate.

Fresh green-herbal acetate with a clear lavender lift and a soft mushroom-earthy base, oilier and rounder than 1-octen-3-ol. Greens lavender, geranium and fougere accords without the raw fungal bite of the parent alcohol.

dsm-firmenich file it as a speciality base reminiscent of dried fruit, fruity with plum notes, a well balanced association of ingredients some of which are captives. Suppliers expand that to the rich sweetness of raisins, sultanas, apricots and prunes, with the astringency of fruit skin and a wine-like fermented edge over a creamy lactonic body, and Fraterworks measures it at 48 hours on a smelling strip. It is a body-and-elegance material rather than a headline: in traces it puts a mysterious depth under a rose or a woody accord, at a few percent it reads as an unmistakable dried-fruit signature that warms fruity-florals and orientals, and the house singles out its effect beside a cassis base in a tropical-fruit context.

A de Laire red-currant base relaunched by Symrise, described as capturing the soul of succulent red berries: the historic Groseille fruity-chic base rediscovered and infused into a frosted sorbet, unfurling a mouth-watering fruity note built on a remarkably powerful captive. It blends fruitiness with a touch of effervescence. In a formula it acts as a scent enhancer as much as a berry note, elevating the red fruity dimension of berries and pulling out the tart facet of rhubarb, which makes it useful in fruity, vibrant and lightly gourmand compositions.

The terpene fraction drawn off when lemon oil is rectified: thin, bright lemon-peel citrus with almost none of the oil's citral body or roundness. A cheap volume-builder and top-note extender for citrus accords; it oxidises fast, so buy small and keep it cold.

Sweet balsam with a sharp, gassy styrene top, then floral-spicy, cinnamon-like and faintly bitter-almond facets over a woody-balsamic base. Turkish oil is styrene-led; Honduran oil is softer and rich in caryophyllene.

Dry violet-orris over a pronounced woody backbone, drier and less fruity than alpha-ionone and the least common of the three isomers. Completes the ionone set for violet and orris work where a powdery, wood-leaning effect is wanted rather than a raspberry one.
Sweet, caramellic-spicy aldehyde with roasted almond, maple and warm brown facets, richer than furfural. Supports coffee, caramel and roasted-nut effects in gourmand accords.
Oily, bland fixed oil with a slight fatty, almost rancid note; used as an emollient and carrier in massage bases and cosmetics (best paired with an antioxidant).

Symrise gives the odour as fruity, grapefruit, rhubarb, vetiver and green pepper. It is the ester counterpart to Vetikon and smells tart and stalky rather than sweet. In a formula it underlines the green-woody elements of vetiver, makes spicy and green compositions livelier and more intense, and imparts the bitterness of grapefruit, which is what stops a citrus top from turning candied. The house recommends 0.1 to 10 percent.
Warm, sweet herbaceous-tobacco lactone with a faint coumarinic body; used in tobacco, coumarin and soft gourmand accords.
Sweet, juicy citrus peel oil close to grapefruit but softer and sweeter. Natural sparkle for modern citrus colognes.

Oily, tea-like jasmine note with herbaceous, slightly mushroomy-lavender and green facets; smooth and natural-smelling. A discreet floralizer that knits jasmine accords together and extends absolutes economically.
Warm, sweet-spicy allspice blending clove, cinnamon and nutmeg facets with a fresh peppery top. A rich all-round spice note for ambers, mulled-wine gourmands and masculine blends; eugenol-rich.

Fuller and creamier than the distilled seed oil, the eucalyptus-cineole spike tamed into a rounder sweet-balsamic spice body. Gives cardamom real presence in gourmand chai, coffee and amber accords without the medicinal bite; a very common indie SKU alongside the oil.
Dense burnt labdanum with amber, leather, tobacco and smouldering incense. A pyrogenic Cistus ladaniferus extract for dark resinous, incense and leather bases.

Intensely warm, animalic-spicy and sweat-like with a green, earthy curry facet; unmistakable and polarizing. In traces it adds sensual human warmth to ambers, leathers and spicy florals; IFRA-restricted (phototoxicity).
Intense tangy rhubarb with a green, lightly eucalyptus-tinged heart. Excellent in fruity and citrus accords; very stable across functional bases and effective in small doses.

A delicate muguet powdery floral with hints of heliotrope and strong stability, offered by dsm-firmenich as a captive in the Sharing Innovation collection. Perfumer & Flavorist describes the aromatic allylic alcohol, introduced in 2014, as nicely floral with lilac and mimosa aspects and an anisic side, comparable to Florol but with more powdery, cosmetic facets that give it additional complexity and velvetiness. In a formula it is a soft muguet and rose modifier: it rounds a lily accord, powders a rose, and holds its shape where lighter muguet alcohols thin out. It is also the building block dsm-firmenich uses inside its own Heliotropin Base.
Harsh phenolic oregano-tar note, medicinal and smoky. Micro-doses add gutsy Mediterranean herb character and leathery warmth to aromatic masculines.
Creamy, soft woody sandalwood oil from the Hawaiian species, warmer and slightly drier than East Indian album, with a smooth milky-woody drydown. Sustainable premium sandalwood grade.

Fresh mentholic ketone reminiscent of dried mint leaf with woody blackcurrant undertones, avoiding the toothpaste effect of common mints. Adds clean fougere coolness; pairs well with lavender and dihydromyrcenol.

Givaudan describes a powerful and fresh citrus bergamot top note combined with a floral, herbaceous heart, and singles it out as excelling at citrus lime effects. It is 2-methyl-6-methylene-7-octen-2-yl acetate, and unlike the natural bergamot it stands in for it survives alkaline media, holding up from pH 2 to 10.5 and performing best in soap, shampoo, all-purpose cleaner and fabric detergent. In a formula it is the citrus you reach for when the top has to still be there hours later: several days on the blotter, used up to 10 percent, giving bergamot and lime brightness that does not collapse the way a cold-pressed oil does.

Heavy, earthy-woody oil with a musty, animalic, spicy-rooty and slightly valerian-like character. A deep, unusual base note for amber and incense accords. Amphora Aromatics' Indian spikenard carries an IFRA 51 certificate with no limit in category 4 (40% in a deodorant, 80% in intimate products, not approved for lips or mouth), the one material with a standard being cedrene at 0.2%; the allergen declaration lists pinene 10%, limonene 0.2%, terpineol 0.2%, linalool 0.06%, terpinolene 0.04% and alpha-terpinene 0.03%. Avena Lab's sheet classifies the oil as a mild skin and eye irritant and a skin sensitiser (H316, H320, H317).
Soft, rosy-honey base note combining rose-petal smoothness with honeyed, slightly balsamic depth. A long-lasting fixative sweetener for rose, honey and opulent floral bases.
Soft, waxy jasmine aldehyde, cleaner and more chamomile-fruity than the amyl homologue, with excellent substantivity. Workhorse jasmine-gardenia base note across fine and functional perfumery.
Fresh, penetrating eucalyptus-like cineole with a sweeter, slightly fruity-floral edge than eucalyptus itself. Useful for medicinal freshness in herbal fougeres and functional fragrance.

Soft, green-floral salicylate with azalea, blond-tobacco and faintly musky-skin facets; smoother and longer than amyl salicylate. Ubiquitous solar-floral diffuser in modern white florals and fougeres.
Fresh melon-rind alcohol, green and watery. Key note for realistic melon and cucumber effects in aquatic florals.

An IFF sandalwood base the supplier presents as a sensory journey through the woods, with a wet earth character, peppery freshness and a soft creamy sandalwood note. Its listed facets are camphorous, earthy, herbal, orangeflower, patchouli, sandalwood, turmeric and woody, so it reads far drier and rootier than a classic creamy sandalwood base: damp forest floor and peppery turmeric first, the milky wood sitting behind them. In a formula it is the sandalwood base to reach for when the accord needs earth and grip rather than sweetness, and it sits naturally alongside patchouli, vetiver and oud.

The waxy hydrocarbon-extracted stage before the absolute: the full narcotic indolic jasmine, muted and rounded by the floral wax carrying it, with little of the absolute's fruity lift. Used neat in solid perfumes and balms, and as the starting stock for perfumers who wash their own absolute.

The Good Scents Company gives the odour type as woody at medium strength and describes it as soft herbaceous pine with spicy hints of ginger and Indian cardamom, followed by smooth natural woods; supplier listings add spicy-woody, fresh and effervescent with a fir facet. It is a methyl methylene tricyclodecanol, an adamantane-type alcohol, and it is a white solid, so it is normally bought or made up in solution before use. In a formula it bridges spice and wood: it sets a fizzy ginger-cardamom lift on top of a woody base and brings clean coniferous freshness to fougere and masculine accords without the medicinal bite of camphor.

Deep, dry amber-woody with velvety musky, softly spicy-powdery undertones; a modern IFF ex-captive with outstanding fixation and sillage. Bridges woody-amber accords from opulent to fresh-aromatic; effective in traces.

Extraordinarily potent fruity-floral ketone of stewed apple, dried rose, honey and blackcurrant, the smell of great Burgundy and rose otto in one molecule. Used at fractions of a percent to give lift, fruit and glow to almost anything; strictly IFRA-limited.
Radiant dried-fruit note of raisins, prunes and cooked apple over a rosy-damascone glow, highly substantive. Used in traces to give luxurious dried-fruit richness to roses, ambers and gourmands.
Intense ambery, powerful tonka bean base developing powdery, sweet tobacco and almond notes with a long-lasting natural coumarin aspect. Blends well in fougere and floral accords.
Soft, sweet, smoky-woody ester derived from guaiacwood, smoother and drier than the parent oil. A gentle woody fixative and rose-woody blender.
Celebrated rose base in the damascena direction: honeyed deep rose with spicy-geranium and fruity facets, ready to wear as the entire rose heart of a composition.

A powerful fruity green oxime (Symrise) built around blackcurrant bud, cassis and buchu leaf with a sulfurous cat-pee edge that reads as juicy realism in trace amounts. Extremely diffusive, so it is dosed in fractions of a percent to lift fruity, green chypre and floral-amber accords with a bright cassis flash.

Grade I ylang, the fraction taken straight after Extra: still sweet and jasmine-creamy but a shade heavier, with a clearer p-cresyl methyl ether lift and a banana-clove body. The value grade for white-floral hearts where the Extra fraction's finesse is not needed.

Brutally skunky sulfur thiol with a hop-resin and cat-spray character, detectable at parts per trillion. The trace that makes beer, hops and cannabis accords read as real; flashes off fast, so it colours the opening only.
Rich herbaceous-honeyed oil from New Zealand tea tree with woody, slightly medicinal and balsamic depth. Natural complexity for herbal-woody accords.
Soft, sweet, creamy-milky sandalwood with balsamic warmth and a nutty, cashew-like tone; some lots open with a brief pine-citrus lift. Diffusive and very long-lasting.
Toasted popcorn, roasted nut and fresh-baked bread character with a sweet corn-chip nuance. A key praline and roasted-hazelnut builder used at trace levels in nutty gourmands.

Robertet publishes the olfactive description as "Floral, orange flower, marine" and files it under the Floral family. The Good Scents Company, listing the same substance as anisyl propanal / methyl anthranilate Schiff's base, gives "sweet anise hawthorn green floral cortex mimosa absolute spicy powdery" at medium odour strength and a blotter life of 316-400 hours at full concentration. In a formula it behaves the way the Schiff class does: almost no volatility of its own, so it holds an orange-blossom and mimosa-hawthorn floral in place across the whole drydown while a soft marine-green lift sits over the top and a powdery anisic tail closes it. Use it to slow, round and fix neroli and white-floral accords rather than to brighten them; it is a fixative that happens to smell floral, not a top note.

The waxy pre-absolute of Tasmanian brown boronia and the commoner trade form: the same beta-ionone-rich violet, freesia and hay-fruity character as the absolute, carried in a heavy floral wax that softens the top and lengthens the tail. Precious and trace-level; the wax makes it convenient in solids and pomades where the absolute would need a solvent.

Givaudan describes it as a green note with aspects of freshly peeled carrots and the dry, earthy qualities of galbanum. In a formula it is the material that builds a green galbanum heart without the harsh sulphury bite of the resinoid itself, and the carrot facet gives it a rooty, slightly waxy lift that reads as natural rather than synthetic. The house uses it up to 3% in detergents to carry that green galbanum heart, and at around 1% of a 10% dilution in toiletries and fine fragrance to support earthy and herbaceous accords. It holds about a day on a blotter, so it works as a top-to-heart green rather than a fixative.

Ripe pear and apple ester with a green stalk edge and a fatty-waxy body; pushed too far it turns musty and overripe. Sits between hexyl acetate and hexyl butyrate, adding juicy ripeness to pear and apple accords when kept restrained.
Rich, dry, sweet-woody Australian oil with sandalwood-like creaminess, a smoky-leathery depth and slight tobacco facet. A characterful natural woody base.
Sharp green, fatty, leafy note with cucumber and nutty facets. Used in trace amounts for natural green and fatty effects.

Nez reports Opalene as an IFF captive whose role in Caroline Dumur's Speed Smelling 2022 composition is to propel its citrus notes, inside a clean-laundry accord built with polygonum essence and pink pepper CO2 extract. The published character is citrus: a radiant, projecting top-note material used to carry and extend citrus rather than to read as a note by itself. IFF has published no chemical identity, CAS or technical data for it, so nothing beyond that citrus character is documented.

Sharp, sweet bitter-almond and maraschino cherry note, the defining aroma of almond extract and amaretto. Essential for cherry, almond, marzipan and heliotrope accords; volatile and prone to oxidation to benzoic acid.
Extremely powerful sulfurous material that becomes roasted coffee and savory-brown at high dilution. A trace tool for coffee, roasted and cooked gourmand effects.
Green, herbaceous-fruity odor with a lavender and bergamot nuance. Used in fougere, lavender and pine accords.

Symrise describe it as a spicy and pungent bouquet combining at once freshness and potency. The base is built around an incisive black pepper together with the Belanis captive, whose aniseed notes deliver the anise effect without relying on anethole, and reviewers report that it brings a burst of adrenaline and a biting freshness to a creation. In a formula it is a sharp spicy accent rather than a warm one: it cuts through and animates an opening or a fougere heart where ground pepper alone would read flat and dusty.
Fresh, floral-lime odor with a linalool-like sweetness and a soft rosy-woody nuance. Used in fresh floral and cologne accords.

Pungent, green-fruity cassis with sulfurous, catty, minty and woody facets, tart and jammy at once. The reference natural for cassis accords; used at low levels in chypres, fruity florals and modern colognes.

Fresh, clean muguet with watery cyclamen facets. It is a muguet speciality base, so it supplies a whole lily-of-the-valley heart in one line rather than being assembled from single molecules, and the watery cyclamen side keeps it transparent and modern, which makes it useful for lifting a floral heart without adding the waxy heaviness older muguet accords carry.
Fresh, balsamic and woody with a bright terpenic, coniferous pine character and a warm-balsamic, faintly citrus top. Distilled from pine oleoresin.
Deep, creamy peach-butter lactone with musky, slightly woody warmth and excellent tenacity. Adds long-lasting lactonic cream to tuberose, gardenia and skin-scent bases.

A floralised frankincense base combining Omani Boswellia sacra resin and essential-oil character with natural oils, absolutes and aroma chemicals. Supplies incense character throughout fragrance development.

Tahitian-vanilla-inspired gourmand base combining vanilla extracts with synthetic ingredients. Fraterworks revision 319883A; a formulated accord, not vanilla absolute, pure vanillin or Vanilla Supreme.
Powdery vanillic aroma chemical with sweet, flowery heliotrope-like nuances.
Camphoraceous, cooling woody-weedy note with fruity berry facets (grape, raspberry, cordial) and a minty edge. Used for woody-fruity tobacco and berry effects.

Smoky, phenolic, charred-wood tar note that is the historical soul of 'cuir de Russie' - burning campfire, smoked leather and creosote with a sweet balsamic underlay. Only rectified qualities are usable and IFRA-restricted; traces suffice for potent leather-smoke effects.

Floral and jasmine, with a slight cis-jasmone note; the floral character is reminiscent of magnolia and tea, with slightly fruity undertones, and a subtle fruity peach aspect is also reported. Odour type is floral and the strength is medium, which is why it is recommended for evaluation at a 10% solution or less rather than neat. It behaves as a building block rather than a signature: it enriches the white floral families and holds up well in fruit-led compositions, and it is specifically useful for building magnolia and jasmine accords where the cis-jasmone facet reads as the living flower rather than the absolute. Stability is described as excellent, and it lasts about 48 hours on a strip at full strength, so it sits squarely in the heart. Note it is the alcohol, not the ketone: do not confuse it with Delphone, 2-pentylcyclopentanone, which is a different material.

Soft, warm amber-woody lactone with tobacco and coumarinic facets; odor is subtle but it rounds, fixes and 'ambers' a base remarkably well. Derived from sclareol and a key precursor to ambroxide; useful powdery-amber background material.
An aldehydic aroma chemical with a fresh, green, herbal lavender character; lends a clean camphoraceous-lavender lift to fougere and herbal accords.

Warm spicy-aromatic bark oil from Croton eluteria with nutmeg, black pepper, myrtle and woody-balsamic incense facets. Interesting naturalizer for spicy-tobacco, incense and chypre compositions; historically used to flavor tobacco.
Sweet anisic-spicy note, softer and rounder than anethole with a mild fennel-licorice warmth. Anise-type modifier.

Steam-distilled from greater galangal root or rhizome (Alpinia galanga). Suppliers describe a fresh herbal-floral, slightly myrtle-like spicy and woody odor with Thai-curry and ginger facets. Published analyses report 1,8-cineole and alpha-fenchyl acetate among prominent constituents, with proportions varying by plant part and origin. Do not confuse with lesser galangal (Alpinia officinarum).

Richer, deeper solvent-extracted counterpart of the essential oil: winey, cognac-like musk with waxy, tobacco-tinged warmth and remarkable tenacity. Used in traces to lend natural muskiness and vintage depth to fine fragrance.

Perfumer's Apprentice, who sell it as Rosessence (Firmenich), give the odour as rose, Bulgarian, and describe the material as a synthetic and very complex reconstitution of Bulgarian rose oil, probably the closest specialty to natural Bulgarian rose essential oil. What it does in a formula follows from that: it is a drop-in rose heart, built to stand where rose otto would stand, so the rose can be carried at a workable cost and at a consistency a natural distillation cannot hold from crop to crop. Note that the name collides with Robertet's Rosessence 80, which is a different base from a different house; this is the Firmenich rose otto reconstitution, not the Robertet peppered rose-oil alternative.

Fresh, rosy-green floral with a delicate rose petal character, a metallic oxide-like sparkle, hints of exotic yellow fruits and a subtle anisic undertone. The supplier frames it against Rosa centifolia, the hundred-petalled rose of Grasse, with the dewy petal reading joined to a modern lifted brightness. In a formula it gives a rose accord transparency and a cool metallic edge rather than depth, so it sits alongside rose alcohols and absolutes instead of replacing them.

Kannauj damascena absolute: deep jammy rose with beeswax, spice and a dried-fruit richness that the Bulgarian keeps in check. The rose behind the Indian attar tradition; heavy and tenacious, so it anchors a heart rather than lifting it.
Sour, sweaty-fruity odor with a fermented cheesy nuance and an underlying fruity aspect. Trace-use for ripe-fruit and body effects.
Clean, dewy muguet-cyclamen floralcy with a crisp juicy melon-rind facet and a subtle green edge of cut flower stems. A key post-Lilial muguet builder with strong diffusive power.
Sweet, rosy-honey floral note with a fruity-apricot facet; used in rose, honey and fruity-floral accords.

Earthy green-peppery herbaceousness with musky, celery-like and slightly animalic undertones; the musk facet grows in the dryout. Small doses give gin-like botanical depth to colognes and green chypres; phototoxic furocoumarins limit use.

Creamy orange-blossom base with white petals, honeyed floral sweetness and a lightly bitter-green edge. A proprietary reconstruction for orange-blossom soliflores and white-floral bouquets, not botanical absolute.

Perfumer's Apprentice, which lists it as Fir Balsam Reconstitution, gives the odour as pine, fruity, moss, smokey and calls it a wonderfully deep and rich synthetic replacement for fir balsam absolute: a dark green-black liquid, used up to a few percent, holding more than forty-eight hours on the blotter. Fraterworks describes an opening rush of fresh pine-needle greenness unfolding into a resinous heart with an unexpected jammy sweetness, raspberry preserves meeting forest sap, anchored by smoky, mossy undertones of the damp forest floor, and rates it moderate in strength and proportional in blends. In a formula it builds authentic coniferous accords, fixes the base, and adds woody-resinous depth to orientals and fougeres.

LMR describes it as a bright and exotic floral note with a spicy character, fruity nuances, a touch of wintergreen, and a solar and creamy background. The fraction is presented as an extra-grade profile, more solar, modern and petal-like than the complete oil, obtained by molecular distillation and fractionation at LMR's Grasse site. In a formula it gives the ylang function without the oil's heavy banana-medicinal weight: it reads as sunlit petal at the heart, lends creaminess to white florals and tuberose accords, and its spice edge keeps a solar floral from going flat.
Soft, warm, sweet-woody oil with a fresh coniferous-lemony top and a calm, resinous cypress-cedar body. A refined, meditative woody note in Japanese-style accords.

Warm coconut-cream lactone with a distinctive woody, slightly bitter caramelized-milk edge from the massoia bark. Gives an addictive creamy-woody coconut effect; strongly IFRA-restricted as a sensitizer.
Bright lemony-rosy freshness with a rustic grassy edge, instantly familiar. Beyond candles it lifts rose and citrus accords and feeds geraniol and citronellal to the blend.

Macrocyclic musk lactone originally identified in ambrette seed: radiant, sweet, slightly fruity-vegetal musk with exceptional exalting and fixative power. Lifts and expands entire compositions, a natural-feeling alternative to nitro musks.
Green fig-leaf and ylang nuance with a mild balsamic sweetness, smooth and natural. Key to fig-leaf reconstitutions and useful for adding leafy naturalness to white florals.
Soft, fresh minty-fruity note with a rosy-tea nuance, much gentler than menthol. Rounds mint accords and adds a fresh lift to lavender and tea compositions.

Distilled from Canada fleabane, and heavy on limonene, so it opens like citrus peel and then refuses to stay there: a weedy green dustiness underneath, a warm anise-spice sweetness through the middle, and an earthy woody close. A citrus top for somebody who wants the weed and not the fruit.

Mild at first, then a heavy, sweet balsam with soft rose, a gentle cinnamic spice and a dried-apricot sweetness. A tenacious fixative for oriental, rose and mimosa bases. An ester found in Peru balsam, storax and benzoin.
Creamy sandalwood note of the santalol type, smooth and lactonic. A sandalwood specialty for supporting natural sandalwood oils.
Sweet caramelised-sugar note over a green celery, fenugreek, balsamic and aromatic background. Adds savory-lovage green depth.
Woody-balsamic ester with a sandalwood-amyris character. Adds richness and a Mysore-style creaminess to woody accords.

A supplier listing of the Firmenich base describes it as a rich, indolic jasmine with animalic depth, and the house's own 2020 perfumery ingredients catalogue lists JASMOPHORE in the FLORAL block of its BASES section alongside its two plain JASMIN bases. The indolic reading is what distinguishes it from those: it supplies the heavy, faintly fecal warmth of real jasmine absolute rather than a clean jasmine reconstruction, so it is the choice when a white floral needs body and a living, skin-like depth underneath the petals.

A synthetic rendition of Mysore sandalwood oil built around its spicy and resinous side rather than its softest creamy one. Supplier listings give the odour as sandalwood, Mysore, woody, milky, and describe it as a relatively strong sandalwood note with spicy undertones that has also been read as resinous. In a formula it works as a sandalwood body rather than a top-dressing: it gives a woody base weight with a milky edge and enough spice-resin lift that it reads as oil rather than as a single santalol-type molecule, so it can carry a sandalwood accord on its own or thicken a thin natural sandalwood.

Sweet, fresh bergamot-lavender ester, fruity-floral and slightly pear-like, smooth and clean. The heart of bergamot and lavender character; used generously in colognes, fougeres and anywhere refined freshness is needed.
The refined, odor-active relative of Iso E Super, softer, more velvety and powdery-woody with greater elegance and diffusion. A premium woody-amber used to add smooth radiance.
Sweet honey and jasmine-floral note with a slightly green, winey-fruity nuance, fresher than phenylacetic acid. Adds diffusive honeyed sweetness to florals, tobacco and honey accords.
Sparkling grapefruit-citrus and spicy-peppery CO2 extract of timut pepper with passion-fruit nuances. Prized modern natural for citrus-spice top notes.

Indian Citrus limetta peel: a low-acid, soft sweet lime with almost none of the bitter terpenic bite of Mexican or Persian lime. Cheap and mild, useful where lime is wanted as a rounded sweetness rather than a sharp accent.
The clean, camphoraceous, cooling eucalyptus everyone knows. A fresh medicinal lift for aromatic and sport accords.

A clean, aldehydic-metallic freshness with pronounced ozonic and watery qualities, underpinned by delicate muguet-like florals. The supplier frames it as metallic ozone clarity with muguet beneath, an ozonic transparency that bridges marine notes and modern florals. In a formula it works as a booster: it opens out citrus tops and lends air and clarity to white florals, and because the odour sits on a heavy bicyclic aldehyde skeleton the effect persists far longer than most ozonic materials, holding on a blotter for days.
Warm powdery floral with a spicy clove-like body, a green olive impression and honey undertones. An increasingly rare absolute, essential for authentic oeillet accords.
Fresh, aromatic-spicy with pronounced eucalyptus-cineole coolness over a warm, sweet, slightly balsamic spice body. A luxurious lift for ambers, colognes and gourmand coffee or chai accords.

Firmenich's intensified muscone analog: powerfully diffusive, warm, slightly dry-woody animalic musk with more radiance than muscone itself. A small dose brings vibrating muskiness and lift to a whole base.

Firmenich polycyclic musk isomeric with Fixolide but roughly ten times stronger: powdery, earthy, slightly humid musk with unusual mineral depth and great tenacity. A specialty for dense, velvety musk drydowns.

Soft cooking-mushroom earthiness with delicate oily-vegetative nuances. Supplied as 10% Agaricus bisporus extract in MCT, not neat extract and not an instruction to dilute again. Supplier reports more than 124 hours on a smelling strip, not an exact lifetime.

Symrise gives the odour as fruity, floral, lactonic, green and peach: a creamy peach-apricot lactone rather than a sharp fruit note, with a green edge that keeps it from going jammy. In a formula it gives naturalness, imparts soft and caring fruity aspects, adds richness and body to white flower concepts, and underlines typical orange characteristics. A C11 lactone boiling at 292.7 C with a published odour threshold in air of 0.0316 ug/l, so it sits low and lends body rather than lift. Symrise recommends a use level of 1 to 5 percent.

The Good Scents Company describes fresh, floral, ozone, salted, basillic herbal notes with good diffusion; IFF read it as ozone marine and anisic with herbal tones, the descriptors falling away in the order anisic, ozone, salt, herbal-basil. Because it is the nitrile rather than the corresponding aldehyde it holds its character in alkaline and bleach-bearing bases where a Floralozone type would not, which makes it the marine-accord choice for functional work as well as fine fragrance. Measured substantivity is 304 hours neat and it is used up to about 10 percent.
Bright, sweet, juicy orange peel: the friendly everyday citrus. Cold-pressed sweet orange, generous and inexpensive in fresh and gourmand tops.

The supplier listing describes it as a selection of floral, rose water, very fresh, fruity pear-lychee fractions, obtained by fractionating Egyptian geranium essential oil. Against a whole geranium oil this reads far cleaner and rounder: the rose-water and pear-lychee facets are pulled forward while the herbal, minty and green-leaf weight of the whole oil is left behind. In a formula it works as a transparent rosy heart, useful where a rose needs juiciness and lift rather than the sharp rhodinol bite geranium normally brings, and it will modernise a classic rose accord without dragging a herbal shadow into it.

Mild fresh-balsamic ester with a sappy green edge and a clean woody drydown. Low enough in odor to serve as a semi-active diluent that quietly extends balsamic and amber bases without stamping its own character on them.

IFF describe it as an interesting combination of green melon and fresh air odours with a novel aldehydic effect: a watery green melon riding on an ozonic lift, with an aldehydic radiance that skips the soapy and fatty side of the classic aldehydes. It is the workhorse for melon-marine accords and for dewy green tops that need to survive, holding a fresh reading past forty-eight hours on the blotter, which is why it also works in soap and fabric bases. Recommended up to 4 percent in the fragrance concentrate.

Mild green-citrus aldehyde, fresh and grassy, with a herbal body and a soft honeysuckle floral nuance. The branched C-9: less sharp and less soapy than straight-chain nonanal, which makes it a rounding aldehyde for fresh green accords and a workhorse masking note in deodorants and detergents.

Overwhelmingly powerful roasted-beef and savoury broth character, the oxidised dimer of 2-methyl-3-furanthiol, turning coffee-like and faintly burnt at extreme dilution. Detectable at parts per billion and dosed only from a 0.01 percent solution, for meaty and gravy effects and as a trace shadow under coffee, roasted and leather accords.

Sweet myrrh: warm balsamic-resinous with distinctive lavender-like, celery-spicy and vine-fruit facets, smoother and sweeter than true myrrh. Key to balsamic-fougere warmth (famously in Shalimar-type ambers); IFRA-restricted.

PPG-20 methyl glucose ether: odorless humectant-fixative that measurably slows evaporation of an alcoholic perfume, extending wear time by hours. Typically added at 1-5% to the concentrate as a longevity booster.

Green, leafy and a little tart at first, turning to jammy dried fruit with davana-like richness and a mulled-wine warmth, then a leathery, balsamic, tobacco-tinged drydown with a mate-tea nuance. The fruit stays delicate; nothing like raspberry candy. Solvent absolute of Rubus idaeus leaves (France).

Diffusive musky-woody 'cashmere wood' note: spicy, slightly pine-resinous and red-fruity with a warm powdery drydown that bridges musk and woods. Technically a musk-adjacent indane ketone; now carries an IFRA standard, check current limits.

Fruity, floral and rosy over a warm amber undertone: crisp and juicy at first impression, then rich and slightly ambery underneath, without the sharp unsaturated bite of a true safranate. TGSC rates the odour medium in strength with substantivity greater than 24 hours at 100%. In a formula it is the lift under a rose or a fruity heart, adding fruity, fresh and rich nuances and keeping a crisp fruity or rosy note from going flat as the top burns off.

Robertet describes it as floral, very fresh and slightly peppered/spicy, and pitches it as a good alternative to a rose oil. The pepper is the tell: this is the bright, dewy, slightly biting side of the living rose rather than the jammy, honeyed weight of an absolute, so it reads as rose oil in the top and heart. In a formula it is the rose itself at a fraction of the cost of the natural, and its freshness lifts heavier floral or chypre structures instead of thickening them. Flash point 68 C. Applicable for a perfumery use only.
The everyday lime: sharp, fresh, zesty-green citrus with a candied cola facet. Distilled lime is the workhorse of colognes and fresh accords.

A Symrise Iconoclast captive the house sums up as Evergreen Captured in a Bottle: cool-air and piney with forest-floor elements. Launch coverage describes a refreshing forest, piney-woody profile with green, woodsy and cooling undertones, and the material is 100% bio-based, upcycled and 100% biodegradable. In a formula it delivers coniferous freshness without the turpentine bite of pine or fir needle absolute, so it can carry a cold-air outdoors effect through a fougere, a woody-aromatic or a modern masculine without turning sharp, and it pairs cleanly with vetiver, patchouli and dry ambers underneath.
Green, spicy-floral absolute with a violet-like, slightly earthy and herbaceous character. Rare classic note (reseda) for green-floral and chypre accords.

Sweet hay and freshly-mown grass with almond, tonka and tobacco-like warmth; dries down powdery and herbaceous. Defining note of the fougere family and vital in amber-tobacco accords; IFRA-restricted allergen present naturally in tonka, hay and liatrix.
The principal patchouli alcohol, giving a soft, dry, woody-earthy and slightly camphoraceous character without the darker mustiness. Used to reinforce or lighten patchouli accords.

Molecular-distilled patchouli redistilled away from iron: pale, clean and transparent, keeping the rooty-earthy core but losing the metallic mustiness of the dark grades. The grade most fine-fragrance patchouli work actually uses, where the dark oil would muddy a pale composition.
Sweet caramel and toffee character. Supplier suggests use in tropical-fruit accords, including lychee.

Bulgarian white rose otto, a separate species from damascena: drier, greener and more leafy-stemmy, with a clean honeyed rose heart and far less of the jammy spice. Reach for it where a rose needs freshness and lift rather than depth; it sits under citrus and green tops without fighting them.

Advanced Biotech specifies an amber to brown liquid with a honey odour, listing the synonym honey type flavour on the sheet itself. It is a reaction product rather than an extract of honey, and the physical numbers mark it as a heavy material: specific gravity 1.150 to 1.240, refractive index up to 1.475, flash point above 105 C, insoluble in water and soluble in most organic solvents. That density and low volatility are why it behaves as a base note and stays on the strip rather than flashing off with the top. In a formula it supplies the sweet waxy honey body that phenylacetic esters and mimosa alone cannot hold, and it is the bridge between a floral heart and an animalic base, since honey is where the two meet. Heavily coloured and strong, so it is dosed as a trace; twelve-month shelf life.

Uniquely boozy, fruity-apricot and dried-fruit character with winey, slightly herbal-camphoraceous facets that famously morph on each wearer's skin. A prized natural for boozy, fruity-liqueur and dried-fruit effects in ambers and gourmands.

Modern Givaudan macrocyclic musk: intensely diffusive, warm and sensual with red-fruity, slightly powdery nuances and outstanding radiance. Excellent for boosting the bloom of musk bases in fine fragrance.

Deep animalic-leathery absolute from beaver castor sacs: warm birch-tar leather, honeyed fruit, musk and a purring animal warmth that smooths into luxurious depth on dilution. Historic keystone of leather and animalic chypres; ethical sourcing concerns drive most modern use toward reconstructions.
Warmer, sweeter and more balsamic than Virginia cedar, with a resinous, slightly smoky-camphoraceous woody body. Used in masculine, chypre and amber woody accords.

Sweet spicy clove and cinnamon over a soft floral-carnation body with a distinct honeyed drydown, far quieter and heavier than isoeugenol itself. A classic long-lasting fixative for carnation, rose and amber spice accords where the spice must survive into the base.
Jasmine-floral note with fresh fruity, herbal and celery-myrrh facets; rounds off white-floral, fruity and marine accords with peach, banana and pear nuances.

Steam-distilled from Pistacia lentiscus foliage and twigs: dry pine-resin and terpenic green with a peppery, faintly minty-woody lift. Nothing like the sticky lentisque absolute, so use it where a Mediterranean scrubland top note has to stay airy over incense, fig and green-woody hearts.

Bedoukian describes a powerful watermelon note with a slight citrus nuance. Their captive BRI 359 is the cis C8 aldehyde, and it gives the cool, wet, green-rind side of melon rather than the sugary flesh, which is what makes it read as fresh fruit and not as candy. In a formula it is the melon top itself: a trace builds watermelon, cucumber and cantaloupe accords, sharpens an aquatic opening with something edible, and adds a green bite over florals. The house works it at a fraction of a percent in the concentrate, so it is a drop-count material; overdosed it turns fatty and green-metallic and takes the whole top with it.

Very mild, powdery strawberry with a hint of grape and a soft orange-blossom, heliotrope-like floral dust, drying down warm and faintly honeyed. Far gentler than methyl anthranilate, and it does not form coloured Schiff bases with aldehydes. Methyl 2-acetamidobenzoate, a crystalline fixative.
Dry amber, woody and diffusive with a green-metallic edge.
The high-cis grade of Hedione: noticeably more radiant, more jasmine-petal and airier than the standard. Where regular Hedione whispers, HC glows; used the same way at lower doses.

Nez describes Mane's lavender Jungle Essence as delicious, a lot more floral and more coumarinic than lavender oil, and specifically without the stalk note or the hay smell that appears with other extraction methods. The supercritical extraction runs cold, so what survives is the flower and its sweet tonka-like facet rather than the herbaceous, camphoraceous top the distilled oil leads with. That makes it a lavender for the heart rather than the opening: it sweetens and rounds a fougere or a lavender accord where the essential oil would cut and dry it out.

A floral accord centred on mimosa, characterised by sweet, powdery facets; almond nuances reinforce the heliotropic softness while vanilla provides a smooth, lactonic sweetness and a rounded, creamy drydown. dsm-firmenich positions it as a clean, CMR 1B-free, one-to-one and ready-to-go replacement for the recently classified heliotropin, built around the Josenol captive. Because it is balanced to match the molecule it replaces, it drops straight into an existing formula in the same place rather than forcing the accord to be rebuilt around it, and it serves floral creations, sweet accords and natural reconstitutions alike.

Sweet honey-tobacco-tea ketone with saffron, dried-fruit and slightly musty-woody facets; a natural component of tea, saffron and tobacco. Great supporting player in tobacco, honey, osmanthus and saffron-leather accords at low levels.
The Spanish rosemary: sharper and more camphoraceous, herbal and medicinal with woody-balsamic and minty facets; more pinene gives it a fresh, conifer-like lift, and the cineole sits behind.
Heavy fixed carrier oil with an oily texture and slow skin absorption. Added in small amounts (5-10%) to slow down a too-fast-absorbing blend. A diluent/carrier, not an odorant.

Strong cumin and caraway spice with a herbal body and a dry leathery tail, rounder and much less shrill than cuminaldehyde. Holds a sweaty-spice edge deep into the drydown of leather, amber and skin accords where the aldehyde has long evaporated.

Classic nitro musk: sweet, powdery, warm musk with a vintage cosmetic character, historically the great fixative-exalter of early 20th-century perfumery. Heavily restricted today; kept mainly for reference and restoration work, with macrocyclics like Ambrettolide as modern alternatives.

Intense, warm cardamom with a fresh eucalyptol lift and a clear ginger nuance at the top, settling into a sweeter woody-balsamic spice that lasts much longer than the oil. Absolute of green cardamom pods (Elettaria cardamomum) from Guatemala.

Sweet tropical terpene alcohol with ocimene-green, fennel-anisic and faintly gingery facets, drying to a fresh floral-woody lift. The linden-blossom and elderflower marker molecule, also a Muscat grape signature, and a key trace in ylang, osmanthus and white-tea accords. Fugitive: it gives a bright headspace-true opening but will not carry past the top.
Extremely sweet gourmand note of raspberry, cotton candy and blackberry jam with cassis and heliotrope associations. Adds fruity-powdery sweetness.
Complex golden honey with waxy nuances interwoven with jasmine and rose, and subtle cocoa undertones in the drydown. Bridges gourmand sweetness and floral elegance.

Symrise's own datasheet gives the odour as floral, rose, geranium, green, parsley and says it adds the metallic touch of rose oxide; The Good Scents Company reads the same material at 10% as rose, fresh, green, herbal, phenolic, bitter and parsley. It is the identical molecule Firmenich sell as Doremox, described there as a powerful rosy note more complex than rose oxide and more refined than diphenyl oxide. In a formula it buys a cool metallic-green sparkle over a rose or geranium accord and can stand in for part of a costly natural rose oxide, at traces to about half a percent. Holds 48 hours on the blotter at full strength.

Not a true aldehyde but a lactone traded under the historic name: lush creamy peach with apricot, coconut and waxy-fruity warmth. The famous 'peach aldehyde' of Mitsouko, essential in peach, osmanthus and fruity-chypre accords.

Myrtle-leaf orange peel: a bitter-green orange with a dry marmalade edge and none of sweet orange's sugar, opening onto a linalool-led orange-blossom warmth after a few minutes on the strip. The bitter citrus behind the Italian soda, used to give a cologne top a drier, more grown-up orange.

Historic tetralin musk with a sweet, powdery, faintly floral profile once common in soaps and colognes. PROHIBITED: found neurotoxic and banned from fragrance use decades ago; listed for reference and vintage formula study only.
Sweet, fruity-floral odor with a banana and mild roasted nuance. Used in fruity and light gourmand accords.

Bedoukian describes a fruity, ethereal, juicy note with natural black cherry nuances, and its own accord literature reads it as a melange of juicy pineapple, apple, blueberry and above all black cherry. The Good Scents Company carries the same CAS as cherry pentenoate, fruity and medium strength, reading at 10% in DPG as fruity green cherry with dusty melon rind, berry, oily weedy and tropical pineapple facets, with tenacity greater than one hour at 100%. In a formula it is the ethereal juicy lift at the top of a fruit accord: it makes cherry, berry and pineapple read as fresh-cut rather than jammy, and it leaves quickly, so it is a top effect and not body. Bedoukian specifies this grade as the high-cis cut of ethyl 2-methyl-3-pentenoate.

A Mane branded base described as fresh, bittersweet orange blossom and neroli character, with crisp green petitgrain at the top and a soft, creamy floral sweetness underneath. The opening is bittersweet orange blossom over dewy neroli, the green petitgrain gives leafy brightness, and the base settles into a creamy, almost marshmallow-like sweetness, so a single bottle carries a complete orange blossom heart. It is built on a high level of the Mane captive Bigarane, which is where the petitgrain freshness comes from. In a formula it brightens citrus colognes, smooths heavy white florals that have gone waxy or indolic, and adds creamy depth under fruity accords. Lasts more than 24 hours on a smelling strip.

Givaudan's diffusive watery-green muguet aldehyde: fresh cut-stem florality with dewy, slightly metallic sparkle and remarkable lift. Small doses brighten any floral; also excellent in aquatic accords to link ozonics with white flowers.
Sweet, balsamic, fruity-cherry with a strawberry and cinnamon nuance; crystalline and well-behaved. Rounds fruity-gourmand and amber compositions and appears naturally in strawberry and basil notes.

Described as the iconic powerful de Laire Iraldeine base tamed into its purest form: a tender, velvety soft leather with no animalic facets at all, a nude leather carrying noble floral powdery notes. Where the older de Laire leathers run smoky and quinoline-sharp, this one is the modern reading, soft and powdery. In a formula it gives suede texture and a powdery floral shadow underneath a composition without dragging in tar, birch or barnyard, so it can sit under florals and iris accords that a classical leather would overwhelm.
A synthetic sandalwood molecule useful in amber, fougere, chypre and muguet accords where it acts as a fixative and adds a soft woody body.
Sweet honey-chocolate note with rosy, slightly green-fruity facets leaning distinctly cocoa. Useful in honey, chocolate and tobacco accords to add sweet warmth without animalic heaviness.

Dark leather, castoreum and tobacco with mineral wet-stone facets and sweet tonka-vanilla warmth. Supplier classifies it as a base note and reports more than 400 hours on a smelling strip; this lower bound is not exact longevity or skin performance.

An Amazonian floral speciality built on Souroubea, of the family Marcgraviaceae, which blossoms as a gleaming yellow-orange spot in the crown of canopy trees.
