Supplier composition documents disagree, so IFRA and constituent exposure require review. The existing strength rating is retained, not reverified from these documents. The supplier's more-than-360-hour blotter claim is not an exact measurement or a skin-life estimate.
Intensely peppery, character-impact odor of black and white pepper; the defining molecule of pepper spiciness. Ultra-trace use for realistic peppery effects.
Creamy coconut-milk lactone with an airy, almost musky softness, far more diffusive than classic coconut lactones. Micro-doses milkify sandalwood, fig and suntan accords.

Sweet, gentle thyme carried almost entirely by linalool: aromatic and green with a soft floral roundness and only a trace of the thymol bite. The chemotype that can be dosed at real percentages where red thyme would scorch a fougere or a herbal cologne.

Symrise gives Floral, White Flower, Animalic; The Good Scents Company reads it as powerful, floral, indole-like, in the direction of jasmine and hyacinth. It is the indolic volume of white flowers without indole's heavy warmth: cooler, more hyacinth than jasmine, with a faint animalic shadow underneath. In a formula it is an impact booster that adds indole-like body to jasmine and orange flower and knits a floral heart onto an ambery base, and unlike indole it stays liquid and does not discolour. Symrise's use level is 0.01 to 1 percent.

Cilantro herb oil, dominated by (E)-2-decenal and decanal: pungent fatty-aldehydic green with a soapy-citrus lift, nothing like the linalool sweetness of the seed oil. A trace gives green and citrus accords a waxy, just-crushed-leaf realism; overdosed it turns to soap and raw stink bug.
IFRA-compliant treemoss: pine-bark moss with a tarry-resinous depth, atranol and chloroatranol removed. Sturdier and smokier than oakmoss for fougere bases.

Symrise gives the odour as woody, aromatic, vetiver, dried fruit and tobacco. It reads as a dry, rooty wood carrying a fruity-tobacco lift rather than a flat amber-wood block. In a formula it harmonises woody and floral elements, increases radiance and elegance, and imparts damascenone-like effects, so it can bridge a rose or a plum accord into the woody base without adding sweetness. The house recommends 0.1 to 3 percent.
Fine, elegant macrocyclic musk lactone with high impact and animalic, balsamic undertones. Smooth, tenacious and diffusive.
Bland, odorless fixed carrier oil with a slippery texture and slow skin absorption. Used to add slip to massage and carrier-oil blends (typically 5-10%); a diluent, not an odorant.

Warm, sweet-peppery and resinous with a woody-balsamic body and none of the terpenic sharpness of black pepper. The caryophyllene-heavy profile makes it the pepper of choice when black pepper cuts too hard, rounding spice into amber, tobacco and warm woody hearts.
Soft green, oily-waxy fruity note. Mild ester used for green-fatty smoothing in fruity accords.

Solvent-extracted Cananga odorata: deeper, sweeter and markedly more indolic than the distilled grades, with a creamy banana-custard body, clove-cresol spice and a heavy benzyl benzoate base. Carries the narcotic weight the Extra oil only hints at; use well under 1% in white-floral and amber hearts. IFRA-restricted.

Soft fruity ester with a winey-cognac warmth and a cinnamyl balsamic base, quieter and less spicy than cinnamyl acetate. Very tenacious for its weight, useful to extend fruity-balsamic bodies in ambers and to carry a boozy edge under heavy florals.

Soft, discreet, waxy-powdery macrocyclic musk (the saturated analog of ambrettolide) with a gentle, clean skin-like warmth. Useful as a quiet fixative filler in musk bases where louder materials would dominate.
Sweet, balsamic-nutty note with roasted cocoa, coffee and faint tobacco-caramel facets. A rounding agent for roasted and toasted gourmand effects in chocolate and coffee accords.
Fresh warm pine-woody note, mildly herbaceous with a cologne-like peppery facet; adds fresh conifer character to accords.
Sweet fruity-jasmine ester, jammier and more apricot-banana than benzyl acetate. Adds fruity roundness to jasmine, gardenia and tropical white-floral tops.
Complex, tenacious woody-earthy oil with smoky, rooty, green-grapefruit and slightly sweet-leathery facets. A cornerstone base note and fixative in masculine and chypre perfumery.

Ripe, juicy peach lactone, creamy-fruity with apricot skin and coconut facets, remarkably natural. The core of peach and apricot accords and a key player in osmanthus and fruity chypre reconstructions.

Givaudan list it among their unique ingredients as a fruity, grapefruit, juicy scent with a touch of cassis. It is one of the molecules produced through their Five Carbon Path programme, designed around renewability and biodegradability. In a formula it is a top-note juiciness material: it gives a grapefruit accord real fruit flesh rather than only peel, and the cassis edge adds the slightly green, blackcurrant-bud sharpness that keeps citrus tops from reading candied.

Fresh, rosy and fruity with a bergamot-like brightness and a sweet finish; The Good Scents Company lists it as a floral odour type of medium strength, described as fresh fruity rose bergamot sweet. This is the enantiopure (S) form sold as a Takasago Chiraroma grade, and the point of the chiral article is that it reads cleaner and closer to the natural than the racemate. In a formula it is the fresh, transparent face of rose: it lifts geranium and muguet accords, takes the waxy heaviness off citronellol, and bridges a citrus top into a floral heart without a seam. TGSC gives about eight hours on the blotter and it tolerates generous use, so it works as a floral diluent as much as a note.
Milky, creamy note with warm broth-like and nutty facets. Used in traces for milk, sandalwood-cream and skin-like effects.

Fresh, fruity-jasmine ester with pear, banana and nail-polish facets; the single largest constituent of jasmine absolute's top. The indispensable opener of every jasmine and white-floral accord, also key in gardenia and ylang bases.

The laevo isomer of Bacdanol isolated on its own: a smooth, creamy-milky sandalwood with a light cedary dryness and a soft rosy-floral lift. Softer and more cosmetic than Polysantol and far less loud, so it works as the naturalistic body of a sandalwood accord rather than its signature; blotter life runs past two weeks.
Woody-rooty vetiver ketone note, dry and slightly smoky. Boosts and extends vetiver oils.

A very powerful and tenacious balsamic, Tonka-like note with a unique tangy quality. It has a sweet yet tart character that suggests tobacco and coconut with a green nuance. In a formula it works as a long-lasting sweet-balsamic base that carries a coumarinic tonka signature without the hay-like flatness of coumarin itself, and it holds up across white floral, citrus and fruity compositions where it lends warmth and persistence from underneath.

Bitter-orange leaves and twigs co-distilled with the blossoms left on the tree at the close of neroli season: a fresh orange-blossom floral riding on the green, linalyl-acetate body of petitgrain, closing sweet-woody and tenacious. Sits between petitgrain bigarade and neroli, and is the affordable way to buy neroli's floral lift into a cologne or fougere top.

Firmenich's reconstitution of agarwood oil, described as woody and balsamic, and by suppliers as intensely woody, animalic and reminiscent of vetiver with sweet balsamic undertones. It is a thick sticky liquid that only pours when warm and is close to impossible to draw into a pipette, which is why it is commonly bought or made up as a 50 percent or 10 percent dilution. Very tenacious, and reported to outlast the Givaudan Black Agar equivalent. In a formula it is the whole oud accord in one bottle: a base-note spine for oriental and woody compositions where natural agarwood oil is out of reach on cost.

Floral, rosy, spicy, honeyed and balsamic. The profile specific to the FIRAD process is very fresh and watery, reminiscent of eau de rose with hints of litchi. It is a cold concentration of the water-soluble volatile fractions present in Bulgarian rose water, highly concentrated in odorant molecules, which is why it carries the dewy, phenylethanol-rich side of the flower that an otto, a concrete or an absolute leaves behind in the still water. Use it where a rose has to read fresh, transparent and alive rather than rich and jammy; it will not substitute for a rose oil, it supplies the half that oil is missing.
A waxy fatty acid (dodecanoic acid) with a soft iris and rose-petal-like nuance; used as a fixative/modifier.
Fresh magnolia-cream character balancing citrusy brightness and creamy richness with subtle green. Valuable in magnolia, rose and modern transparent florals.

The crystallised, higher-purity form of Amberever, the cedarwood fragrance ingredient dsm-firmenich launched in early 2025 and described as delivering exceptional performance against the market trend for powerful woody notes, with a rich ambery undertone and impressive longevity. Neo is obtained by crystallisation to isolate the isomer responsible for the odour and the strength, so it reads cleaner and hits harder at equal weight than the standard grade; it was launched in November 2025 and is produced at La Plaine in Switzerland. It is a base-note engine: it gives volume and drydown length under a floral, a fougere or a woody amber, and it must be weighed against the standard grade rather than swapped one for one.

Mane describes a soft and delicate petal-like rose profile carried by a fruity freshness with hints of liquorice, over a rich texture that gradually turns into subtle tea notes with comforting undertones of hay. It reads as a fresher, less jammy rose than damascena absolute, so in a formula it works as the rose itself rather than as a rose modifier: it gives a transparent petal heart that stays soft under aldehydes and does not fight citrus, and its tea-and-hay drydown ties a floral heart into dry woods, tobacco or hay accords without an added bridge. The variety is the Crimean 'Lani' rose, now grown in Moldova with local partner farms, and Mane states it is the only house still extracting it.
Green, sweet rose with a natural oily-leaf herbaceousness, like a dark red petal still attached to its stem. Used to make PEA and rose bases read fresher and more leafy instead of soapy.

Heavy balsamic ester, sweet and ambery with a faint ylang-rose ghost of the geraniol it carries. Almost silent on its own; used as a low-cost tenacity donor that drags rose and ylang accords into the drydown without adding character.

Fresh green-melon aldehyde with watery, slightly fatty cucumber facets; instantly reads as honeydew rind. Classic top-note freshener for aquatic, fig and fruity-floral accords; harsh neat, lovely in traces.

A sweet, candy-like basil: the green herbal note is softened by a cinnamon-balsamic warmth and strawberry- and cherry-like fruit from methyl cinnamate, with a linalool freshness and no camphor. Essential oil of the methyl cinnamate chemotype of Ocimum basilicum, Egypt.

Advanced Biotech's specification gives the odour as green, leafy, on a colourless to pale yellow liquid declared a natural flavouring in the EU. It is a preparation rather than a single substance, carried at 25 to 40 percent ethanol, with a flash point near 24 C, a low specific gravity of 0.815 to 0.850 and no water solubility. The effect is crushed-leaf green, the cut-stem freshness that opens a fougere or a green floral, and it is the ready-made version of what a perfumer would otherwise assemble from leaf alcohol and its esters. Being ethanol-carried it is comparatively soft per gram and it evaporates fast, so it belongs in the top accord and needs a fixed green in the heart if the effect is meant to last. Do not confuse it with Green Note Enhancer Natural, which is a different and more concentrated product.

True cured Vanilla planifolia extract: deep, rummy, balsamic-sweet vanilla with leathery, tobacco, dried-fruit and slightly animalic complexity far beyond vanillin. Luxurious signature material for amber, tobacco and gourmand bases; expensive and deeply fixative.
Sweet, jammy strawberry-and-cinnamon note; classic fruity workhorse for strawberry accords.

The Good Scents Company describes it as a natural herbal, woody and fruity note that recalls artemisia, pine, juniper berry and cedar, over a slightly fruity undertone, and rates its odour strength as medium. In a formula it acts as a herbal-woody bridge: one material carries both the artemisia and juniper facet of an aromatic top and the cedar facet of a dry woody base, so it links the two without adding a raw herb oil. It is a Firmenich captive ketone, colourless, boiling around 271 to 272 degrees C, which puts its persistence in the heart rather than the top.

Nearly odorless heavy salicylate with only a faint sweet floral-balsamic whisper. Used as a cheap fixative and carrier that quietly extends florals while doubling as a UV filter to protect fragile fine-fragrance oils from light.

Steam-distilled Cedrelopsis grevei bark oil from Madagascar with dry pale wood and pencil-shaving facets, damp earthy-mineral depth, a sharp green-camphoraceous opening and a softly powdery balsamic drydown. No valid whole-product CAS is assigned by the supplied evidence.

Fresh floral, sweet and citrus. The house publishes a blotter substantivity of twelve hours and recommends it between 0.1 and 5 percent, with about 0.5 percent typical. It is a fixed blend of tetrahydrolinalool (45-50 percent) and tetrahydromyrcenol (48-53 percent), minimum 97 percent combined, so it reads as a clean muguet-lily transparency carried on a citrus lift rather than as either constituent alone. Privi rates it as performing very well in alcoholic perfumery, talc and soap or shampoo, and well in hair conditioners and shower products, which is where a hydrogenated alcohol of this type earns its keep: it is stable in base and does not go rancid or discolour the way linalool can.
The character-impact molecule of hazelnut: sweet, nutty-roasted with green, fruity and nougat facets. Trace amounts create convincing hazelnut and praline notes in chocolate gourmands.
Tart, bright fruitiness between strawberry, green apple and plum with a subtle anisic undertone. Adds clean fruity sparkle to florals and builds convincing strawberry effects.

Faithful reconstruction of Tonkin deer musk built on macrocyclic musks; richly animalic with a slightly urinous warmth, ambergris depth and sweet caramel-vanilla facets. Fixes leather, chypre and amber accords at traces.

Another Western Australian myrtle, and the rounded one: eucalyptus clean at first with a dry pine-resin edge, then a floral-sweet lift from its linalool and terpineol that tea tree never has. Reads as a medicinal note somebody has already softened for you.
Green-fruity with pungent apple and banana-peel character. Useful sparkle in fruity-green topnotes, especially apple and pear reconstructions.

The commercial alpha and beta ionone blend, giving dry violet and orris over a cedar-woody body with a raspberry lift; beta-rich in most grades, so it sits closer to the dry isomer than the sweet one. The cheap workhorse ionone for violet, boronia and osmanthus accords, and for rounding florals into woods.
Fresh green violet-leaf note with waxy melon and fig-leaf facets, cleaner and safer than the alkyne carbonates it replaces. Modern choice for violet-leaf effects in fougeres and sport fragrances.

Old-school rose material with a sweet, honeyed rose-geranium body and a peculiar slightly medicinal-chloroform nuance. Historically used in soap roses; now heavily restricted and mostly of archival interest.

No isolated description is published for the captive; its profile is read through Spicyrup, the Mane speciality built on an overdose of it. Mane describes that arc as initially fresh and aromatic with notes of camphor and earth, giving way to warm woody aromas of liquorice and spices, then revealing powdery vanilla and caramel, long-lasting and warm with a sillage reminiscent of luscious carrot cake. Fraterworks describes the same base more bluntly as dank earth at the start with a rich gourmand drydown of carrot cake, caramel, liquorice and spices. What the molecule does in a formula is bridge a cold camphoraceous-earthy opening into a spiced gourmand base, so a vanilla or caramel accord gains depth and a savoury root edge instead of reading flat and sweet. Not sold neat; treat the character as attributed through the overdose base.
Waxy, fatty, orange-peel tinted alcohol; a softer alternative to aldehyde C-10. Smooths aldehydic and citrus compositions.

Nez describes Verdima as an IFF molecule evoking tomato leaf, rediscovered from the house archive where it had sat since 1949, and used by Domitille Michalon-Bertier to build a vegetal Speed Smelling 2022 composition backed by armoise heart and the sweet burn of Timur pepper CO2 extract. It is a leafy green of the tomato-leaf type, sharp and vegetal rather than floral or herbal-aromatic, sitting at the opening of a green structure. Its structure and CAS are unpublished, so an overlap with a green material already on the shelf cannot be ruled out.
Sweet creamy and buttery ester with a soft fruity lift. Useful for dairy, caramel, pastry and rounded fruit-gourmand effects.
Fruity-woody ionone with a distinct fresh pineapple topnote over violet and cedar undertones. Adds tropical juiciness to floral bouquets and links violet accords to fruity and woody themes.

Robertet gives tobacco, tea, herbaceous, with the status natural on carrier (MPG) and a note that it is appropriate for both flavour and perfumery use. It is the most transparent of the three mate clarextracts: dry leaf and black-tea bitterness without the stewed fruit of the fruity grade or the weight of the tobacco grade. Useful as a light green-tobacco veil over citrus, fig or tea accords where the darker mates would flatten the top.

Takasago calls it an exceptionally powerful amber woody note, complemented by a dry clean facet and a touch of animalic warmth reminiscent of androstenol. It is a Norlimbanol-family amber-woody alcohol of formidable substantivity, over four weeks on the blotter, supplied here as a non-racemic Chiraroma grade. In a formula a trace gives diffusive lift to the top while anchoring the heart, adding dry radiant woodiness and skin-warm depth without changing the true character of the accord it sits under. Takasago recommends working from a 1% or 10% solution and dosing under one percent.

Extraordinarily intense, pure lemon-sherbet citral note, cleaner and sweeter than lemongrass, with a light green-herbal edge. Used in traces to give explosive lemon freshness that outlasts lemon oil itself.
Wintergreen-medicinal salicylate with a herbal-sweet nuance; used in trace for minty-wintergreen and medicinal effects.

Drier, more sophisticated orange than the sweet oil, with bitter-peel, slightly woody and fresh-marmalade facets. Prized in colognes and amber compositions for a grown-up citrus opening. FCF grade: bergapten/furocoumarins removed for photo-safety; the scent profile is essentially the same, marginally less full in the deep facets.
True lemon balm: luminous citral-lemon over a green herbaceous heart, softer and more honeyed than lemongrass. Precious and dosed in traces for natural lemony sparkle.

Sweet woody-herbaceous Bulgarian oil built on germacrone, with a rosy geranium-leaf lift and a dry ambery, faintly tobacco-like base; it pours as a waxy semi-solid and needs warming. Prized as a natural fixative in chypres, fougeres, rose bases and precious-wood accords, where it holds the composition without adding volume of its own.

Metallic green pineapple with galbanum and grapefruit facets, extremely diffusive. Defines the 'sport fresh' genre; a few tenths of a percent radiates through fougeres, aquatics and shampoo-type accords.

Fresh citrus-terpene note with herbal and green facets, a dry woody body and a distinct black-pepper edge carrying a discrete minty nuance. Reinforces pepper, dill and elemi accords and lends a natural terpenic lift to citrus and conifer top notes.

Moellhausen calls it sound and charmingly intense, with toasted-sugary shades that read as warm and nostalgic rather than sharp or terpenic. It is a compounded fir balsam accord, so it brings the balsamic-coniferous body of the raw material already sweetened and rounded, working as a warm resinous foundation under woody and gourmand structures where a raw conifer extract would sit too green and too volatile.
Rare musky lactone found in black tea, tobacco and fenugreek, with delicate nuances of spice, peach and dates. Harmonises with tea accords, tobacco, coumarin and tonka materials.
A soft, delicate floral lily-cyclamen, hydroxycitronellal-like base; a low-to-non-discolouring, IFRA-51 and EU compliant replacement for HMPCC (Lyral / Kovanol).

Very powerful green, metallic rose and geranium note with lychee-like fruitiness. The laevo grade is distinct from racemic Rose Oxide and has a lower reported odour threshold. Use in small amounts to add fresh rosy diffusion; evaluate a dilution before dosing.

Soft, dry woody sesquiterpene with a green hoppy-herbal tone and only a whisper of the clove-pepper warmth its co-occurring partner beta-caryophyllene carries. Quiet naturalizer for hop, hemp, balsam fir and dry woody accords; too weak to lead, useful to make a reconstitution stop smelling synthetic.

Deep, fatty peach-butter lactone with musky, waxy and slightly floral facets, quieter but more tenacious than C-14. Extends peach-apricot themes into the drydown and enriches osmanthus and musk accords.

Intensely sweet, licorice-anisic with a warm, slightly herbal-fennel roundness, dominated by trans-anethole. The go-to natural for licorice and anise effects in gourmands, ambers and aromatic fougères.
Fresh, green, balsamic-coniferous oil with a sweet, resinous and slightly fruity pine-forest character. A bright top note for pine, fougere and forest accords.
Intensely fruity, ethereal rummy note with a sharp juicy grape-and-strawberry lift; powerful trace top note for fruity accords.

Sharp, airy sea-herb: sabinene-green and thyme-like over a salty iodine-marine lift, closing on a parsley-anisic dillapiole tail. The rare natural that gives a marine accord real herbal grip instead of a synthetic melon-ozone core.

An IFF sandalwood base the supplier describes as a deeply spiritual and devotional essence, built on an immensely rich sandalwood note over a creamy, lactonic backdrop. Its listed facets run apple, coconut, cumin, lactonic, leather, musky, rose, sandalwood and woody, so the wood arrives already dressed in milky lactones, with a rosy-fruity lift on top and a faint cuminic, leathery animalism underneath. In a formula it stands in for scarce Mysore sandalwood oil, giving body and creamy persistence to woody-oriental, oud and white-floral accords without the cost or supply risk of the natural.

Perfumer's Apprentice describes Robertet's accord as the "sweet and slight tart essence of a freshly cut Pineapple". The sweetness is the ripe flesh and the tartness is the acid edge that stops it reading as candy. It is a compounded all-natural base, so it drops a finished pineapple into a formula rather than asking you to build one out of single esters, and the tart facet is the part a lone ester will not give you. Use it as the fruit statement in a tropical or cocktail top and let citrus or a green note carry the lift underneath it.
Powerful ambergris-animalic with earthy tobacco undertones; dirty ambergris heart in traces.

Privi describes it as "Woody ambery with velvet like with cedar sensation", that is a cedar impression delivered soft rather than pencil-sharp, with an ambery warmth wrapped around it. It is a mixture of saturated alcohols, not a ketone, so it does not behave like the usual woody-amber workhorses even where the effect overlaps. Privi publishes a tenacity of about one week and a use level up to twenty percent, which is unusually generous and tells you this is a body and texture material: dose it heavily to give a woody accord smoothness and staying power without adding harshness. Good under cedar, vetiver and amber, and useful when a cedar note needs rounding rather than reinforcing.

Volatile, odorless hydrocarbon carrier that evaporates quickly without residue, used in body mists, dry oil sprays and anhydrous formats to deliver fragrance with a weightless dry-touch feel. Useful alcohol-free alternative for sensitive-skin products.

Intense citronella-lemon aldehyde with green, slightly rosy-metallic facets; the smell of lemon eucalyptus and insect-repellent candles. Used sparingly for citrus-green lift in rose and muguet, and as the synthetic precursor of hydroxycitronellal.

The classic Grasse/Egyptian jasmine: rich, warm, narcotic white floral with fruity banana-like esters, indolic animalic depth and a tea-like elegance. Irreplaceable rounding agent; even 1% naturalizes any floral heart.
Ethereal, sweet solventy top note with a fruity nuance. Very volatile; used sparingly for lift in fruity accords and as a fast-flashing diluent.

Sweet cherry-pit fruitiness with maraschino and bitter-almond tones, a phenolic, naphthyl-like warmth, hawthorn and a dry cumin-like spice that together read slightly brandied. Useful for cherry-stone and almond effects. Ethyl 3-oxo-3-phenylpropanoate.

Sweet cinnamon and cassia spice with a warm balsamic depth, rounder and less biting than cinnamaldehyde itself. A stable modifier for cinnamon accords that holds for days on a strip; used in amber, chypre and spice bases, and IFRA-restricted in its own right.
Fresh minty-herbaceous ester with sweet citrus and floral undertones. Modifier for mint, lavender and herbal fougere notes.

The woody member of the methyl ionones: a smooth, polished wood with an orris-floral heart, a waxy, ambergris-like dryness and a faint fruitiness. Far less violet-sweet than the alpha isomer; gives body and blends readily into woody notes. Isomethyl ionone beta.
The Moroccan and Tunisian rosemary: fresh, eucalyptus-like cineole with a minty, camphoraceous lift over a balsamic, woody-green heart. Cleaner and less camphor-heavy than the Spanish type.
